Both are constructed from `G_fit` measured perturbation responses alone, before any predictor is fitted, and both are frozen constants rather than tunable choices. The implementation lives in two files — `basis.py` holds the mathematics, `contract.py` holds the decisions — and is orchestrated as Phases 1–2 of `run.py`. This basis is the coordinate system in which every downstream artifact of the pipeline (ridge targets, predicted effects, cosine scores) is expressed.

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L1-L9), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L1), [PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md](PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md#L3-L11)

## Position in the Distillation Pipeline

The contract's hypothesis motivates why a basis is needed at all: STRING and MAP-KG descriptors live in a space with no relationship to the desired gene transition, so a ranker would otherwise have to learn *what a candidate does* and *how to compare it* simultaneously, from weak supervision. Distillation removes the second half — the pipeline first learns `static knowledge → signed gene-space effect` on `G_fit`, where measured responses are legally available, and a deployment candidate's predicted effect then lives in the same 8248-gene coordinate system as the query direction `d_q`, where comparison is a plain cosine that needs no learning. The basis is what defines that shared coordinate system.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L3-L12)

The legality boundary is strict and the basis construction respects it exactly: training may read `G_fit` static knowledge together with `G_fit` measured responses; inference reads only a candidate's static knowledge; a `G_select` candidate's measured response is used for grading and never as an input in any view; `G_check` is sealed. The basis, being derived from `G_fit` responses only, is therefore a legal training-time asset that is *reused* at inference but never *refit* there.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L14-L19), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L2-L6)

The following diagram shows how Phases 1 and 2 feed the rest of the pipeline, with exact tensor shapes at every boundary:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    T["G_fit transitions<br/>shape [2, N_fit, 8248]<br/>two batch-disjoint views"] --> C["Phase 1: consensus_response<br/>r̄ = 0.5·(view 0 + view 1)<br/>shape [N_sup, 8248]"]
    C --> B["Phase 2: randomized_basis<br/>rank 256, uncentered, seed 20260918<br/>B shape [8248, 256]"]
    B -->|"project: X·B"| Z["ridge targets z<br/>shape [N_sup, 256]"]
    S["static features<br/>STRING + MAP-KG blocks + presence flags"] --> R["Phase 3: multi-output ridge<br/>selected inside G_fit only"]
    Z --> R
    R --> P["predicted coefficients<br/>shape [N_sel, 256]"]
    B -->|"reconstruct: z·Bᵀ"| E["Phase 4: predicted effect<br/>shape [N_sel, 8248]"]
    P --> E
    E --> Q["Phase 5: PREDICTED_EFFECT_COSINE<br/>unit query · unit predicted effect"]
```

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L64-L102), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L121-L129)

Module-level interaction is deliberately narrow: `contract.py` feeds constants to `basis.py`, whose `ResponseBasis` object is consumed by both `predictor.py` (for target projection and reconstruction in cross-validation) and `run.py` (for orchestration and artifact output). Protocol tests in `test_protocol.py` pin the invariants of exactly these two files.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph mod["candidate_effect_distillation_v1"]
        CO["contract.py<br/>frozen constants"] --> BS["basis.py<br/>ResponseBasis, randomized_basis,<br/>consensus_response, diagnostics"]
        BS --> PR["predictor.py<br/>RidgePath, cross_validate"]
        BS --> RU["run.py<br/>Phases 1 to 6"]
        PR --> RU
    end
    TS["test_protocol.py<br/>tests 01, 02, 10"] --> BS
    RU --> ART["artifacts:<br/>response_basis.npy float32<br/>candidate_effect_distillation.json"]
```

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L7-L10), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L33-L35)

## The Response Target: Consensus of Batch-Disjoint Views

Phase 1 builds the supervision signal. `consensus_response` takes the transition tensor of shape `[2, candidates, genes]` — two batch-disjoint measurement views of the same identities — and returns `r̄_c`, the per-candidate mean `0.5·(view 0 + view 1)`. The function validates its input shape and rejects anything that is not a two-view stack, so a single-view tensor cannot silently pass as a target.

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L38-L43), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L46-L48)

The supervision population defaults to **every `G_fit` identity**. There is also a declared variant, `--eligible-targets`, that restricts supervision to measurement-eligible `G_fit` identities via `QUERY_ELIGIBILITY_V1`. The code comment is explicit that this variant is *motivated by a measurement rather than by a result*: the median `G_fit` response has a cross-view cosine of about 0.05, meaning for most identities the target is largely noise; eligibility flags which transitions are measurable. Crucially, the variant touches only the supervision population — evaluation, metric, and gate are unchanged. The schema record marks `supervision_is_a_declared_variant` so downstream readers can tell the two regimes apart.

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L64-L77), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L84-L93)

Because the target is a two-view average, the pipeline also *measures its own quality*. `view_reliability` computes the per-candidate cosine between the two views and reports median, mean, p05, p95, and the fraction of candidates with non-positive cosine. The record stores this both over the supervision population and over every `G_fit` identity, making the noise level of the target a first-class, reported quantity rather than an assumption.

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L46-L55), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L90-L91)

## Frozen Construction Constants

Every basis hyperparameter is a named constant frozen before any experiment ran — the module docstring states it plainly: *"Frozen before the first number."* Most consequential is that `BASIS_RANK = 256` is described as "one value, fixed in advance, no grid": rank is not selected by cross-validation or energy-threshold sweep, which removes an entire degrees-of-freedom channel through which leakage or overfitting could enter. Protocol test 10 asserts the declared values so any silent change fails loudly.

| Constant | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `BASIS_RANK` | 256 | Subspace dimension; fixed a priori, explicitly no grid search |
| `BASIS_CENTERED` | `False` | Uncentered SVD — the basis spans responses, not deviations from the mean |
| `BASIS_SEED` | 20260918 | Seeds the random sketch; construction is fully deterministic |
| `BASIS_OVERSAMPLE` | 32 | Extra sketch columns beyond rank for QR-based accuracy |
| `BASIS_POWER_ITERATIONS` | 4 | Refinement passes concentrating the sketch on the leading subspace |
| `RESPONSE_DIM` | 8248 | Gene-space width; `B` is 8248 × 256 |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L1), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L50-L55), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L154-L160)

## Randomized SVD Construction

`randomized_basis` implements the classic Halko-style randomized SVD: a Gaussian sketch orthonormalized by QR, refined by power iterations, followed by an exact SVD of the small projected matrix. The guard `rank >= min(rows, columns)` rejects invalid configurations up front. The returned `ResponseBasis` stores the **right factor's** leading 256 rows, transposed — so `B` has shape `[8248, 256]` with orthonormal columns spanning the row space of the consensus responses.

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L58-L75)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input X = consensus responses<br/>shape [N, 8248], float64"] --> B["Guard: rank must be smaller<br/>than both dimensions"]
    B --> C["Draw Omega: standard normal<br/>shape [8248, rank+32]<br/>seeded default_rng(20260918)"]
    C --> D["Sketch: Y = X·Omega"]
    D --> E["Orthonormalize: QR(Y) yields Q"]
    E --> F["Power iterations x4:<br/>QR(Xᵀ·Q) then QR(X·Q)"]
    F --> G["Small map: S = Qᵀ·X"]
    G --> H["Exact SVD: S = U Σ Vᵀ"]
    H --> I["B = Vᵀ[:256].T<br/>singular_values = Sigma[:256]"]
    I --> J["total_energy = sum of squares of X<br/>ResponseBasis frozen dataclass"]
```

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L60-L75)

> [!TIP]
> Because `B` is the transposed right singular factor, its columns are orthonormal: `project` returns *exact coordinates* in that basis, and `reconstruct(project(X))` is the rank-256 least-squares projection of `X` onto the row space. Test 02 verifies both properties mechanically — the Gram matrix `Bᵀ·B` equals the identity to 1e-8, and projection is idempotent (`reconstruct(project(·))` applied twice equals once).

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L40-L48)

Determinism is total: the sketch is drawn from `np.random.default_rng(20260918)`, and there is no adaptive rank or tolerance anywhere in the path. Two runs on the same consensus matrix produce bit-identical bases — a property the reproduction protocol depends on.

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L65-L66)

## The Uncentered Design: Spanning Responses, Not Deviations

The single most consequential design decision is `BASIS_CENTERED = False`. The module docstring explains it: `B` spans the response space itself rather than deviations from the mean response, which is what makes `r̂ = B·ẑ` a **complete reconstruction** rather than an offset from one. A centered PCA basis would require carrying the mean vector separately and would move the common perturbation response out of the basis entirely.

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L1-L5), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L51-L52)

The trade-off is honestly priced. The uncentered choice means the leading direction of `B` is the **common perturbation response** — the component every candidate shares — so a predictor that learns nothing candidate-specific will still produce a plausible-looking vector. The protocol's response is not to hide this but to instrument it (see the next section) and to couple it with the ridge design: `RIDGE_HAS_INTERCEPT = True` with the comment "the common response direction is a constant in z-space," and `RidgePath` de-means targets and adds the target mean back at prediction, absorbing that constant into an explicit intercept rather than pretending it away.

| Aspect | Uncentered (chosen) | Centered PCA (not chosen) |
|---|---|---|
| What `B` spans | The response space itself; `r̂ = B·ẑ` is a complete reconstruction | Deviations from the mean; reconstruction needs the mean vector stored separately |
| Leading direction | The common perturbation response | The first principal *deviation* |
| Failure mode | A candidate-blind predictor still yields plausible-looking effects | The shared-direction effect becomes invisible to diagnostics |
| Protocol mitigation | `common_direction_share` and cosine-to-mean diagnostics report it explicitly | Not applicable in this protocol |
| Predictor coupling | Intercept in z-space absorbs the constant (`RIDGE_HAS_INTERCEPT = True`) | Different intercept semantics |

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L3-L8), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L62), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L49-L55)

> [!TIP]
> The uncentered basis and the ridge intercept are one *coupled* decision, not two independent ones: keeping the mean-response direction inside `B` means a constant offset in z-space, which `RidgePath`'s target de-meaning handles. Do not "clean up" the basis by centring it without re-deriving intercept semantics and re-reading the diagnostics — the two constants were frozen together.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L51-L52), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L62), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L52-L55)

## Instrumenting What the Basis Conceals

`common_direction_share` exists, in the docstring's words, "to make that visible rather than flattering." It computes how much of the total response energy lies on the single direction shared by every candidate — the unit mean response — and reports `share_of_response_energy_on_the_mean_direction` plus the distribution of per-candidate cosines to that direction (median, p05, p95). If the mean response explains most of the energy, then any predictor, however weak, reconstructs something that looks like a response, and a cosine against it ranks candidates almost identically for every query. The recorded number is the context in which the design result must be read — a built-in confound disclosure, not a marketing metric.

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L78-L98), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L92)

The same honesty extends downstream of Phase 2. At Phase 5, diagnostics compute the median cosine between predicted and measured `G_select` effects, per-coordinate correlations against basis-projected truth (`basis.project(measured)`), and — directly exploiting the uncentered design — the median cosine of the predicted effect to the `G_fit` mean response, plus the query-independent share of the score. The CLI prints the two headline basis numbers first: explained energy fraction and mean-direction share.

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L188-L217), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L210-L212), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L277-L280)

Every construction decision is written into the run record for audit:

| Record field | Content | Verified at |
|---|---|---|
| `rank` / `centered` / `seed` | 256 / `False` / 20260918 | `run.py` Phase 2 record, mirroring `contract.py` |
| `selected_on` | `"G_fit only, no grid"` | Declares that no data-driven rank selection occurred |
| `explained_energy_fraction` | `basis.explained` — Σσᵢ² / total Frobenius energy | The subspace's coverage of `G_fit` responses |
| `singular_value_first` / `_last` | Spectrum endpoints | Shape of the decay across the kept 256 directions |
| `response_target.*` | Consensus definition, population, view reliability | Phase 1 audit of target noise |
| `common_response.*` | Mean-direction energy share | Phase 1 confound disclosure |

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L95-L102), [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L27-L29)

## The `ResponseBasis` Interface

The class is a frozen dataclass — immutable after construction — carrying exactly the three things downstream consumers need, plus two algebraic operations. The narrow surface is intentional: consumers can express responses in basis coordinates and reconstruct effects, but cannot mutate the basis.

| Member | Type / behavior |
|---|---|
| `basis` | `np.ndarray`, shape [8248, 256], float64, C-contiguous; orthonormal columns |
| `singular_values` | Top-256 singular values of the consensus matrix |
| `total_energy` | Sum of squares of all consensus entries (Frobenius norm squared) |
| `explained` | Property: `Σσ² / total_energy` |
| `project(X)` | `X @ B` → coefficients in z-space, [N, 256] |
| `reconstruct(Z)` | `Z @ Bᵀ` → gene-space effects, [N, 8248] |

Sources: [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L19-L35)

The pipeline uses all of it: Phase 2 projects consensus responses to produce ridge targets; Phase 3's cross-validation reconstructs held-out predictions to gene space for cosine evaluation against the measured consensus; Phase 4 reconstructs predicted `G_select` coefficients into full signed effects, with all-missing candidates set to exactly `0.0` — the declared neutral score, never a learned one; and the final basis is persisted as `response_basis.npy` in float32 alongside the JSON record.

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L96-L97), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L74-L77), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L121-L129), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L255-L263), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L30-L36)

## From Basis to Predictor

The basis is where construction ends and learning begins: the ridge predictor is, by its own module docstring, "a multi-output ridge onto the response basis" — the simplest linear map from STRING and MAP-KG descriptors to the 256 basis coefficients, deliberately minimal so that a negative result remains attributable. The penalty governing that map is selected by identity-level cross-validation inside `G_fit`, choosing held-out mean *gene-space cosine* over squared error, because the deployment use is a direction comparison. The mechanics of that selection belong to the next page.

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L1-L10), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L74-L77), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L63-L68)

**Suggested reading progression**: continue to [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor) for how static features map onto these coefficients, then [Knowledge Features: STRING and MAP-KG](13-knowledge-features-string-and-map-kg) for the input side of that map, and [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection) for how the reconstructed effect is blended into final rankings. For the evaluation semantics of the cosine scores this basis enables, see [Ranking Metrics: BU@B, MU@B, PHR@B](8-ranking-metrics-buatb-muatb-phratb).


# Ridge Effect Predictor



The ridge effect predictor is the learnable core of the Candidate Effect Distillation (CED) pipeline: a multi-output ridge regression that maps a candidate's static knowledge descriptors (STRING and MAP-KG) to a signed perturbation effect expressed in the 8248-gene coordinate system. It is deliberately the simplest model that could carry design signal — if a linear map works, that is the finding; if it does not, a larger model would only make the negative result harder to attribute. This page dissects the predictor's feature encoding, the single-SVD regularization path, the identity-level cross-validation that selects its one tunable hyperparameter, and the protocol guarantees that keep the whole construction honest.

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L1-L11), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L1-L12)

## Position in the Distillation Pipeline

Within `run.py`, the predictor occupies Phase 3 (fit and penalty selection, entirely inside `G_fit`) and Phase 4 (coefficient prediction and reconstruction for `G_select` deployment candidates). It consumes two upstream artifacts: the static feature matrix built from candidate knowledge, and the rank-256 response basis with its coefficient targets produced by [Response Basis Construction](11-response-basis-construction). Its output — the predicted effect `r̂_c` — is consumed downstream by the direct design probe, which scores candidates via `PREDICTED_EFFECT_COSINE = cos(d_q, r̂_c)`, and later by [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection). The legality boundary is strict and encoded in the contract: training may read `G_fit` static knowledge together with `G_fit` measured responses; inference reads only a candidate's static knowledge; a `G_select` candidate's own measured response is used for grading and never as an input; `G_check` is sealed.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph FIT["G_fit — training side"]
        direction TB
        SK["G_fit static knowledge (STRING + MAPKG)"] --> SF["StaticFeatures: zero-filled blocks + present flags"]
        MR["G_fit measured responses (two batch-disjoint views)"] --> CR["consensus response, 8248 genes"]
        CR --> RB["rank-256 response basis B"]
        RB --> TG["targets z = consensus · B"]
        SF --> CV["cross_validate: 5 identity folds x 8 penalties"]
        TG --> CV
        CV --> PEN["selected penalty: argmax held-out gene-space cosine"]
        PEN --> RP["final RidgePath fitted on all G_fit rows"]
    end
    subgraph SEL["G_select — deployment side"]
        SK2["static knowledge only — no measured response"] --> SF2["StaticFeatures"]
    end
    RP --> PC["predicted coefficients = predict(features, penalty)"]
    SF2 --> PC
    PC --> RE["predicted effect = coefficients · B-transpose"]
    RE --> AM["all-missing rows forced to exactly 0"]
    AM --> CS["PREDICTED_EFFECT_COSINE: cos(d_q, r-hat)"]
```

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L104-L129), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L14-L19), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L71-L76)

## Static Feature Encoding: What the Ridge Is Allowed to See

The predictor never sees raw knowledge records; it sees a `StaticFeatures` frozen dataclass built by `static_features()`. For each primary modality, the descriptor block is multiplied elementwise by its presence mask — so descriptors of an absent modality are **exactly zero**, not imputed — and a single 0/1 flag per modality is appended to the feature vector. The `present_any` column marks candidates with at least one modality present, and `fit_rows()` returns exactly those row indices, implementing the frozen training population `RIDGE_FIT_POPULATION = "G_fit candidates with at least one primary modality present"`. The primary track uses `PRIMARY_MODALITIES = ("STRING", "MAPKG")` only: literature-derived TEXT is excluded under `GENE_INFORMATION_POLICY_v1`, and anything carrying TEXT is reported only as a labelled legacy-contract comparator.

| Feature segment | Width | Content | Absent-modality behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| STRING descriptors | `d_STRING` | zero-filled capability block | rows exactly zero |
| MAPKG descriptors | `d_MAPKG` | zero-filled capability block | rows exactly zero |
| Present flags | 2 | one 0/1 indicator per modality | always written |

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L21-L43), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L41-L44), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L61)

## RidgePath: One SVD, Every Penalty for Free

`RidgePath` implements the entire regularization path from a single eigendecomposition, as its docstring states: "One SVD, every penalty for free." In the constructor, features are standardized (per-column mean, with scale floored at `1e-8`) and the target mean is subtracted; the standardized design matrix is then factored once via `np.linalg.svd`, and `U.T @ (targets − target_mean)` is precomputed. For a standardized design `X̃ = UΣVᵀ` and centered targets, the multi-output ridge solution at penalty λ is `W(λ) = V · diag(σ / (σ² + λ)) · UᵀỸ`. Only the diagonal shrinkage factor depends on λ, so `weights(penalty)` is a cheap post-hoc evaluation — the eight-decade penalty grid costs almost nothing beyond the one SVD. Prediction re-standardizes new features, applies `W(λ)`, and adds back the target mean, which realizes `RIDGE_HAS_INTERCEPT = True` (the contract notes the common response direction acts as a constant in coefficient space).

| Method | Signature | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `__init__` | `(features, targets)` | caches standardization statistics, the SVD factors, and the projected targets once |
| `weights` | `(penalty) → coefficient matrix` | applies ridge shrinkage; only the diagonal term depends on the penalty |
| `predict` | `(features, penalty) → predicted targets` | standardize → shrink → de-center, in one matrix product |

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L46-L63), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L62)

## Identity-Level Cross-Validation and Penalty Selection

The single tunable quantity — the ridge penalty — is chosen by `identity_folds` + `cross_validate`, both operating on `G_fit` only. `identity_folds` permutes candidates with the frozen seed `20260918` and splits them into 5 disjoint, sorted blocks; because each row *is* one candidate identity, the disjointness is exact, and no candidate ever appears on both sides of a fold. `cross_validate` then, per fold, fits a `RidgePath` on the complement and evaluates all eight penalties on the held-out block, recording two criteria per penalty: gene-space cosine (predictions reconstructed through the basis and compared directionally against the measured consensus response, via `_gene_space_cosine`) and squared error in coefficient space. The frozen grid is `RIDGE_PENALTIES = (1e-2, 1e-1, 1e0, 1e1, 1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5)`.

The selection rule is a deliberate protocol decision, stated in the contract comments: the penalty is chosen by **held-out mean cosine in gene space**, not by squared error, because the deployment use is a direction comparison (`cos(d_q, r̂_c)`) and squared error would spend the penalty budget on magnitude. Both criteria are `G_fit`-only; the squared-error choice is retained in the record as a declared sensitivity, not a decision input. The returned record carries the fold sizes, per-penalty held-out means for both criteria, `selected_penalty` (cosine argmax), `selected_penalty_by_squared_error` (squared-error argmin), the cosine at the selected penalty, and a distribution summary (median, mean, p05, p95, fraction non-positive) over per-candidate cosines.

| Constant | Frozen value | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `RIDGE_FOLDS` | `5` | number of identity-level cross-validation folds |
| `RIDGE_FOLD_SEED` | `20260918` | permutation seed for fold assignment |
| `RIDGE_PENALTIES` | `1e-2` … `1e5` (8 values) | decade grid searched from one SVD |
| `RIDGE_HAS_INTERCEPT` | `True` | target mean absorbed as intercept |
| `RIDGE_CRITERION` | `held_out_mean_cosine_in_gene_space` | primary selection rule |
| `RIDGE_SENSITIVITY_CRITERION` | `held_out_mean_squared_error_in_basis_space` | reported sensitivity only |

| Criterion | Evaluation space | Rule | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| held-out mean cosine | reconstructed 8248-gene effect vs measured consensus | argmax over penalties | **primary** — matches deployment scoring |
| held-out mean squared error | coefficient space vs projected basis targets | argmin over penalties | sensitivity check only |

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L66-L71), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L74-L110), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L57-L68)

## From Coefficients to a Signed Effect

Phase 4 of `run.py` turns the fitted path into deployment predictions in three steps. First, `path.predict(select_features.values, penalty)` produces basis coefficients for every `G_select` candidate from static knowledge alone. Second, `basis.reconstruct(predicted_coefficients)` maps coefficients back to the full 8248-gene space — an uncentered reconstruction `ẑ·Bᵀ`, which is a complete response rather than an offset from the mean. Third, the all-missing rule is applied: candidates with no primary modality present get `predicted_effect` forced to exactly zero, recorded with per-role counts and the rule string `"score fixed at 0.0, no learnable token"`. This is a corrective design choice: the contract explains that a shared learnable token for knowledge-free candidates is what previously put 92 information-free genes at the top of every goal-blind ordering, so neutral is defined as the cosine indifference point (zero) and fixed rather than tuned.

A consequence worth internalizing when reading results: because the basis spans responses (not deviations), its leading direction is the common perturbation response, so even a predictor that learns nothing candidate-specific produces a plausible-looking vector. That is why Phase 3's record and Phase 5's diagnostics surround the predictor with context — `common_direction_share`, goal-conditioning contrasts against `PREDICTED_EFFECT_MAGNITUDE`, and a non-deployable `MEASURED_EFFECT_COSINE` oracle row — so the design result can be read honestly rather than flatteringly.

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L121-L129), [basis.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/basis.py#L31-L35), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L30-L36), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L138-L149)

## Protocol Guarantees and the Test Suite

The predictor's behavioral guarantees are pinned by `test_protocol.py`, whose stated philosophy is that each test "names a failure that would otherwise look like a valid gain." The suite verifies that static features carry no response information and flag missingness exactly (the one structural guarantee the phase rests on); that identity folds partition the candidate set exactly; that out-of-fold predictions are measurably less optimistic than in-sample ones (asserting `optimistic > honest` on the fixture, and that all-missing rows stay exactly zero); that cross-validation never scores a fold with its own predictor; and that every frozen constant matches its declared value, so silent contract drift fails CI rather than surfacing in a paper number. The submitted implementation's penalty selection cut folds over row indices and let held-out responses shape the basis — the identity-level machinery here is the corrected form, as documented in [Post-Review Corrections](22-post-review-corrections).

| Test | Failure it names | Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `test_04_identity_folds_partition_exactly` | folds overlap or drop candidates | [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L64-L70) |
| `test_05_out_of_fold_predictions_are_not_in_sample` | in-sample optimism inflating apparent prediction quality | [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L73-L93) |
| `test_06_all_missing_candidates_get_the_declared_neutral_score` | a learnable token preferring information-free candidates | [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L96-L117) |
| `test_09_cross_validation_never_scores_a_fold_with_its_own_predictor` | a fold evaluated by a predictor that saw it | [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L139-L150) |
| `test_10_the_frozen_constants_are_the_declared_ones` | silent drift of modality, basis, fold, or scoring constants | [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L153-L160) |

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L1-L19), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L8-L10)

## Reusing the Predictor Out of Fold

The predictor's fold machinery is deliberately reusable, and the fusion stage exploits it. `out_of_fold_effect()` in `fuse.py` re-runs the identical `identity_folds` partition so that every `G_fit` candidate's predicted effect comes from a ridge that never saw that candidate's measured response — a necessity for honest β selection, since an in-sample effect would make the effect branch look far better on `G_fit` than it can be on a deployment candidate. The all-missing zero rule is reapplied identically (`effect[missing] = 0.0`), and `run.py` persists the selected penalty in `candidate_effect_distillation.json` precisely so the fusion stage can reload it rather than re-derive it. The mechanics of how this out-of-fold effect is weighted against the incumbent scorer are covered in [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection).

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L56-L68), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L118-L119)

## Minimal Working Example

The bundled synthetic demo exercises the predictor end-to-end in under a dozen lines, with no biological data: build `StaticFeatures` from two synthetic capability matrices (with the last two candidates missing all knowledge), fit a rank-8 basis on the training split, project responses to coefficient targets, fit `RidgePath`, predict held-out candidates at a fixed `penalty=1.0`, reconstruct effects, and zero-fill the all-missing rows. Scoring then takes the cosine of each predicted effect against a goal direction and fuses it with a base score via per-row standardization — exactly the structure the production pipeline uses at scale. The demo prints the ranked prefix and the all-missing raw scores (both exactly zero), serving as a software smoke test rather than a biological result.

```python
fitted_basis = basis.randomized_basis(responses[:train_count], rank=8)
targets = fitted_basis.project(responses[:train_count])
path = predictor.RidgePath(features.values[:train_count], targets)
effect = fitted_basis.reconstruct(path.predict(features.values[train_count:], penalty=1.0))
effect[~features.present_any[train_count:]] = 0.0
```

Sources: [ced_demo.py](examples/ced_demo.py#L31-L35), [ced_demo.py](examples/ced_demo.py#L37-L44), [README.md](README.md#L57-L59)

## Where to Go Next

Two natural continuations follow this page. To understand where the STRING and MAP-KG descriptor blocks actually come from — their construction, coverage, and provenance — continue to [Knowledge Features: STRING and MAP-KG](13-knowledge-features-string-and-map-kg). To see how the predicted effect becomes a deployed ranking signal alongside the incumbent base scorer, continue to [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection). For the upstream artifact the ridge regresses onto, revisit [Response Basis Construction](11-response-basis-construction), and for the leakage rules governing the `G_fit`/`G_select` split, see [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation).


# Knowledge Features: STRING and MAP-KG



This page documents the two static knowledge modalities — **STRING** and **MAP-KG** — that carry candidate-gene information into the Candidate Effect Distillation (CED) predictor. It covers where each modality comes from, how its feature archive is built and standardized, the provenance gates that guard it, how missing knowledge is handled, and how the features are assembled into the ridge predictor's input matrix. Predictor training mechanics are covered in [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor); how the resulting scores are combined with the base scorer is covered in [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L93-L104), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L5-L12)

## Position in the Candidate Effect Distillation Pipeline

CED addresses a specific deployment problem: for a candidate whose measured response is unavailable, the only legal inputs are static knowledge descriptors. The protocol's framing is explicit — STRING and MAP-KG live in a space with no built-in relationship to the desired source-to-target transition, so instead of asking a ranker to learn both *what a candidate does* and *how to compare it* under weak supervision, distillation learns a single map `static knowledge → signed gene-space effect` on `G_fit`, after which deployment-time comparison is a plain cosine in the shared 8248-gene coordinate system. The knowledge features are therefore the *only* carrier of candidate identity at inference time.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    K["Static knowledge<br/>STRING (512-d) + MAP-KG (1024-d)"] --> SF["static_features<br/>zero-filled blocks + presence flags"]
    SF --> R["RidgePath<br/>penalty chosen by identity-level CV on G_fit"]
    RB["Response basis B (rank 256)<br/>built from G_fit responses only"] --> R
    R --> PE["Predicted signed effect<br/>in 8248-gene space"]
    PE --> C["Cosine against goal direction d_q"]
    C --> F["Fusion with base scorer"]
```

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L5-L12), [README.md](README.md#L93-L104)

## The Two Knowledge Modalities

The primary track fixes exactly two modalities: `PRIMARY_MODALITIES = ("STRING", "MAPKG")`. A third modality, TEXT (literature-derived gene descriptions), exists in the frozen asset chain but is excluded from the primary model by the `GENE_INFORMATION_POLICY_v1` literature-leakage bar and is carried only as a labelled legacy-contract comparator. The comparison below summarizes each modality's provenance, geometry, and presence semantics as implemented in the build and loading code.

| Property | STRING | MAP-KG | TEXT (legacy comparator only) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Upstream source | STRING v12.0 protein interaction database | MAP frozen knowledge-graph gene representation ([MAGIC-AI4Med/MAP](https://github.com/MAGIC-AI4Med/MAP)) | NCBI gene descriptions + text encoder |
| Raw representation | 512-d interaction embedding (`Z` archive) | 1024-d output of the frozen MAP checkpoint's `gene_projector` applied to 5120-d ESM-2 gene embeddings | 384-d description embedding |
| Presence rule | `degree > 0` ∧ all-finite ∧ non-zero norm | gene present in the ESM embedding archive | non-empty mapped description |
| Standardization | mean/σ from G_fit-present rows only | mean/σ from KG_fit-present rows only | mean/σ from G_fit-present rows only |
| Status in primary track | Primary modality | Primary modality | Excluded (`PRIMARY_EXCLUDES_TEXT = True`) |

Sources: [DATA_SOURCES.md](DATA_SOURCES.md#L7-L14), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L41-L44), [build_features.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/build_features.py#L54-L67), [assets.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/assets.py#L116-L123)

## How the Feature Archive Is Built

Both modality archives are produced by `mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/build_features.py`, whose module contract is stated in its first line: extract static STRING and frozen official MAP-KG gene features, **never reading any perturbation response**. The STRING path is purely algebraic: it loads the 512-dimensional `Z` matrix, forms the presence mask from network degree, finiteness, and non-zero norm, and standardizes present rows. The MAP-KG path is a frozen forward pass: each gene's 5120-d ESM-2 embedding is pushed through the checkpoint's `gene_projector` — a `ResidualProjector` mapping 5120 → 1536 → 1024 with a sigmoid-gated residual branch — under `torch.inference_mode()`, with no fine-tuning and no downstream MAP training state loaded.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph STRING["STRING v12.0"]
        S1["Z: 512-d interaction embedding"] --> S2["present = degree>0 ∧ finite ∧ non-zero norm"]
    end
    subgraph MAPKG["MAP-KG (frozen official MAP checkpoint)"]
        M1["ESM-2 gene embeddings (5120-d)"] --> M2["gene_projector: ResidualProjector<br/>5120 → 1536 → 1024, gated residual"]
        M2 --> M3["present = gene exists in ESM archive"]
    end
    S2 --> STD["standardise_present<br/>μ, σ estimated on G_fit-present rows only;<br/>degenerate dims and missing rows zeroed"]
    M3 --> STD
    STD --> NPZ["features.npz + manifest<br/>sha256, coverage, governance record"]
    NPZ --> ASSETS["GlobalAttributionAssets<br/>re-checks provenance, maps to cache identities"]
```

The shared standardization primitive, `standardise_present`, is deliberately conservative: μ and σ are computed **only over G_fit-present rows** (in this module's split, `KG_fit`), dimensions whose σ falls below a configured floor are zeroed, and all absent rows are written as zeros. This means no evaluation-side candidate ever contributes to feature preprocessing statistics.

Sources: [build_features.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/build_features.py#L1-L16), [build_features.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/build_features.py#L54-L67), [common.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/common.py#L73-L82)

> [!TIP]
> The `standardise_present` rule is a leakage firewall, not just normalization hygiene: because μ/σ come solely from G_fit-present rows, G_select and G_check candidates influence neither the feature scale nor the dimensionality mask. This is the same identity-level separation discipline documented in [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation).

## Provenance Gates and Integrity Assertions

Both feature construction and asset loading are guarded by hard assertions that bind each knowledge archive to its claimed provenance. At build time, the runner refuses to proceed unless the upstream legality gate reads **PASS**, the MAP checkpoint matches a recorded size and MD5, and the ESM archive matches a recorded SHA-256. The extractor additionally strips only the `gene_projector.` prefix from checkpoint state and asserts that no response-prediction-specific keys (`perturb`, `scfm`, `condition_encoder`, `cell_projector`, `gene_decoder`, `project_out`) are present — preventing a downstream perturbation-trained model from being smuggled in under a MAP-KG label. The emitted manifest records `STATIC_FEATURES_COMPLETE_NO_RESPONSE_READ` status plus governance flags asserting that no perturbation response, no relevance data, no downstream MAP checkpoint, and no MAP-KG fine-tuning were involved.

| Check | Location | Failure mode |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Legality gate text `Gate status: **PASS**` | Build entry | Refuses to build features |
| MAP checkpoint size + MD5; ESM SHA-256 | Build entry | Refuses to build features |
| No downstream perturbation keys in checkpoint | State extraction | Assertion error |
| Manifest status `STATIC_FEATURES_COMPLETE_NO_RESPONSE_READ`, governance flags false | Asset loading | `RuntimeError` on load |
| Manifest-bound archive hash; universe/shape validation | Asset loading | `RuntimeError` on load |

The loader re-verifies everything independently: `GlobalAttributionAssets._load_multi` rejects any MAP-KG archive whose manifest fails the response-independent provenance contract, validates the TEXT freeze against its own manifest hash, then maps each archive from its native gene universe onto the frozen cache identities, dropping any row that is absent, non-finite, or zero-norm.

Sources: [build_features.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/build_features.py#L44-L53), [build_features.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/build_features.py#L28-L42), [build_features.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/build_features.py#L70-L75), [assets.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/assets.py#L105-L123)

## Contract Rules: Primary versus Legacy Modalities and Role Limits

The modality whitelist is enforced structurally, not by convention: `GlobalAttributionAssets.__init__` accepts only the frozen `("STRING",)` factorial path or the full `("STRING", "MAPKG", "TEXT")` path, and the CED runner instantiates the latter while consuming only `PRIMARY_MODALITIES` downstream. The TEXT exclusion is resolved by *non-dependence* rather than argument — anything carrying TEXT is reported as a labelled legacy-contract comparator, per `TEXT_EXCLUSION_REASON`. Role access is equally narrow: `role_arrays` raises for any role other than `G_fit` or `G_select`, so `G_check` is structurally inaccessible to the feature pathway.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["GlobalAttributionAssets<br/>(whitelist: STRING ∣ STRING+MAPKG+TEXT)"] -->|"role_arrays('G_fit') / role_arrays('G_select')"| B["AttributionRoleArrays<br/>capabilities + capability_present"]
    B -->|dict of per-modality arrays| C["static_features()"]
    C --> D["StaticFeatures<br/>values, present_any, names"]
    D --> E["RidgePath / cross_validate<br/>(G_fit only)"]
    E --> F["PREDICTED_EFFECT_COSINE<br/>on G_select"]
    X["G_check"] -.->|"access forbidden"| A
```

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L23-L28), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L41-L44), [assets.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/assets.py#L36-L39), [assets.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/assets.py#L129-L131), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L59-L60)

## Feature Assembly into the Predictor Input

`static_features(role, modalities)` is the single choke point where knowledge archives become a predictor-ready matrix. For each modality it takes the standardized capability block, zeroes rows where the modality is absent (`values * present[:, None]`), and appends one binary present-flag column per modality, yielding a `StaticFeatures` record with `values`, an `any`-modality `present_any` mask, and modality names. With the primary pair, the deployed feature dimension is 512 (STRING) + 1024 (MAP-KG) + 2 (flags) = **1538**; the runner records this as `feature_dimension` in its output manifest. The fit population is likewise knowledge-defined: `RIDGE_FIT_POPULATION` is "G_fit candidates with at least one primary modality present", selected via `StaticFeatures.fit_rows()`.

| Input component | Shape per candidate | Absent-row behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| STRING block | 512 | zeroed; flag column = 0 |
| MAP-KG block | 1024 | zeroed; flag column = 0 |
| Presence flags | 2 | encodes exactly which modalities exist |

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L21-L43), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L104-L119), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L61-L62)

> [!TIP]
> The presence-flag columns make missingness itself a learnable feature: the ridge can condition its use of the knowledge blocks on which modalities exist, rather than treating zero-fill as ordinary signal. The paired `present_any` mask then serves a separate, non-learned role in the all-missing rule below.

## Handling Candidates with Missing Knowledge

A candidate carrying **no** static modality has no predicted effect at all. The contract fixes this case to an exactly neutral score of `ALL_MISSING_SCORE = 0.0` — a cosine's own indifference point, fixed in advance and never tuned — explicitly rejecting the alternative of a shared learnable token, which in a previous phase put 92 information-free genes at the top of every goal-blind ordering. The implementation enforces this at two points: Phase 4 zeroes the reconstructed effect vector for all-missing rows, and Phase 5 forcibly overwrites their score column to 0.0 so they can never win a ranking slot through geometry. The counts and fractions of such candidates in both roles are recorded in the run output under `all_missing`.

| Scenario | Predicted effect | Score behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ≥1 primary modality present | Ridge output reconstructed through basis | Standard cosine against goal direction |
| All modalities missing | Zeroed | Fixed at 0.0, excluded from learned ranking |

The bundled synthetic demo exercises this exact path with toy capability matrices (12-d STRING, 10-d MAPKG — deliberately not the deployed dimensions, since it is a software smoke test): it zeroes the two all-missing candidates' effects and prints their resulting raw scores, confirming the neutral-score behavior end to end.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L32-L36), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L71-L76), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L121-L129), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L145-L149), [ced_demo.py](examples/ced_demo.py#L23-L36)

## Why Static Knowledge Enters Only Through Distillation

The design's central bet is architectural: a linear map from knowledge space to basis coefficients, chosen entirely inside `G_fit`, is the *simplest* transfer mechanism that can carry design signal — and its simplicity is diagnostic. If a linear map from STRING and MAP-KG carries ranking signal, that is the finding; if it does not, a larger model would only make the negative result harder to attribute. Every tunable choice is made by identity-level cross-validation on `G_fit` (a candidate never appears on both sides of a fold), and the deployment comparison itself requires no learning: the predicted effect lands in the same 8248-gene coordinate system as the query direction, so scoring is a cosine.

| Design choice | Rationale | Trade-off accepted |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Multi-output ridge (linear map) | Negative results remain attributable; signal, if present, is provable | Forfeits nonlinear knowledge interactions |
| Zero-fill + presence flags | Missingness is explicit, uniform-shape matrix | Absent rows contribute exact zeros |
| Fixed neutral score for all-missing | No learnable token to be exploited by goal-blind orderings | Such candidates cannot be ranked above others by the effect branch |
| Penalty by held-out gene-space cosine | Deployment use is direction comparison, not magnitude | Squared-error choice reported only as sensitivity |

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L1-L11), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L5-L12), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L63-L68)

## Reading Progression

To see how the response basis these features are mapped onto is constructed, continue with [Response Basis Construction](11-response-basis-construction); for the ridge fitting, cross-validation, and penalty selection that consume `StaticFeatures`, see [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor); for how `PREDICTED_EFFECT_COSINE` is combined with the base scorer, see [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection). The governance and hashing discipline around these knowledge archives connects directly to [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests), and the deployment regime where measured candidate responses are masked — making these static features the only legal carrier of candidate information — is analyzed in [Response Masking and Open-Vocabulary Analyses](18-response-masking-and-open-vocabulary-analyses).


# Score Fusion and Beta Selection



This page documents Phases 8–9 of the Candidate Effect Distillation pipeline: how the learned ridge-based effect branch is fused with the frozen incumbent scorer, and how the single fusion weight β is selected. The implementation lives entirely in `fuse.py`, which produces one artifact — `fusion.json` — recording the β selection curve, honesty diagnostics, and paired evaluation rows. The module's design constraint is stated in its first line: *"the smallest form that respects the firewall"* — exactly one quantity is fitted (the scalar β), and it is fitted on `G_fit` alone.

This page builds directly on the preceding pipeline stages: the response basis from [Response Basis Construction](11-response-basis-construction), the ridge map from [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor), and the static descriptors from [Knowledge Features: STRING and MAP-KG](13-knowledge-features-string-and-map-kg).

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L1-L20), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/run.py#L1-L8)

## The Fusion Rule

The integrated score composes two branches per query–candidate pair, per view:

```
s(q,c) = z[ s_incumbent(q,c) ] + β · z[ cos(d_q, r̂_c) ]
```

where `z` is a **per-query standardization** across candidates: each score row is centered and scaled to mean 0, variance 1 within one query (with a `1e-12` epsilon floor, so a query with constant scores does not divide by zero). This is implemented in `_row_z`. Standardizing per query — rather than globally — is what makes β dimensionless and comparable across queries whose incumbent score spreads differ by orders of magnitude. The effect branch computes the cosine between the query's own transition direction `d_q` and the candidate's predicted effect `r̂_c` (both L2-normalized via `_unit`, which floors norms at `1e-30`).

The standardized combination is **rank-preserving within each branch**: `z` is a monotone per-row transform, so `argsort` of the fused matrix equals `argsort` of the sum of rank-preserving components (enforced by test_08). This also guarantees the `β = 0` edge case exactly restores the incumbent ordering, since `β · z(cosine)` collapses to an exact zero matrix (enforced by test_07).

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L4-L19), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L46-L53), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L124-L136)

### Concept relationships

To read the diagram: the incumbent branch is the frozen neural scorer from the base model; the effect branch is the distilled linear ridge from the earlier phases. Each branch is standardized independently per query, then combined by a weighted sum where β scales only the effect branch.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Incumbent["Incumbent branch (frozen)"]
        MSET["M_SET checkpoint<br/>(GlobalObjectiveKnowledgeAttributionModel)"] --> SI["s_incumbent(q,c)<br/>per view"]
    end
    subgraph Effect["Effect branch (distilled)"]
        SK["Static knowledge<br/>STRING + MAPKG"] --> RIDGE["Ridge predictor<br/>(penalty frozen in Phase 5)"]
        RIDGE --> EFF["r̂_c predicted effect<br/>8248-gene space"]
    end
    T["d_q : query transition direction"] --> COS["cos(d_q, r̂_c)"]
    EFF --> COS
    SI --> Z1["z(·) per-query"]
    COS --> Z2["z(·) per-query"]
    Z1 --> SUM((+))
    Z2 -->|"× β"| SUM
    SUM --> S["s(q,c) fused"]
```

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L71-L80), [query_conditional_capacity_v1/run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/query_conditional_capacity_v1/run.py#L36-L55)

### Module interaction map

`fuse.py` is deliberately thin: it orchestrates frozen components rather than defining new models. It pulls the consensus response and randomized basis from `basis.py`, the ridge machinery (`RidgePath`, `identity_folds`, `static_features`) from `predictor.py`, every tunable constant from `contract.py`, the incumbent scorer entry point `_starting_scores` and the J-guardrail from the frozen model assets, the ranking metric `_direction_metrics` from the sampler evaluator, and bootstrap statistics from `utility_gt_v2`.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CED["candidate_effect_distillation_v1"]
        FUSE["fuse.py<br/>(orchestrator)"]
        BASIS["basis.py<br/>consensus_response, randomized_basis"]
        PRED["predictor.py<br/>RidgePath, identity_folds, static_features"]
        CONTRACT["contract.py<br/>ALL_MISSING_SCORE, BASIS_RANK, ..."]
    end
    subgraph FROZEN["Frozen model assets"]
        QCC["query_conditional_capacity_v1<br/>_starting_scores, _guardrail"]
        DAS["decision_aligned_sampler_v1<br/>_direction_metrics"]
        FTA["open_vocab_dual_encoder_v1<br/>FrozenTransitionAssets.cross_view_utility"]
        GOA["global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1<br/>GlobalAttributionAssets"]
    end
    U["utility_gt_v2<br/>cluster_bootstrap, summarize"]
    FUSE --> BASIS
    FUSE --> PRED
    FUSE --> CONTRACT
    FUSE --> QCC
    FUSE --> DAS
    FUSE --> FTA
    FUSE --> GOA
    FUSE --> U
```

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L32-L43), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L1-L12)

## The Out-of-Fold Firewall

The central honesty problem: β is selected by measuring how much the effect branch improves ranking on `G_fit` — but the ridge was *trained* on `G_fit` measured responses. If β were fitted against in-sample effect predictions, the effect branch would look far better on `G_fit` than it can be on any deployment candidate, and *"β would be chosen for a model that does not exist."* The fix is `out_of_fold_effect`: for every `G_fit` candidate, the effect prediction is produced by a ridge that never saw that candidate's measured response.

The mechanism reuses the identity-level fold machinery from `predictor.py`: the eligible `G_fit` rows are partitioned into 5 disjoint identity blocks (`identity_folds`, seed `20260918` — a candidate is one identity, so leakage across folds is structurally impossible). For each held fold, a fresh `RidgePath` is fit on the remaining folds and predicts coefficients for the held candidates; coefficients are then reconstructed into gene space via the shared basis. Candidates outside the eligible set (all modalities missing) get an exactly-zero effect vector.

The cost of skipping this firewall is not left to argument — it is measured. The run computes both an out-of-fold and an in-sample median cosine-to-measured on `G_fit` and records them as `prediction_honesty`; the in-sample value exists *"only to show how much an in-sample beta would have been misled."* Test_05 asserts on a synthetic fixture that the in-sample cosine strictly exceeds the honest one, proving the fixture is capable of detecting the optimism it guards against.

> [!TIP]
> Every `G_fit` effect prediction used anywhere in β selection comes from a ridge trained on the other four folds — the same `identity_folds` primitive that selects the ridge penalty. This means β is calibrated against exactly the predictor quality that deployment can deliver, not the inflated quality of a predictor grading its own training data.

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L11-L16), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L56-L68), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L103-L112), [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L70-L75), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L85-L101)

## Beta Selection Protocol

β is selected by grid search over the frozen constant `BETA_GRID = (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0)` — eight values, spanning "effect branch off" (`0.0`) through parity (`1.0`) to effect-branch dominance (`3.0`). For each grid value, the fused scores are computed on `G_fit` using the out-of-fold effects, evaluated with `_direction_metrics` on both views over the **eligible** `G_fit` queries (rows from `G_fit_eligible.npy`), and the per-query MBRU values from both views are concatenated; the selection criterion is the **median** MBRU. The chosen β is the grid maximizer of that median. The full curve is preserved in the artifact as `beta_selection_curve_G_fit_MBRU`, alongside the declaration `"beta_selected_on": "G_fit eligible queries only"`.

The criterion metric — MBRU (from `mbru_from_nru(normalized_ranked_utility(...))`) plus `Mean@B` and `HighValueCount@B` at a 95th-percentile high-value threshold — is the same training-side direction-utility surrogate the base scorer was optimized against, computed with `stable_order` excluding the self-pair. Full metric definitions are covered in [Ranking Metrics: BU@B, MU@B, PHR@B](8-ranking-metrics-buatb-muatb-phratb).

The second firewall: **`G_select` is never consulted while choosing β**. Only after `chosen = max(BETA_GRID, key=...)` is fixed are the select-role assets loaded — incumbent scores, transitions, features, and the select-side effect predicted by the fully-fit ridge (the same `RidgePath` fit on all eligible `G_fit` rows, using the penalty inherited from the earlier distillation artifact's `cross_validation.selected_penalty`). After selection, the fit-side incumbent scores and utilities are explicitly `del`eted before the select side is built, so the two phases cannot share state.

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L43), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L114-L124), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L126-L133), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L93-L94), [decision_aligned_sampler_v1/evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/decision_aligned_sampler_v1/evaluate.py#L54-L69)

### Selection and evaluation flow

Reading the diagram: everything above the "β fixed" barrier touches only `G_fit` (with out-of-fold effects); everything below reads `G_select` exactly once, with β already frozen.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Load ridge penalty from<br/>candidate_effect_distillation.json"] --> B["G_fit: consensus → basis →<br/>targets → static features"]
    B --> C["out_of_fold_effect<br/>5 identity folds"]
    C --> D["G_fit incumbent scores<br/>+ cross-view utility (eligible rows)"]
    D --> E{"β ∈ BETA_GRID<br/>(8 values)"}
    E --> F["fusion_scores on G_fit"]
    F --> G["MBRU, both views,<br/>eligible fit queries"]
    G --> H["median per β →<br/>selection curve"]
    H --> I["chosen β = argmax (β FIXED)"]
    I --> J["G_select read once:<br/>incumbent + select-side effect"]
    J --> K["3 rows: INCUMBENT /<br/>FUSED_BETA_1 / FUSED_BETA_SELECTED<br/>paired stats + guardrail"]
    K --> L["fusion.json"]
```

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L83-L133), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L146-L155)

## Reporting Rows: Three Numbers, Not One

The select-side evaluation emits exactly three rows, each isolating a different claim. Every row is evaluated with the same `_direction_metrics` on both views and the same `_guardrail` on the four-way eligible subset — the physical-units endpoint-improvement check `J(a) = 2a⟨r,d⟩ − a²‖r‖²`, cross-fitted so the measurement that chooses attenuation never grades it (see [Held-Out Context Evaluation Protocol](9-held-out-context-evaluation-protocol)). Each fused row also carries a **paired-against-incumbent** block: per-query MBRU differences against the incumbent row, summarized with a cluster bootstrap (95% CI at the median) and the fraction of queries improved.

| Row | β | What it isolates |
|---|---|---|
| `INCUMBENT` | `null` | The frozen base scorer alone; the reference every other row is paired against |
| `FUSED_BETA_1` | `1.0` | Fusion at unit weight — needs **no fitting at all**; a result surviving only at a fitted weight is explicitly reported as weaker |
| `FUSED_BETA_SELECTED` | argmax of G_fit curve | The fitted-fusion result, with its paired bootstrap CI |

| Selection-curve fields | Content |
|---|---|
| `beta_grid` | The frozen 8-value grid |
| `beta_selected_on` | `"G_fit eligible queries only"` |
| `beta_selection_curve_G_fit_MBRU` | Median MBRU per β, both views concatenated |
| `prediction_honesty` | Out-of-fold vs in-sample median cosine to measured consensus |
| `read_G_check` | Always `false` — the sealed context is never opened |

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L18-L19), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L157-L176), [decision_aligned_sampler_v1/evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/decision_aligned_sampler_v1/evaluate.py#L1-L22)

## All-Missing Candidates and the Neutral-Score Policy

Candidates whose static knowledge is entirely absent have no predicted effect. The contract fixes their raw effect-branch score at `ALL_MISSING_SCORE = 0.0` — *"a cosine's own indifference point, fixed here and not tuned"* — with **no learnable token**, because the previous phase showed a shared learnable token is what pushed 92 information-free genes to the top of every goal-blind ordering. In `fusion_scores`, the zero-norm effect rows are detected (`norm ≤ 0`) and their cosine columns overwritten with `0.0` **before** per-query standardization.

This placement has a subtle consequence that the protocol tests make explicit: after `z`, the neutral candidates' fused scores are equal *to each other within a query row*, but their absolute fused value depends on that query's own score spread. Test_06 therefore asserts the correct invariant — row-equality (`block − block[:, :1] ≈ 0`) and finiteness, not cross-row equality — so the policy can never prefer one information-free candidate over another, while the same candidates may sit at different fused values under different queries. The all-missing candidates themselves are zeroed out of the effect vector in both the out-of-fold (`effect[missing] = 0.0`) and select-side (`select_effect[~present_any] = 0.0`) paths.

> [!TIP]
> The neutral score `0.0` is applied to the *raw cosine block* before `_row_z`, not to the fused output. Post-standardization, "neutral" means "indistinguishable from every other neutral candidate within the query," not "value zero." Reproducing or extending the fusion code must preserve this ordering of operations or the all-missing policy silently changes meaning.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L26-L30), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L63-L74), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L71-L80), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L104-L121)

## Protocol Invariants Enforced by Tests

The test module's stated purpose: *"Each names a failure that would otherwise look like a valid gain."* The fusion-relevant invariants form a defense-in-depth chain around the two firewalls:

| Test | Invariant | Failure it prevents |
|---|---|---|
| test_05 | Out-of-fold cosine < in-sample cosine on the fixture; all-missing rows exactly zero | β tuned against an optimistic predictor that does not exist at deployment |
| test_06 | All-missing candidates equal within every query row, finite fused scores | A "neutral" policy that secretly prefers specific information-free candidates |
| test_07 | `β = 0` reproduces the incumbent `argsort` exactly | Fusion code silently perturbing the baseline it claims to improve upon |
| test_08 | `_row_z` is per-query (row mean 0, std 1) and rank-preserving | Standardization changing branch orderings, making β non-interpretable |
| test_09 | CV fold sizes partition exactly; a fold is never scored by its own predictor | Penalty (and thus effect quality) selected on leaked folds |
| test_10 | Frozen constants match declarations (`ALL_MISSING_SCORE == 0.0`, `RIDGE_FOLDS == 5`, …) | Silent drift of the contract between runs |

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L1-L6), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L85-L169)

## Artifact and CLI Interface

The module writes a single JSON artifact, `fusion.json`, under schema `VCDESIGN_CANDIDATE_EFFECT_DISTILLATION_V1_FUSION`, with sorted keys and a runtime block (UTC timestamp, Python and NumPy versions). The console output prints the honesty contrast, the full β selection curve, and a per-row table of MBRU, `Mean@B`, `HighValueCount@B`, guardrail `RU@10` / `J>0@10`, and the paired bootstrap interval against the incumbent.

| CLI argument | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--config` | Frozen `AuditConfig` JSON (checkpoint paths, asset arguments) |
| `--eligibility` | Directory holding `G_fit_eligible.npy` / `G_select_eligible.npy` |
| `--asset` | Directory with `quarter_responses.npy`, `identity_axis.npy`, `four_way_eligible.npy` (guardrail inputs) |
| `--distillation` | Directory of the Phase 1–6 artifact supplying the selected ridge penalty |
| `--output` | Destination for `fusion.json` |
| `--device` | Torch device, default `cuda` |

Sources: [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L146-L155), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L178-L182), [fuse.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/fuse.py#L184-L209)

## Position in the Broader Evaluation

The fusion stage is the integration point of the distillation pipeline: it answers whether the knowledge-feature effect branch adds ranking value *on top of* the incumbent scorer, under leakage-controlled calibration. The leakage mechanics it relies on — identity-level folds, the sealed `G_check`, the fit/select discipline — are analyzed in depth in [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation). For the next stage of the pipeline, continue to [Final Clean Base Scorer](15-final-clean-base-scorer); for how these fused numbers land in the paper's headline results, see [Key Benchmark Findings](26-key-benchmark-findings).


# Final Clean Base Scorer



The Final Clean Base Scorer is the locked retrieval model that produces the paper's primary results. It lives in `src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/`, a self-contained module that defines the model pair (`CLEAN_BASE` and `CLEAN_EFFECT`), the frozen evaluation contract, the training entry point, and the single gated evaluation that reads the `G_check` split. The module's design philosophy is minimal delta: it inherits the incumbent architecture literally and changes exactly one thing — it removes the learnable unknown token — so that every measured difference is attributable to that one correction and nothing else.

Sources: [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L1-L8), [\_\_init\_\_.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/__init__.py#L1-L2)

## Design Thesis: One Correction to the Incumbent

The clean model is a subclass, not a reimplementation. `CleanAttributionModel` extends `GlobalObjectiveKnowledgeAttributionModel` (the SRC-Energy-V2 global retrieval pathway) and swaps only the capability encoder, while `CleanCapabilityEncoder` extends `GlobalCapabilityEncoder` and deletes `unknown_token` from the parameter set. Every other weight, layer, and forward rule is inherited verbatim. This inheritance-by-construction guarantees that a before/after comparison isolates a single causal variable.

Sources: [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L18-L42), [model.py (incumbent)](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/model.py#L1-L3)

The correction matters because the incumbent gave candidates with no legal modality a shared *learnable* token — and the previous phase measured that token sitting at the top of every goal-blind ordering, placing 100% of information-free genes in its Top-10. The clean encoder replaces it with a fixed neutral: a candidate with no evidence contributes exactly zero to the score for every query. Zero is not arbitrary — it is a cosine similarity's own indifference point, chosen before looking at any selection data.

Sources: [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L1-L8), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L1-L28)

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GlobalObjectiveKnowledgeAttributionModel {
        +source_context_encoder
        +global_delta_encoder
        +global_context_modulation
        +global_query_projection
        +logit_scale
        +encode_query(source, goal)
        +score_embeddings(query, candidates)
    }
    class GlobalCapabilityEncoder {
        +adapters: ModuleDict
        +modality_embedding
        +unknown_token: Parameter
        +global_projection
    }
    class CleanCapabilityEncoder {
        unknown_token: deleted
        +forward(descriptors, masks)
    }
    class CleanAttributionModel {
        +capability_encoder: CleanCapabilityEncoder
    }
    GlobalObjectiveKnowledgeAttributionModel <|-- CleanAttributionModel
    GlobalCapabilityEncoder <|-- CleanCapabilityEncoder
    CleanAttributionModel o-- CleanCapabilityEncoder
```

The diagram shows the deliberate one-class-deep inheritance chain: `CleanAttributionModel` replaces its parent's capability encoder with `CleanCapabilityEncoder`, whose defining act is deleting `unknown_token` in `__init__`. The modality adapters and pooling arithmetic flow down unchanged from the frozen V2 knowledge layer.

Sources: [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L18-L26), [knowledge.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/structured_requirement_capability_energy_v2/knowledge.py#L10-L23)

| Behavior | Incumbent (M_SET) | Final clean model |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate present in ≥1 modality | Pooled normalized tokens | Identical (inherited) |
| Candidate missing all modalities | Shared **learnable** UNKNOWN token | Fixed zero embedding → score exactly 0.0 |
| All-missing handling differs per arm | N/A | No — identical in both arms |
| Modality-restricted candidate banks | Available via `encode_modality_embeddings` | Deliberately `NotImplementedError` |
| Goal-blind ordering pathology | Unknown token ranked top of every ordering | Eliminated by construction |

Sources: [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L25-L42), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L44-L48)

> [!TIP]
> The zero-embedding rule is what makes `CLEAN_EFFECT − CLEAN_BASE` a clean causal contrast: because both arms share every weight of one trained network, the score difference isolates the effect branch alone. Insert any learned fallback and the contrast becomes confounded.

## The Frozen Contract: Constants Before Computation

`contract.py` is the module's constitution: every design decision that could have been tuned is pinned as a named constant with a written justification, frozen before training and never revisited. The method of record is `CANDIDATE_EFFECT_DISTILLATION_V1`, the fusion is z-score additive with `beta = 1.0` — chosen *before any `G_check` access* for a principled reason: it is the only member of the fusion family with no fitted coefficient, so it cannot have been tuned on anything.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L31-L38)

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FINAL_METHOD` | `CANDIDATE_EFFECT_DISTILLATION_V1` | Method of record |
| `FINAL_FUSION` / `FINAL_BETA` | `z_score_additive` / `1.0` | No fitted coefficient, selected before `G_check` |
| `PRIMARY_MODALITIES` | `("STRING", "MAPKG")` | Strict legal candidate features |
| `TEXT_STATUS` | `EXCLUDED_FROM_FINAL_PRIMARY_TRACK` | Banned by `GENE_INFORMATION_POLICY_v1` (literature-leakage bar) |
| `ALL_MISSING_CONTRIBUTION` | `0.0` | Neutral cosine value, identical in both arms |
| `ARMS` | `("CLEAN_BASE", "CLEAN_EFFECT")` | One network, two scoring rules |
| `EVALUATION_SPLIT_NAME` | `locked final evaluation split` | Must **not** be called "untouched blind test" |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L31-L61)

Two exclusions deserve attention. TEXT is barred from the primary track because literature-derived gene descriptions leak information the deployment cannot legally use — the legacy incumbent that carries TEXT stays in result tables as historical context but is explicitly *not* the paired comparator. And the split naming is deliberate honesty: earlier phases of the wider programme did read `G_check`, so this phase claims only that its method, predictor, fusion, and checkpoints were selected without it — not that the split is pristine.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L40-L52), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L108-L114)

## Architecture Walkthrough: Query, Candidates, and the Neutral Embedding

The query path is inherited intact. A source state and goal state (each `[B, 8248]`) are encoded separately: a source context encoder produces a 512-dim context vector, while a deeper delta encoder embeds `goal − source`. A zero-initialized context modulation layer then produces FiLM-style `gamma`/`beta` parameters that scale and shift the delta embedding, and the result is projected to 256 dimensions and L2-normalized.

Sources: [model.py (incumbent)](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/model.py#L128-L151)

The candidate path is where the clean model diverges. Each modality (STRING: 512-d, MAPKG: 1024-d) passes through its own frozen V2 `CapabilityAdapter` (LayerNorm → Linear-512 → GELU → Dropout → Linear-128 → LayerNorm), is augmented with a learned modality embedding, and normalized into a token. The clean encoder then performs masked mean pooling over *present* tokens only — no UNKNOWN token is appended — projects to 256 dims, normalizes, and finally zeroes the embedding of any candidate with no present modality via `torch.where`.

Sources: [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L28-L36), [knowledge.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/structured_requirement_capability_energy_v2/knowledge.py#L15-L23)

Scoring is a scaled inner product: `logit_scale.exp().clamp(max=100) × (query · candidate)`. Because an all-missing candidate's embedding is the zero vector, its inner product against *every* query is exactly zero — the neutral cosine value falls out of the arithmetic rather than being special-cased in the scorer. A convenience helper, `all_missing_mask`, recomputes the all-missing flag from role arrays by OR-ing the per-modality presence masks, keeping the candidate axis ordering stable.
