Sources: [model.py (incumbent)](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/model.py#L153-L166), [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L45-L67)

> [!TIP]
> Training enforces the architecture's invariant at runtime: `train.py` scans `model.named_parameters()` and aborts if any name ends with `unknown_token`. The invariant is tested, asserted at build time, and structurally impossible to violate silently.

## Two Arms, One Network: CLEAN_BASE and CLEAN_EFFECT

One network is trained; the two arms are two *scoring rules* over the same weights. `CLEAN_BASE` is the network's raw retrieval score. `CLEAN_EFFECT` fuses that score with the frozen distillation effect branch: per-query-row z-scores of the base matrix plus `beta = 1.0` times per-query-row z-scores of `cos(d_q, r̂_c)` effect matrices, where all-missing candidates receive the declared neutral `0.0`. Row-wise z-scoring is order-preserving, so it changes only the calibration between arms, never the base ranker's internal ordering.

Sources: [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L10-L16), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L95-L133)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Strict-legal role arrays<br/>STRING + MAPKG only"] --> B["base_scores<br/>encode_candidates once,<br/>query encoding batched (64)"]
    A --> C["FrozenEffectPredictor.effect<br/>rank-256 basis + ridge,<br/>all-missing → 0.0"]
    B --> D["row_z<br/>(per query row)"]
    C --> E["effect_scores<br/>cos of delta vs predicted response"]
    D --> F["fuse:<br/>row_z base + 1.0 × row_z effect"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["CLEAN_EFFECT matrix"]
    B --> H["CLEAN_BASE matrix"]
```

The effect predictor is not loaded from disk — it is *rebuilt deterministically* from `G_fit` (consensus response → randomized rank-256 basis → ridge path at the CV-selected penalty) and then verified against the artifact the distillation phase saved, with a hard failure above `1e-3` max absolute difference. Recomputing makes the locked evaluation self-contained; checking makes it provably the same predictor.

Sources: [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L73-L92), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L1-L9)

| Property | CLEAN_BASE | CLEAN_EFFECT |
|---|---|---|
| Score source | Trained network only | Network + frozen ridge effect predictor |
| Extra artifacts needed | Checkpoint only | Checkpoint + `G_fit` arrays + penalty |
| Effect-branch information | None | Static legal features → predicted response |
| All-missing candidate score | 0.0 | 0.0 (identical rule) |
| Checkpoint selection | Own epoch, own rule | Own epoch, own rule |
| Role in comparison | Baseline arm | Primary arm (`CLEAN_EFFECT − CLEAN_BASE`) |

Sources: [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L130-L133), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L82-L92)

## Phase D: Training by Construction, Not by Inspection

Phase D's central claim is that the incumbent's recipe is *imported, not reimplemented*: `_epoch`, `_role_tensors`, `_seed`, `capture_branch_state`, and every hyperparameter constant come from the incumbent's `train_factorial.py`, so optimizer, scheduler, loss, sampler, batch size, seed, and objective schedule are identical **by construction** rather than by inspection. Exactly two deltas exist: the modality set is the strict legal pair (no TEXT), and the capability encoder has no learnable unknown token.

Sources: [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L1-L35)

| Recipe element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Seed | 20260916 | `train_factorial.SEED` (imported) |
| Optimizer | AdamW, LR 1e-4, WD 1e-4 | imported constants |
| Gradient clip | 1.0 | `CLIP_NORM` |
| Batch size | 8 identities | `BATCH_SIZE` |
| Objective schedule | PAIR epochs 1–5 → SET epochs 6–10 | `_epoch(objective=...)` |
| PAIR loss | `top_focused_pairwise_loss` (gt/predicted top-128, 256 random negatives, ≤4096 pairs/query) | imported |
| SET loss | `gt_top20_positive_set_loss` (positive_k=20) | imported |
| Precision | bfloat16 autocast on CUDA | `amp = device.type == "cuda"` |

Sources: [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L19-L30), [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L72-L77), [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L110-L121)

The data path enforces legality defensively. The frozen asset loader only admits STRING or STRING+MAPKG+TEXT configurations, so `train.py` uses it *exactly as frozen* and then drops TEXT immediately via `strict_legal_role` — before any tensor exists — double-checking with runtime assertions (`"TEXT" in tensors` → hard failure). Checkpoints for epochs past the base phase are saved with SHA-256 digests, tagged with the schema `VCDESIGN_FINAL_CLEAN_MODEL_V1`, and a `train_manifest.json` records the full recipe, history, parameter count, and a `read_G_check: False` attestation.

Sources: [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L38-L60), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L29-L48), [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L62-L107)

## Phases E–G: Selection, Lock, and the One Gated Evaluation

Phase E (`select.py`) is allowed exactly one decision: which epoch of the single training curve each arm uses, scored on `G_select` by median MBRU, with each arm free to pick its own checkpoint because each is scored by its own rule. Everything else — architecture, fusion, predictor, feature set, sampler, loss, query gate — is fixed before the script runs, and each per-epoch evaluation also records a guardrail block and the fraction of all-missing candidates in the top-budget prefix.

Sources: [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L1-L9), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L84-L131)

Phase F (`lock.py`) writes the pre-evaluation seal: it hashes every source file in the four dependent packages into a combined `code_digest` (because a commit hash alone cannot identify uncommitted work), records the git commit, the selected checkpoints, the fusion, the predictor penalty, and the full evaluation protocol — then refuses to overwrite an existing lock and self-hashes the record into `lock_sha256`. After this file exists, no configuration change is permitted.

Sources: [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L1-L9), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L21-L58)

Phase G (`gcheck.py`) is the one locked final evaluation — the *only* code in the repository that reaches `G_check`, and only through `locked_check_arrays`, which demands the explicit acknowledgement string `"I_AM_PERFORMING_THE_ONE_LOCKED_FINAL_EVALUATION"` and refuses to overwrite its own output. It scores seven policy rows (RANDOM, STRICT_LEGAL_CANDIDATE_PRIOR, EFFECT_BRANCH_ONLY, LEGACY_M_SET, CLEAN_BASE, CLEAN_EFFECT, MEASURED_RESPONSE_ORACLE), applies the frozen `QUERY_ELIGIBILITY_V1` gate at FDR 0.05 unchanged, and reports paired identity-cluster bootstrap contrasts (10,000 replicates) with `CLEAN_EFFECT − CLEAN_BASE` as the primary comparison.

Sources: [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L25-L26), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L55-L70), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L1-L17), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L43-L55)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D["Phase D: train.py<br/>reads G_fit only<br/>PAIR → SET schedule"] --> E["Phase E: select.py<br/>reads G_select<br/>one checkpoint per arm"]
    E --> F["Phase F: lock.py<br/>code digest + checkpoint hashes<br/>config frozen"]
    F --> G["Phase G: gcheck.py<br/>G_check via acknowledgement gate<br/>refuses overwrite"]
```

| Phase | Module | Split read | Decision permitted | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D | `train.py` | `G_fit` | None (frozen recipe) | Checkpoints + `train_manifest.json` |
| E | `select.py` | `G_select` | Checkpoint epoch per arm, nothing else | Selection record + SHA-256s |
| F | `lock.py` | none | None (hashes + seals) | `VCDESIGN_FINAL_LOCK_V1` record |
| G | `gcheck.py` | `G_check` (gated) | None (reads the lock) | Locked evaluation record |

Sources: [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L30-L35), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L125-L131), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L56-L70), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L54-L55)

## Protocol Guarantees: What the Test Suite Pins Down

`test_protocol.py` converts the contract's prose promises into twelve executable assertions, so the guarantees survive refactoring. They cover the model invariants (no unknown token, exact-zero all-missing scores, single-modality candidates not treated as missing), the security gate (wrong acknowledgements raise `PermissionError`; the frozen loader still refuses `G_check` for all other callers), the fusion's frozen form and ordering preservation, TEXT exclusion, honest split naming, and the strict-legal restriction's error paths.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/test_protocol.py#L1-L19)

| Test | Guarantee enforced |
|---|---|
| `test_01` | No parameter named `*_unknown_token` exists on the clean model |
| `test_02` | All-missing candidate embedding is exactly zero; scores exactly `ALL_MISSING_CONTRIBUTION` |
| `test_03` | A candidate present in one modality is *not* treated as missing |
| `test_04` / `test_05` | `G_check` unreachable without the acknowledgement; loader refuses it elsewhere |
| `test_06` / `test_07` | Fusion is exactly `row_z(base) + row_z(effect)`; `row_z` preserves per-query orderings |
| `test_08` / `test_09` | TEXT excluded; split named "locked final evaluation split", never "untouched blind test" |
| `test_10`–`test_12` | Strict-legal restriction drops TEXT, errors on missing modality; modality banks undefined |

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/test_protocol.py#L20-L142)

## Running It and Where to Go Next

Reproduction starts with the Phase D entry point, which writes checkpoints and a manifest and refuses non-empty output directories; the frozen reference checkpoint for the paper run is `checkpoints/final_clean_epoch_008.pt`, whose SHA-256 is recorded in `configs/paper_run_v1.json` and the processed-data manifest:

```bash
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.final_clean_model_v1.train \
  --config configs/paper_run_v1.json \
  --output outputs/final_clean_train \
  --device cuda
```

Sources: [REPRODUCE.md](REPRODUCE.md#L28-L43)

To go deeper, follow the catalog: [Training Pipeline and Frozen Configuration](16-training-pipeline-and-frozen-configuration) details the incumbent recipe internals that Phase D imports; [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection) explains the fusion family that `beta = 1` was chosen from; [Knowledge Features: STRING and MAP-KG](13-knowledge-features-string-and-map-kg) covers the candidate descriptors feeding the capability adapters; [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation) and [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests) expand the hygiene machinery seen in Phases F–G; and [Key Benchmark Findings](26-key-benchmark-findings) reports what the locked evaluation found.


# Training Pipeline and Frozen Configuration



This page documents how the final clean base scorer is trained, how checkpoints are selected, and — critically — **what is frozen, when it was frozen, and why it can never be re-tuned**. The system is organized as a four-phase pipeline (train → select → lock → evaluate) under a strict information barrier: the held-out evaluation role `G_check` is structurally unreachable until the final phase, and every hyperparameter is committed *before* that phase runs. This page assumes you have read the model description in [Final Clean Base Scorer](15-final-clean-base-scorer).

## Pipeline Position: Four Phases Under an Information Barrier

The training pipeline is not a single script but a sequence of phases, each producing artifacts that later phases consume and hash. The defining constraint is that Phases D and E operate exclusively on `G_fit` (fitting) and `G_select` (selection); `G_check` is sealed behind an explicit acknowledgement string and a pre-evaluation lock:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    D["Phase D: train.py<br/>Train ONE network on G_fit<br/>Recipe imported from incumbent<br/>Saves branch checkpoints (epochs 6-10)"]
    E["Phase E: select.py<br/>Score every checkpoint on G_select<br/>Pick ONE epoch per arm<br/>Verify frozen effect predictor"]
    F["Phase F: lock.py<br/>Hash code + checkpoints + penalty<br/>Refuses overwrite<br/>Record: VCDESIGN_FINAL_LOCK_V1"]
    G["Phase G: gcheck.py<br/>The ONE locked evaluation<br/>Requires acknowledgement string<br/>Reads G_check"]
    GC[("G_check<br/>sealed split")]
    X(["No config change<br/>permitted after this point"])

    D -->|"train_manifest.json + .pt files"| E
    E -->|"selection record<br/>per-arm epoch + sha256"| F
    F -->|"lock record"| G
    F --> X
    G -.->|"locked_check_arrays<br/>acknowledgement required"| GC
    E -.->|"read_G_check: False"| GC
    D -.->|"read_G_check: False"| GC
```

Each training and selection manifest explicitly records `"read_G_check": False` ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L86-L91), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L85-L91)), and the selection phase states the only decision it may take: *"the checkpoint epoch of each arm, and nothing else"* ([select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L87)).

Sources: [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L1-L124), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L1-L146), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L1-L162), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L1-L70)

## The Imported Recipe: Identical by Construction

The most consequential design decision in Phase D is a negative one: **the training recipe is not reimplemented**. The optimizer, scheduler, loss, sampler, batch size, seed, horizon, and objective schedule are *imported as Python objects* from the incumbent's training module, `global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1.train_factorial` — so they are identical to the incumbent *by construction* rather than by inspection ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L6-L12)). This eliminates an entire class of reproduction bugs: a transcription error in a constant would be a *different program*, and here that program cannot exist.

Exactly **two deliberate deviations** from the incumbent exist, and both are enforced with runtime assertions rather than comments:
1. The modality set is the strict legal one (STRING + MAPKG) without TEXT — enforced by raising if TEXT ever reaches a tensor ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L38-L53)).
2. The capability encoder has no learnable unknown token — enforced by scanning `named_parameters()` for any name ending in `unknown_token` ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L54-L56)).

The frozen recipe constants ([train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L27-L28)):

| Constant | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `SEED` | `20260916` | Seeds `random`, NumPy, and Torch (all devices) before training |
| `LR` | `1e-4` | AdamW learning rate |
| `WEIGHT_DECAY` | `1e-4` | AdamW weight decay |
| `CLIP_NORM` | `1.0` | Gradient clipping bound |
| `BATCH_SIZE` | `8` | Rows per optimizer step |
| `BASE_EPOCHS` | `5` | Epochs 1–5 run the `PAIR` objective |
| `FINAL_EPOCH` | `10` | Total horizon; epochs 6–10 run the `SET` objective |

The optimizer is constructed once — `torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=LR, weight_decay=WEIGHT_DECAY)` — and randomness flows through a dedicated `torch.Generator` seeded with `SEED`, which the sampler, pairwise-loss pair selection, and negative mining all share ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L57-L60), [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L74-L75)). Mixed precision is enabled automatically whenever the device is CUDA, using `torch.autocast` with `bfloat16` ([train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L83-L84)).

Sources: [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L6-L60), [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L27-L84)

## Objective Schedule: PAIR Then SET

Training runs one network through a **two-stage objective schedule**. Epochs 1–5 (`BASE_EPOCHS`) optimize the `PAIR` objective; epochs 6–10 optimize the `SET` objective. The stage name maps deterministically to a loss composition via `combined_v2_loss` ([train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L41-L47)):

| Objective | Epochs | Composition | Loss components |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PAIR` ("global") | 1–5 | `pair_loss` alone | `top_focused_pairwise_loss` |
| `SET` ("conditional") | 6–10 | `pair_loss + 0.5 * set_loss` | pairwise + `gt_top20_positive_set_loss` |

The **pairwise term** is top-focused and utility-gap-weighted: for each query it takes the union of the ground-truth top-128, the predicted top-128, and 256 random eligible candidates (never materializing a full N² grid), forms pairs whose utility gap exceeds the measurement margin, caps at 4096 pairs per query, and weights each pair by its utility gap normalized by the eligible IQR ([loss.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/open_vocab_dual_encoder_v1/loss.py#L20-L46)). The generating intervention itself is masked out via `self_indices` in both pair construction and reduction ([loss.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/open_vocab_dual_encoder_v1/loss.py#L40-L46)).

The **set term** is a top-20 set loss: `logsumexp` over all legal candidates minus `logsumexp` over the ground-truth top-20 legal candidates ([loss.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/structured_requirement_capability_energy_v2/loss.py#L9-L33)). During `PAIR` epochs the set loss is present but detached and zeroed (`pair_loss.detach() * 0.0`), keeping the graph shape uniform across stages ([train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L87-L91)).

Sources: [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L41-L91), [loss.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/open_vocab_dual_encoder_v1/loss.py#L20-L46), [loss.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/structured_requirement_capability_energy_v2/loss.py#L35-L41)

## Checkpoint Policy: Branch States After the Objective Switch

Checkpoints are **not** written every epoch. Only epochs after `BASE_EPOCHS` — i.e., the epochs where the `SET` branch objective is active — are persisted, and each payload is a complete *branch state* captured by `capture_branch_state`: model weights, optimizer state, generator state, plus the Python/NumPy/Torch/CUDA RNG states ([train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L44-L62)). Full RNG capture means any checkpoint can restore bit-exact training continuation; the restore path even guards against serialized RNG byte tensors having been moved to CUDA by `map_location` ([train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L64-L76)).

Each saved payload is stamped with the schema `VCDESIGN_FINAL_CLEAN_MODEL_V1`, its epoch, its objective, the modality list, and the all-missing rule, then immediately hashed to SHA-256 ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L82-L92)). The run terminates by writing `train_manifest.json`, which embeds the entire recipe, per-epoch history (loss, pair/set components, gradient norm, wall-clock seconds), parameter count, and the checkpoint→sha256 map ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L86-L108)).

> [!TIP]
> The single-network design is what makes the two arms scientifically meaningful: `CLEAN_BASE` is the network's score, and `CLEAN_EFFECT` is that same score fused with the frozen effect branch at β=1. Because they share every weight, `CLEAN_EFFECT − CLEAN_BASE` is a *clean causal contrast* isolating the effect branch — no architecture confound is possible ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L6-L12)).

Sources: [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L61-L108), [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L44-L76)

## Per-Arm Checkpoint Selection (Phase E)

Phase E scores **every** saved checkpoint on `G_select` under both arms and then picks one epoch per arm — and per-arm selection is explicitly permitted because each arm is scored by its own rule ([select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L1-L8)). Before any scoring, Phase E performs a self-integrity check: it *rebuilds* the frozen effect predictor deterministically from `G_fit` (consensus response → randomized basis → ridge path with the penalty recorded in the distillation artifact) and verifies the reconstruction against the saved prediction array, aborting if the max absolute difference exceeds 1e-3 ([scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L66-L84), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L86-L95)).

For each candidate epoch, both arms are evaluated on directional metrics (aggregated over the two measurement views), the production guardrail, and the fraction of all-missing candidates appearing in each budget prefix ([select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L99-L121)). Selection is then a single argmax per arm:

```python
best = max(record["epochs"],
           key=lambda e: record["epochs"][e]["arms"][arm]["direction"]["MBRU"]["median"])
```
([select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L123-L130))

The paper's frozen outcome is recorded in the release configuration: `FINAL_CLEAN_EPOCH_008` was selected for both `CLEAN_BASE` and `CLEAN_EFFECT`, with its SHA-256 (`58da13d2…`) pinned in `configs/paper_run_v1.json` ([paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L26-L44)).

Sources: [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L85-L136), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L66-L84), [paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L17-L44)

## The Frozen Configuration Contract

The contract module is the normative statement of what is frozen. It was **frozen before training and never revisited** ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L3-L5)). Each entry pairs a decision with its justification, and several entries encode anti-hindsight rules as booleans:

| Frozen item | Value | Stated reason |
|---|---|---|
| Method of record | `CANDIDATE_EFFECT_DISTILLATION_V1` | The pipeline's declared method ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L23)) |
| Fusion form | `z_score_additive`, β = 1.0 | The only fusion in the family with **no fitted coefficient**, so it cannot have been tuned on anything; chosen before any `G_check` access, not on performance ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L24-L29)) |
| Primary modalities | `("STRING", "MAPKG")` | TEXT excluded by `GENE_INFORMATION_POLICY_v1` (literature-leakage bar) ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L32-L34)) |
| All-missing contribution | `0.0`, non-learnable | Zero is a cosine's own indifference point; the incumbent's learnable shared unknown token produced goal-blind top-10s of information-free genes ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L36-L40)) |
| Arms | `CLEAN_BASE`, `CLEAN_EFFECT` | Legacy M_SET is context only, never the primary comparator ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L42-L44)) |
| Split naming | "locked final evaluation split" | Must **not** be called "untouched blind test" — earlier programme phases read `G_check` ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L46-L48)) |
| Post-lock policy | `NO_CONFIG_CHANGE_ALLOWED_AFTER_G_CHECK_ACCESS = True` | No configuration change permitted after `G_check` access ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L50)) |

The release configuration `configs/paper_run_v1.json` (schema `VCDESIGN_PAPER_RUN_V1`) operationalizes this contract as concrete artifact paths: eleven input assets (freeze records, response cache, STRING/MAPKG features), comparator checkpoints (`M_PAIR` and `M_SET` at epoch 10 under the "frozen GOKA final config endpoint" rule), five cached score arrays, and the pinned SHA-256 of the selected final checkpoint ([paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L1-L44)).

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L1-L61), [paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L1-L44)

## Pre-Evaluation Lock (Phase F) and the G_check Gate

Phase F writes the pre-evaluation lock — the mechanism that turns "we promise not to retune" into a machine-checkable artifact. It hashes **every source file** in the four code packages the evaluation depends on (`final_clean_model_v1`, `candidate_effect_distillation_v1`, `utility_gt_v2`, `action_conditioned_utility_v1`) into a combined digest, deliberately, because a commit hash alone cannot identify code in a checkout with uncommitted work ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L19-L40)). The record also pins the effect-predictor penalty, fusion form, per-arm selected checkpoints with their SHA-256s, the bootstrap statistic (paired identity-cluster bootstrap, 10000 replicates, seed 20260916), and an explicit `G_check_never_used_to_select` block asserting this for method, predictor, fusion, checkpoints, query gate, and feature contract alike ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L68-L134)). It **refuses to overwrite an existing lock** and self-hashes into `lock_sha256` ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L62-L66), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L134)).

`G_check` itself is reachable through exactly **one** function in the entire repository, `locked_check_arrays`, which refuses to run unless the caller passes the literal acknowledgement string `"I_AM_PERFORMING_THE_ONE_LOCKED_FINAL_EVALUATION"` — deliberately awkward to call, so it cannot be reached by accident or by a default argument ([scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L18-L63)). Phase G is the only caller; it also refuses to overwrite its own output, making a second, adjusted run into the same path impossible ([gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L40-L42)). The evaluation module reads its checkpoints and predictor penalty **from the lock record**, so the lock is load-bearing, not ceremonial ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L4-L7)).

> [!TIP]
> The honesty boundary is encoded in naming: the contract requires this split be called a "locked final evaluation split" and forbids calling it an "untouched blind test", because earlier phases of the wider research programme *did* read `G_check` ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L46-L48), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L97-L104)). What is guaranteed is narrower and verifiable: this phase's method, predictor, fusion, and checkpoints were selected without it.

Sources: [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L19-L134), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L18-L63), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L1-L70)

## Running the Pipeline

After installing the package and downloading the processed data snapshot (verified against `DATA_MANIFEST.json` via `tools/verify_processed_data.py`), Phase D runs as a module invocation with three arguments ([REPRODUCE.md](REPRODUCE.md#L26-L39)):

```bash
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.final_clean_model_v1.train \
  --config configs/paper_run_v1.json \
  --output outputs/final_clean_train \
  --device cuda
```

| Parameter | Required | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--config` | yes | — | Path to the frozen `AuditConfig` (release: `configs/paper_run_v1.json`) |
| `--output` | yes | — | Output directory; **must not exist** — the run refuses to overwrite ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L38-L39)) |
| `--device` | no | `cuda` | Any Torch device string; CPU runs are possible but the recipe assumes CUDA-speed AMP |

Note that `--device` defaults to `cuda`, and AMP (`bfloat16`) activates automatically only on CUDA; on CPU the identical arithmetic runs in full precision ([train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L59-L60), [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L83-L84)). For a lower-friction entry point before committing to the full run, the synthetic demo at [Synthetic Demo Walkthrough](3-synthetic-demo-walkthrough) exercises the same contracts on a small fixture.

Sources: [REPRODUCE.md](REPRODUCE.md#L26-L39), [train.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/train.py#L111-L123), [train_factorial.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1/train_factorial.py#L83-L84)

## Where to Go Next

The training pipeline sits at the center of a web of contracts documented elsewhere in this catalog. To understand *what the network computes* (query/candidate encoders, scoring), read [Final Clean Base Scorer](15-final-clean-base-scorer). For the frozen effect branch that `CLEAN_EFFECT` fuses in — the rank-256 response basis, ridge predictor, and β-fusion family — see [Response Basis Construction](11-response-basis-construction), [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor), and [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection). The lock and hash mechanisms connect directly to artifact integrity verification in [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests) and to the protocol tests guarding them in [Protocol Test Suite](24-protocol-test-suite). Finally, how the two arms are compared at budgeted ranking is the subject of [Ranking Metrics: BU@B, MU@B, PHR@B](8-ranking-metrics-buatb-muatb-phratb).

# Four-Context Data Contracts



This page documents the `four_context_v1` package: the pre-registered data contracts that let one experiment ask whether a perturbation-response model improves when its atlas grows from one cell context (K562) to four (K562, RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat). The contracts govern who trains on what, which genes every context is reduced to, how the measurement recipe is inherited from the frozen K562 lock, and which quantities were fixed before any model ran. Everything here lives in `src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/`, and nothing in it retunes a threshold after seeing a result.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L1-L52), [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L1-L18)

## Why Four Contexts: Three Pre-Registered Questions

The contract exists to answer three questions, stated in the module docstring before any HepG2 or Jurkat number existed: **Q1** — does a larger perturbation atlas improve the `static knowledge → effect geometry` mapping; **Q2** — does any improvement come from more training rows or from more biological contexts; **Q3** — after controlling atlas size, does `f(candidate, source context)` beat `f(candidate)` on a cell context never seen in training. Q2 is the reason the mission exists: a pooled atlas gains both rows and diversity simultaneously, so a pooled win alone is uninterpretable. Every scaling claim in the package is therefore paired with a row-count-matched control in which the only thing that changes is how many contexts the same number of rows came from.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L3-L13)

## The Four Contexts and Their Asymmetric Provenance

The context roster is frozen as a module constant — `CONTEXTS = ("K562", "RPE1", "HepG2", "Jurkat")` — with K562 designated the **anchor** (`ANCHOR_CONTEXT = "K562"`) and HepG2/Jurkat the new acquisitions from accession `GSE264667`. There is a declared asymmetry: RPE1, HepG2 and Jurkat are produced by `build.py` through a single code path, while K562 is loaded from its frozen assets because the anchor lock forbids rebuilding it. The package's safety argument for this asymmetry is recorded rather than hidden — the anchor's source states carry exactly the definition `build.py` implements, and the anchor's manifest records that `x_goal − x_source` reproduces the frozen response cache to 4.2e-06.

| Context | Role | Data provenance | Build path | Training input | Query population |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K562 | Frozen anchor | Frozen lock assets (`VCDesign_FINAL_LOCK_2026-09-18.md`) | Loaded, never rebuilt | Anchor `G_fit` identities only | `G_select` identities, eligibility-gated |
| RPE1 | Built context | Per audit record | `build.py`, frozen recipe | Every usable identity | Every usable, eligible identity |
| HepG2 | New context | `GSE264667_hepg2_raw_singlecell_01.h5ad` | `build.py`, frozen recipe | Every usable identity | Every usable, eligible identity |
| Jurkat | New context | `GSE264667_jurkat_raw_singlecell_01.h5ad` | `build.py`, frozen recipe | Every usable identity | Every usable, eligible identity |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L56-L65), [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L1-L9), [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L30-L32)

## The Uniform `Context` Dataclass

Every context — built or frozen — is reduced to the same frozen dataclass so that nothing downstream special-cases a dataset. A `Context` carries the identity axis `ids`, the gene axis `genes`, the response tensors `responses` and `sources` (each `[2, n, g]` float32, one layer per measurement view, with responses defined as *perturbed minus matched control*), and four boolean gates: `usable` (depth gate passed in both views), `eligible` (`QUERY_ELIGIBILITY_V1`), `train_ok` and `query_ok`. Two derived properties, `fit_rows` (`usable & train_ok`) and `query_rows` (`usable & query_ok & eligible`), are the only rows any consumer is permitted to touch, and `summary()` emits a per-context dict that folds embed verbatim in their output records.

Sources: [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L35-L61)

Two loaders produce this object. `load_built()` reads the arrays `build.py` wrote to disk (`identity_axis.npy`, `gene_axis.npy`, `side_responses.npy`, `side_sources.npy`, `usable.npy`, `eligible.npy`) and accepts an optional gene axis to restrict to. `load_anchor()` reads K562 from the frozen lock instead: it takes the cached responses and source states, sets `train_ok` only on `role_indices["G_fit"]` and `query_ok` only on `role_indices["G_select"]`, loads per-role eligibility vectors, and — critically — **drops `G_check` rows from every array the programme can reach**, raising a `RuntimeError` if any sealed identity ever becomes reachable.

Sources: [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L79-L91), [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L94-L132)

## The Inherited Measurement Contract

The new contexts do not get a recipe chosen for them; they get the anchor's recipe, reproduced. Phase 2 of the protocol requires that the A/B batch hash, the quarter refinement, the minimum cell threshold, per-batch control subtraction, the identity-incidence-weighted control reference and the `QUERY_ELIGIBILITY_V1` gate are taken from the frozen K562 lock and applied unchanged. The frozen constants are module-level: `LIBRARY_TARGET = 1.0e4`, `MIN_VIEW_CELLS = 25`, `VIEW_SEED = 20260914`, the namespaces `REPLOGLE_BATCH_DISJOINT_V1` and `REPLOGLE_BATCH_QUAD_REFINEMENT_V1`, and `ELIGIBILITY_FDR = 0.05`. One documented quirk is accepted rather than worked around: the batch hash is applied to each context's *own* batch names, so two contexts whose lanes coincidentally share names receive the same A/B pattern — harmless because no quantity in the programme ever pairs a batch in one context with a batch in another.

| Parameter | Frozen value | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LIBRARY_TARGET` | 1.0e4 | Normalize each cell to this library size, then `log1p` |
| `MIN_VIEW_CELLS` | 25 | Minimum cells per identity per view, both sides |
| `VIEW_SEED` / namespaces | 20260914 / `REPLOGLE_BATCH_DISJOINT_V1`, `..._QUAD_REFINEMENT_V1` | Deterministic A/B side and four-way quarter assignment per batch |
| `ELIGIBILITY_FDR` | 0.05 | FDR level of the `QUERY_ELIGIBILITY_V1` query gate |
| `INHERITED_FROM` | `VCDesign_FINAL_LOCK_2026-09-18.md` | The K562 anchor lock these values come from |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L16-L33), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L67-L74)

`build.py` implements this recipe as a streaming pipeline that trains nothing and ranks nothing. `view_side()` derives each batch's frozen A/B bit from a SHA-256 token over the namespace, seed and batch name, and `quarter_of()` derives the four-way refinement used for cross-fitted estimation. `accumulate()` performs one pass computing per-side, per-quarter and per-batch-control sums — with the deliberate detail that the library-size denominator is computed on the full gene row *before* ambiguous-gene restriction, because normalization is a property of the cell, not of whichever genes the programme keeps. Duplicated gene symbols are dropped entirely (both copies) rather than deduplicated, since a repeated symbol would otherwise let one column silently win untraceably.

Sources: [build.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/build.py#L1-L12), [build.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/build.py#L33-L43), [build.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/build.py#L46-L104), [build.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/build.py#L124-L136)

> [!TIP]
> Phase 1 (`audit.py`) runs *before* the build and reads data properties only, never a model. It resolves the perturbation, batch and guide columns from a priority list declared before looking at the files, and its `count_semantics()` check detects whether a matrix is raw counts or already normalized — because the inherited 1e4/log1p recipe applied to an already-normalized matrix would produce a plausible-looking response that no downstream stage could detect as wrong.

Sources: [audit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/audit.py#L1-L36), [audit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/audit.py#L56-L92)

## Hard Qualification Conditions (Phase 1)

A context only enters the programme if it passes eight hard qualification conditions, evaluated by the audit and recorded as failed rather than relaxed when they fail: gene-level CRISPRi knockdown, explicit non-targeting controls, batch/gemgroup structure, every retained batch having controls, minimum view cells on both sides, at least several hundred usable identities (`MIN_USABLE_IDENTITIES = 300`, fixed before the audit runs), a sufficient common gene axis, and no candidate response leaking into inference features. These are the contract's admission gate; a dataset that fails one is out, not adjusted.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L97-L108)

## The `G_4` Gene Axis and the Anchor Bridge

**The gene axis is the one genuinely new construction** in this programme. `G_4` is the intersection of the four measured axes, taken once via `common_gene_axis()` before any model runs; the historical K562 result keeps its 8248-gene axis and is not recomputed, making the four-context programme a separate experiment on `G_4`. Restriction is strict: `_restrict()` raises `KeyError` naming the count if a context does not measure a requested gene, rather than filling with zeros.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L28-L32), [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L64-L76), [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L135-L142)

Because every context is scored by the same frozen K562 `CLEAN_BASE` ranker, every context's `G_4` values must be placed on the anchor's 8248-gene axis. `harness.anchor_bridge()` computes where each `G_4` gene sits on the anchor axis (raising if any gene is absent), and `embed()` places values there and zeros everything else. The embed applies to K562 too — leaving the anchor on its full axis while others carry ~7000 would make the base stronger in one context for a reason unrelated to the question. The base is never retrained, never adapted, and never told which context it is looking at, which deliberately makes the K562 fold's `effect − base` delta *harder* rather than easier; the contract declares this asymmetry instead of correcting it.

Sources: [harness.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/harness.py#L49-L71), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L34-L43)

## Architecture: From Contexts to Folds

The module interaction pattern is "pack once, fold many": contexts are loaded, reduced to `ContextPack`s (features, base scores, utility, fit masks) exactly once per context, and every fold, arm and atlas size reuses those packs. This separation is deliberate — if packs were rebuilt per arm, an arm-to-arm difference could come from a rebuild rather than from the arm.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Frozen["Frozen zone — never rebuilt"]
        K562["K562 anchor assets<br/>cache + sources + eligibility"]
        LOCK["CLEAN_BASE checkpoint<br/>(frozen lock)"]
    end
    subgraph Built["Built per context"]
        AUDIT["audit.py<br/>Phase 1: 8 conditions"]
        BUILD["build.py<br/>Phase 2: frozen recipe"]
        NEW["RPE1 / HepG2 / Jurkat"]
    end
    AUDIT --> BUILD --> NEW
    K562 --> PACK
    NEW --> PACK
    LOCK --> PACK["harness.py<br/>ContextPack (once per context)"]
    PACK --> OV["overlap.py<br/>strata + overlap matrix"]
    PACK --> LOCO["loco.py<br/>Phases 6-7: 4 LOCO folds × 7 designs"]
    PACK --> MATCH["matched.py<br/>Phase 8: row-budget matched"]
    PACK --> V2["v2.py<br/>Phases 12-14: context residual"]
    LOCO --> SC["scaling.py<br/>Phase 9: N vs C decomposition"]
```

Sources: [harness.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/harness.py#L1-L8), [harness.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/harness.py#L28-L47)

## Candidate Strata: Two Generalizations, Never Collapsed

Phase 5 defines the strata every result is split by, and the contract's note is explicit: **context generalization and candidate generalization are different questions and are never collapsed into one number**. A candidate whose response was measured in a training context had its own effect supervised, so evaluating it in a held context tests whether the *context* transfers; a candidate no training context measured additionally tests whether the *candidate mapping* transfers. `COMMON4` — identities usable in all four contexts — is the only population on which a context residual can be estimated at all. Membership is a property of which identities were measured where; it never depends on a score.

| Stratum | Definition | Question answered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ALL` | Every usable candidate in the held context | Overall performance |
| `SEEN_CANDIDATE` | Response was supervised in ≥1 training context | Does the *context* transfer? |
| `UNSEEN_CANDIDATE` | No training context measured it | Does the *candidate mapping* transfer too? |
| `COMMON4` | Measured in all four contexts | Only population for residual estimation |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L110-L115), [overlap.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/overlap.py#L1-L13), [overlap.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/overlap.py#L21-L43)

`overlap.py` also computes the pairwise identity-overlap matrix (shared counts and Jaccard per context pair) and the histogram of identities measured in exactly *k* contexts, all from data alone via `fold_strata()` so a fold needs no recomputation.

Sources: [overlap.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/overlap.py#L46-L80)

## The LOCO Fold Design and Its Fixed Evaluation Population

`loco.py` (Phases 6–7) runs four leave-one-context-out folds. In each, the held context's responses are invisible to every predictor because the training pool is built only from the other three contexts — there is deliberately **no hash split inside a context**, since a held context contributes no training row at all in a LOCO fold, and splitting it further would only throw away half its queries (this is the anchor-only exception discussed below). Each fold trains the unchanged V1 recipe on seven atlas designs: three single contexts, three pairs, and the pooled triple. The evaluation population is fixed per fold — `SEEN_CANDIDATE` is defined against the *full* three-context training set, not per design, so a one-context and a three-context design are graded on the same candidates, with each design separately reporting what fraction of each stratum it actually supervised.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L76-L82), [loco.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/loco.py#L1-L17), [loco.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/loco.py#L44-L49), [loco.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/loco.py#L94-L110)

A `RANDOM` score arm (seeded per fold) is present but explicitly not the comparison of record: it exists so `BASE` is interpretable in a context the frozen base ranker has never seen — if `BASE − RANDOM` collapses somewhere, a large `V1 − BASE` there says more about a failed base than about the effect model, and the fold record makes that visible. Every LOCO record self-describes its compliance: `"read_anchor_G_check": False` and `"context_feature_given_to_any_model": False`.

Sources: [loco.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/loco.py#L80-L107)

## Separating Size from Diversity: Row-Budget Matching (Phase 8)

`matched.py` holds one growth factor fixed at a time. **8B, row-count matched**: every arm trains on exactly `N` rows, where `N` is the largest budget every comparable arm can meet — the smallest single-context usable training pool in the fold, computed from row counts alone (`row_budget()`), never from a model result. A one-context arm takes all `N` from one atlas; a two-context arm takes `N/2` per context; a three-context arm `N/3` per context — so anything that differs between arms is context mix, not size. **8C, unique-candidate matched**: rows are restricted to identities every training context measured, giving three readings — one context at `M` rows, the same identities spread across three contexts at `M` rows (the sharp arm: same identities, same rows, only context mix moves), and all three contexts at `3M` rows. Both phases run the five pre-registered `MATCH_SEEDS`; the seed count is never raised after seeing a result.

| Arm | Rows | Context mix | What a win over single-context means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 context | N | 1 context | Baseline |
| 2 contexts | N (N/2 each) | 2 contexts | Diversity at fixed size |
| 3 contexts | N (N/3 each) | 3 contexts | Diversity at fixed size |
| 3 contexts | 3M (all rows) | 3 contexts | Natural growth (size + diversity together) |

Phase 9 (`scaling.py`) then fits `Gain = α + β_N·log N_rows + β_C·N_contexts` descriptively: the *full* fit (natural arms only, `β_C` unidentified), the *matched* fit (rows constant by construction, `β_C` is the whole answer), and a *pooled* fit with per-held-context intercepts. Ordinary-least-squares errors are reported as descriptive spread only — points within a fold share a held context and pool, so the claims rest on the paired bootstraps of the producing phases, not these errors.

Sources: [matched.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/matched.py#L1-L23), [matched.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/matched.py#L51-L78), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L117-L126), [scaling.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/scaling.py#L1-L24)

## The V2 Context-Residual Contract

The context representation itself is pre-registered in the contract before the first V2 number: `CONTEXT_DIM = 32` (no dimension search), `CONTEXT_BASIS_SEED`, `INTERACTION_RANK = 32`, and a ridge penalty grid `CONTEXT_PENALTIES = (1e1 … 1e7)` selected by leave-one-training-context-out validation *inside* the three training contexts only. The rank is not tuned — the modulation is a Hadamard product of two projections, so interaction features equal the rank, and since `v_x = B·h_x` has at most `CONTEXT_DIM` degrees of freedom, setting rank = dimension is the largest value the architecture can use, not a chosen one. The penalty grid's top end is documented to leave V1 inside the selectable model class (modulation effectively switched off), and `V2_IS_RESIDUAL = True` records the degeneracy guarantee: if context carries nothing, the weight goes to zero and V2 becomes V1 by construction.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L128-L155)

The math is a single fitted object on top of a frozen recipe:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    X0["source states x₀<br/>(training contexts ONLY)"] -->|sketched SVD, dim 32| P["P_ctx basis"]
    Q["held/query source state"] --> P
    P --> H["h_x (32-d)"]
    Z["z_c = V1 prediction<br/>(frozen recipe)"] --> A["A: pool SVD, rank 32"]
    A --> U["u_c"]
    U --> M["m = u_c ⊙ h_x"]
    H --> M
    M --> WM["W_m — the ONLY fitted object<br/>(ridge, LOTCO penalty)"]
    WM --> SUM["z_c + W_m·m"]
    SUM --> BR["B_r response basis"] --> R["r̂ predicted effect"]
```

Everything except `W_m` is fixed before it is fitted — `P_ctx` is the training-context source-state SVD at dimension 32 (`context_basis()`, fitted on source states only, no perturbed cell entering it), `A` is the training-pool SVD of `z_c` at rank 32, and the V1 branch is the frozen recipe. A headroom gate additionally requires the residual to be both non-trivial in variance share and reproducible across the two independent measurement views before V2 is built at all. The implementation never materializes the naive `queries × candidates × genes` tensor: with `g_k = B_r·W_m[k]` fixed gene-space directions, the needed inner products and norms expand into small matrix products over the interaction rank, and `test_protocol` checks the expansion against a brute-force evaluation.

Sources: [v2.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/v2.py#L1-L32), [v2.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/v2.py#L54-L70), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L157-L161)

> [!TIP]
> The `WeightedRidgePath` used to fit V1 on pooled pools keeps the frozen penalty grid meaningful: its row scaling uses weights whose *mean* is one (not weights summing to one), so equal weights reduce exactly to the frozen `RidgePath` — dividing by the sum instead would multiply the effective penalty by row count and quietly turn every pooled fit into a different model than the one the programme claims to reuse. The test suite asserts that equivalence rather than assuming it.

Sources: [predictors.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/predictors.py#L26-L63)

## The Deployment Firewall

The contract ends with a hard input firewall, stated as tuples rather than prose: a deployed caller may supply **candidate static knowledge** and a **source or control state** — nothing else. `FORBIDDEN_INPUTS` names what must never reach a predictor: the candidate's perturbed state, the target perturbation outcome, or any held-context candidate response. And `ANCHOR_G_CHECK_IS_SEALED = True` makes the sealed zone explicit at the contract level, matching the loader-level `RuntimeError` in `load_anchor()` and the `G_check` row-drop enforced in every fold. This is the structural complement to the identity-level cross-validation described in [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation).

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contract.py#L163-L170), [contexts.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/contexts.py#L104-L110)

## Verification, Documentation Regeneration, and Self-Testing

The contract closes its own loop in three ways. First, every context is independently verified under the frozen `RESPONSE_ASSET_VERIFIER_CONTRACT_V1_FLOAT32_STORAGE_AWARE` with no per-context tolerance, and each run carries a deliberately corrupted asset witness — a run whose witness does not FAIL is itself a failure. Second, `dataset_doc.py` regenerates the four-context dataset audit document entirely from the JSON artifacts on disk (provenance table with SHA-256s, per-context verdicts, the measurement contract as built), so the document cannot drift from the run that produced it — the same artifact-first philosophy documented in [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests). Third, `selftest_phases.py` runs Phases 8–17 end-to-end on synthetic contexts with planted answers (V1 must beat random; a known variance-share residual must be recovered), so long phases are never executed for the first time on real data where a shape error costs hours and looks like a result that failed to appear. To reproduce the pipeline end-to-end, follow the frozen-snapshot verification and training steps in [Reproducing Paper Results](4-reproducing-paper-results) before loading any context.

Sources: [dataset_doc.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/dataset_doc.py#L1-L20), [dataset_doc.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/dataset_doc.py#L72-L80), [selftest_phases.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/selftest_phases.py#L1-L13), [REPRODUCE.md](REPRODUCE.md#L1-L47)

## Where This Fits in the Catalog

The four-context contracts are the substrate the surrounding experiments stand on. The graded per-query quantities (`cross_view_utility`, MBRU deltas) consumed by the folds come from the evaluation framework in [Ranking Metrics: BU@B, MU@B, PHR@B](8-ranking-metrics-buatb-muatb-phratb) and the protocol in [Held-Out Context Evaluation Protocol](9-held-out-context-evaluation-protocol); the V1 recipe the folds reuse unchanged is detailed in [Response Basis Construction](11-response-basis-construction) and [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor); and the downstream consumers of these contracts are covered in [Response Masking and Open-Vocabulary Analyses](18-response-masking-and-open-vocabulary-analyses) and [External Baselines: GEARS, CellNavi, PHR](19-external-baselines-gears-cellnavi-phr). For the head-to-head comparison this contract enables, continue to [Key Benchmark Findings](26-key-benchmark-findings).


# Response Masking and Open-Vocabulary Analyses



This page documents `open_vocab_generalization_v1`, the module that measures how far historical response measurements reach: does knowing a candidate's measured responses improve budgeted intervention design when that candidate's responses have never been measured? The module is a pre-registered, multi-phase analysis program — a frozen contract, a natural-experiment audit, a controlled masking experiment, a pool-size confound curve, a deployment mixture study, and an independent verifier — all judged on budgeted design utility (BU@B/MU@B-family quantities) and never on response reconstruction accuracy. It sits in the *Experiments and Baselines* section, directly downstream of the four-context data contracts and upstream of the external-baseline comparisons.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L1-L85), [PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md](PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md#L11), [__init__.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/__init__.py#L1-L2)

## The Question, the Factorial, and the Pre-Registered Contract

The motivating evidence is a natural experiment from the held-out-context programme: on the K562 fold, the effect branch delivered `delta MBRU = −0.0103` on the 6,255 training-atlas-unseen candidates but `+0.0095` on the same fold's 1,570 seen candidates. Because library membership — not assignment — determined which candidates were unseen, candidate novelty is entangled with context novelty, and two incompatible hypotheses survive: **H1** says unseen candidates fail because their static knowledge is poorly supported; **H2** says static knowledge cannot extrapolate effects to a response-unsupervised intervention at any support level. `contract.py` exists to separate them, and it is frozen *before any support number or masked result exists*.

The design is a factorial over two axes, never added together: the **context axis** (C: has the predictor seen the evaluated context's responses?) crossed with the **candidate axis** (G: has it seen this candidate's responses anywhere?).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["Primary quantity:<br/>ΔMBRU(effect − base)<br/>budgeted utility, never reconstruction"]
    subgraph F["The 2 × 2 generalization factorial"]
        direction TB
        R11["C_seen × G_seen<br/>interpolation reference"]
        R12["C_seen × G_unseen<br/>pure candidate transfer"]
        R21["C_unseen × G_seen<br/>pure context transfer<br/>(established by the held-out protocol)"]
        R22["C_unseen × G_unseen<br/>joint open-vocabulary transfer"]
    end
    Q --> F
```

The contract also records, rather than fixes, two inherited defects so they cannot silently distort conclusions: `predictors._cross_validate` folds by row index, making penalty selection in a pooled atlas mildly optimistic (identical across arms, and irrelevant in the G-unseen arm where masked identities are absent entirely); and the frozen `cluster_bootstrap` resamples the two batch-disjoint query views as if they were independent clusters. Everything else — the frozen CLEAN_BASE scorer, the CED architecture, the basis rank, the ridge penalty grid, the fusion weight, the utility definition and the budget set {10, 20, 50} — is explicitly *not re-opened*: this mission adds no model, it measures a capability boundary of the model that already exists.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L1-L85), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L200-L240)

## Module Architecture

The module is a pipeline of sibling scripts sharing one contract and one support library, importing the frozen four-context harness, evaluator, and ridge fitter:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C["contract.py<br/>pre-registration constants, regimes,<br/>calipers, verdicts"] -.-> A & B & M
    S["support.py<br/>SupportTable: leverage, d10,<br/>coverage, STRING neighbourhood"] -.-> A & B
    A["natural.py — Phase A<br/>natural unseen audit (K562 only)"] --> PS["poolsize.py<br/>ΔMBRU vs pool size curve,<br/>noise probes"]
    B["masking.py — Phase B<br/>controlled candidate masking,<br/>all four contexts"] --> LS["leverage_sensitivity.py<br/>terciles under restricted leverage"]
    B --> M["mixture.py — Phase C<br/>deployment mixture shares,<br/>entrant value, harm test"]
    B --> V["verify_masking.py<br/>independent witness"]
    subgraph FC["four_context_v1 (frozen)"]
        H["harness: packs"]
        P["predictors: ridge fit"]
        E["evaluate: arms, fuse, paired"]
    end
    A & B & PS --> FC
```

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `contract.py` | Pre-registration: regimes, support diagnostics, masking folds, calipers, verdicts — all frozen before any result |
| `support.py` | `SupportTable`: deployment-time support diagnostics computed from static features + atlas membership only |
| `natural.py` | Phase A: explain the natural unseen failure on K562; stratification, matching, controls |
| `masking.py` | Phase B: controlled candidate masking; cross-context (primary) and within-context (reference) designs |
| `mixture.py` | Phase C: nested unseen-share deployment mixtures; entrant value; support-predicts-harm test |
| `poolsize.py` | ΔMBRU as a function of candidate-pool size, with a noise-injection mechanism probe |
| `leverage_sensitivity.py` | Re-runs Phase B terciles with degenerate leverage columns removed |
| `verify_masking.py` | Independent re-derivation of the masking run's claims; FAIL-not-raise verdicts |

Sources: [PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md](PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md#L11), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L196-L215), [mixture.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/mixture.py#L110-L200)

## Deployment-Time Support Diagnostics (`support.py`)

Every diagnostic is a function of the candidate's **static** features and of which identities the training atlas measured — no response, score, or result is ever read, so all of them are usable at deployment time for a gene nobody has perturbed. None is a model input; they only describe and stratify. The **primary** diagnostic is the ridge's own extrapolation statement, leverage:

$$L_c = k_c^T (X^T X + \lambda I)^{-1} k_c$$

with X the standardized training matrix and λ the penalty the fit actually selected. It is computed from the SVD stored on the fitted path, and the null-space remainder term is kept explicitly: with 1,538 features (512 STRING + 1,024 MAP-KG + 2 modality flags) and fewer training rows than features, the unspanned part is the dominant term, and dropping it would make every candidate look equally well supported.

| Diagnostic | Definition | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `leverage` / `leverage_percentile` | Ridge leverage above, in the ridge's own standardization | Primary support axis; stratification and matching |
| `d10` (+ `d1`, `d50`, `mapkg_d10`) | Mean Euclidean distance to the 10 nearest *unique* training identities in the frozen feature space | Secondary; k ∈ {1, 50} reported as sensitivity, never substituted |
| `coverage` | `BOTH / STRING_ONLY / MAPKG_ONLY / NEITHER` from the two modality flags | Matched **exactly** in support matching |
| `string_degree`, `training_neighbours`, `training_neighbour_weight` | STRING graph degree and how much of it lands inside the training atlas | Descriptive; degree is diagnostic-only, never a model feature |

Two implementation subtleties matter. `_sorted_distances` excludes each candidate's own training row: a static feature vector is a pure function of the gene symbol, so an atlas-measured candidate sits at distance exactly zero from itself, and leaving that in would give every seen candidate a free "well supported" score precisely on the axis being compared. And `neighbourhood` deduplicates training rows to unique identities, so a candidate measured in three contexts cannot inflate its neighbours' support by counting three times.

Sources: [support.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/support.py#L1-L19), [support.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/support.py#L100-L127), [support.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/support.py#L155-L172), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L98-L135)

## Phase A: The Natural Unseen Audit (`natural.py`)

Phase A is deliberately restricted to the **K562 fold** — the only one whose unseen pool is not degenerate (6,255 candidates against a largest budget of 50; the other folds hold 25, 73, and 105) — and trains no new model. It refits the same three-context pooled V1 predictor under the same recipe and seeds, and its first output is a **reproduction check**: does the refit reproduce the C-014 delta MBRU it is trying to explain? Only then does it stratify. The unseen pool is split into five equal-count quintiles of ascending leverage (`Q1_best_supported` … `Q5_weakest_supported`) via `quantile_strata`, which splits by rank so per-stratum results are never statements about how many candidates fell in a value band.

Seen candidates are then matched to unseen ones **one-to-one without replacement**: coverage pattern matched exactly, leverage and d10 percentiles matched within a caliper of 0.05 on each axis (a box covering ~1% of the joint support space; 0.02 is a sensitivity only), greedy in ascending joint pair distance. Both matched pools end exactly the same size, so absolute MBRU is comparable.

> [!TIP]
> Phase A round 1 produced a decomposition that did not behave like a decomposition — every leverage stratum was 3–7× more negative than the pool it partitions, and the support-matched unseen pool came out positive while its source pool was negative. The fix was not a new metric but a **size-matched null**: random equal-size strata over the same pool (seeds `20260918–20`), and twelve seeds for the matched-size null because three seeds gave a null spanning 0.030 — wider than the 0.027 effect it was meant to bound. Controls are sized by their resolution, not by convention.

Because the frozen standardization clips a feature's scale at 1e-8, columns the training rows never vary acquire enormous standardized coordinates — and enormous leverage. Phase A therefore also recomputes leverage from scratch (`leverage_from_matrix`, a **second independent implementation**, so agreement is evidence rather than tautology) with those degenerate columns dropped, and reports the Spearman correlation between primary and restricted leverage beside the unchanged primary stratification.

Sources: [natural.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/natural.py#L1-L16), [natural.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/natural.py#L47-L88), [natural.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/natural.py#L90-L110), [natural.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/natural.py#L200-L372)

## Phase B: Controlled Candidate Masking (`masking.py`)

Phase B *manufactures* the response-unseen condition instead of inheriting it. The candidate identity, its static knowledge, the evaluation pool, the queries, the base ranker and the graded utility are all held fixed; the single thing that varies is whether that identity's measured responses were available to fit the effect predictor. Masking folds come from `fold_assignment`: `sha256("VCDESIGN_OPEN_VOCAB_CANDIDATE_MASK_V1:{symbol}")` mod 5 — deterministic, outcome-independent, and stable across contexts, so the same identity is masked in the same fold everywhere it appears. Removal is **by identity in every named training context at once**, and the response basis and ridge are rebuilt inside each masked pool — reusing the seen arm's basis would leak the masked responses through the very object the protocol says must be rebuilt.

| Property | `cross_context` (primary) | `within_context` (reference) |
|---|---|---|
| Training atlas | The other three contexts | The same single context |
| SEEN arm fits on the graded candidate's own response? | No | Yes |
| `SEEN − MASKED` reads as | Clean exposure effect | **Upper bound**; leverage interaction mechanically confounded |
| Role | Pre-registered estimate of record | Reported with caveat only |

RPE1, HepG2 and Jurkat are primary masking contexts (pools of 254/152/290 at `MASK_FOLDS = 5`, all clearing the floor of 200 = 4× the largest budget); K562 is **secondary** because the frozen base ranker was trained on K562 responses, so a masked K562 candidate can retain exposure through the base even after the effect branch loses it. HepG2, below the floor, is diagnostic-only in the per-fold contrast but still enters the pooled cross-fitted contrast (pool 764).

Three effect arms, not two — this is the design's core:

| Arm | Effect source | What it isolates |
|---|---|---|
| `EFFECT_SEEN` | Full three-context predictor | The deployed model |
| `EFFECT_MASKED` | Crossfit of the five fold predictors (offset 0) | Candidate-specific exposure loss |
| `EFFECT_SIZE_CONTROL` | Crossfit of the same five predictors (offset +1) | Removing one fold's rows *only* |

> [!TIP]
> The size control costs **zero extra fits**: "fold M is size controlled by the predictor that masked fold (M + 1) mod 5." Removing a candidate's rows also removes *rows*, and atlas size is the primary driver of distillation quality (established in C-013), so `SEEN − MASKED` alone cannot separate "this candidate was never measured" from "the atlas is a fifth smaller." The primary exposure quantity is therefore `exposure_value_size_controlled = SIZE_CONTROL − MASKED`, with `exposure = SEEN − MASKED` as the upper bound and `atlas_shrinkage_cost = SEEN − SIZE_CONTROL` as the decomposition's second half.

Because the crossfit mixes five independently fitted predictors into one score matrix, a **homogeneity gate** guards the secondary contrast: minimum pairwise cosine between intercept reconstructions ≥ 0.99 (the direction test alone cannot fail), identical selected penalties, and a candidate-specific-share ratio ≤ 1.05. The primary contrast is immune by construction — both arms mix the *same* five predictors permuted by one fold, so any mixing distortion cancels. Non-eligible candidates keep the seen arm's effect in every arm, so the frozen fusion's full-pool standardization cannot turn exposure into a fusion-weight artifact.

> [!TIP]
> Every headline interval is computed twice. The frozen `cluster_bootstrap` resamples the length-2Q concatenated vector entry-by-entry, treating the two views of one query as independent clusters — narrower intervals than its own docstring's cluster unit implies, for C-013 and C-014 alike. Changing it would break comparability, so `query_cluster_bootstrap` (10,000 replicates, seed 20260916) resamples **query identities** carrying both views together, and is reported *beside* the frozen interval so a reader can see whether any conclusion depends on it.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    H["fold_assignment<br/>sha256(symbol) → 5 folds"] --> F0 & F1 & F2 & F3 & F4
    S["Seen predictor<br/>full 3-context atlas"] --> SEEN["EFFECT_SEEN"]
    F0["fold predictor 0<br/>basis + ridge rebuilt"] --> MASKED["EFFECT_MASKED<br/>crossfit offset 0"]
    F1 & F2 & F3 & F4 --> MASKED
    F0 & F1 & F2 & F3 & F4 -->|"offset +1"| SC["EFFECT_SIZE_CONTROL"]
    SEEN & MASKED & SC --> G["Homogeneity gate:<br/>cos ≥ 0.99 · penalties equal · share ratio ≤ 1.05"]
    G --> K["exposure = SEEN − MASKED<br/>primary: SIZE_CTL − MASKED<br/>shrinkage = SEEN − SIZE_CTL"]
    K --> B["query-identity bootstrap<br/>beside frozen interval"]
```

Sources: [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L1-L29), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L50-L85), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L254-L296), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L299-L390), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L439-L478), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L140-L199)

## The Pool-Size Confound (`poolsize.py`)

Added on 2026-09-18, after Phase A's size-matched null exposed something larger: **random** subsets of the 6,255 unseen candidates give a *positive* delta MBRU at stratum size 1,251 while the whole pool gives a negative one — same candidates, same predictor, same queries; only how many candidates each query ranks changed. Mechanically, the first B slots of a larger pool are filled by the largest order statistics of the score, so a score with systematic error pushes more of that error into a fixed budget as the pool grows. That makes the C-014-style 1,570-vs-6,255 contrast uncontrolled unless the curve is flat.

The script measures delta MBRU against pool size (250, 500, 1,000, 1,570, 3,000, 6,255; three seeds) separately inside the seen pool, the unseen pool, and the full pool, plus a **mechanism probe**: a deliberately degraded score entering the fusion exactly where the effect branch does — `row_z(base) + λ · row_z(noise)` at λ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}, weights fixed before the run — should trace the same shape if the mechanism is real. Only the shape is read, never the level (D-005 stands: random is never the comparison of record). A `--standardize` flag separates `pool` fusion (each branch standardized over the whole fold, as published) from `subset` fusion (re-standardized per subsample), isolating whether the curve depends on the standardization population.

Sources: [poolsize.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/poolsize.py#L1-L37), [poolsize.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/poolsize.py#L43-L58), [poolsize.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/poolsize.py#L74-L180)

## Phase C: The Deployment Mixture and Support-Predicts-Harm (`mixture.py`)

A real vocabulary is neither all measured nor all unmeasured. Phase C holds the candidate pool, queries, base and graded utility fixed and varies only *which* candidates take their predicted effect from the predictor that masked them, at nested unseen shares of 25%, 50% and 75%. Nesting comes from a per-identity hash value in [0, 1): whatever is unseen at 0.25 is unseen at 0.50 and 0.75, so differences between shares are about how much unseen material the pool holds, not about which candidates happened to be drawn.

The evaluated arms are `BASE`, `ALL_SEEN`, `ALL_UNSEEN`, and `MIXED` (per-candidate seen/masked effects fused over the full pool, then restricted — matching the fusion convention of Phases A and B so one arm never reports two numbers). Composition diagnostics report what fraction of the first B slots and how much of their utility each group contributes — `seen`, `unseen`, and `unseen_{high,medium,low}_support` terciles. The unit of value is deliberately not the promoted candidate's own utility but its **entrant value**: for a candidate entering the top-B under the fused score but not under the base alone, `utility(q, c)` minus the mean utility of the candidates it displaced — what the effect branch *actually bought* by the swap.

Section 21 asks one question and builds nothing: does support predict the sign of what the effect branch buys? The primary statistic is `spearman(leverage_percentile, mean_entrant_value)` at share 0.50. **No support-aware gate is implemented in this mission under any name** — the module only measures whether support predicts harm; gate design would be a new mission with its own pre-registration.

Sources: [mixture.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/mixture.py#L1-L20), [mixture.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/mixture.py#L28-L92), [mixture.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/mixture.py#L110-L200), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L200-L219)

## Sensitivity and the Independent Witness

`leverage_sensitivity.py` answers a targeted question: do Phase B's support terciles survive the leverage diagnostic's degenerate-column defect? It recomputes terciles with the 1e-8-clip columns removed and re-evaluates using the effect cosines the masking run **cached** (`support_{held}.npz`, `effect_cosine_{held}.npz`), refitting nothing, so the arms are numerically the ones Phase B produced. It is a sensitivity, not a replacement — the pre-registered primary stays as registered.

`verify_masking.py` implements the programme's Lesson L3: *a script must not be its own only witness*. From the cached packs and frozen assets alone, with its own code rather than the run's, it re-derives the masking folds from the symbols, rebuilds one context's masked training pool with a different loop, refits the named predictor and checks the recorded penalty and held-out cosine (tolerance 1e-12), and re-ranks both arms with an ordering that breaks ties **differently on purpose** — agreement proves the result does not rest on a tie convention, and disagreement is reported as the tie rate. It refuses to overwrite its own output and downgrades to FAIL rather than raising, so a failure is a recorded verdict, not a missing file.

Sources: [leverage_sensitivity.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/leverage_sensitivity.py#L1-L14), [leverage_sensitivity.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/leverage_sensitivity.py#L18-L105), [verify_masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/verify_masking.py#L1-L16), [verify_masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/verify_masking.py#L40-L76)

## Allowed Verdicts and the Frozen Boundary

The contract enumerates exactly four verdicts this mission may reach — everything else is out of scope by construction:

| Verdict token | Reading |
|---|---|
| `STATIC_KNOWLEDGE_SUPPORT_LIMITED` | H1: unseen candidates fail because static support is poor |
| `MEASURED_CANDIDATE_COVERAGE_LIMITED` | H2: exposure to measured responses is the binding constraint |
| `SUPPORT_DEPENDENT_OPEN_VOCABULARY` | The effect branch's value for unseen candidates varies with support |
| `OPEN_VOCABULARY_FAILURE_UNRESOLVED` | Neither axis explains the deficit |

The frozen boundary is explicit: K562 CLEAN_BASE, the CED architecture, the ridge penalty recipe, the fusion weight, the utility definition and more are not re-opened; STRING adjacency is read for degree and neighbour counts as diagnostics only and is never given to a model as a feature; and no uncertainty model or OOD detector is trained anywhere in this mission.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L221-L240)

## Running the Analyses

All scripts are module invocations taking explicit `--packs` (the four-context processed packs) and a new `--output` path; the complete command sequence for a full reproduction lives in [REPRODUCE.md](REPRODUCE.md).

| Script | Command | Distinguishing flags | Consumes / emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase A | `python3 -m gene_open_inverse.open_vocab_generalization_v1.natural` | `--string-adjacency` | Emits the audit JSON + `k562_support_table.npz` |
| Phase B | `python3 -m gene_open_inverse.open_vocab_generalization_v1.masking` | `--string-adjacency` | Emits masking JSON + `support_{ctx}.npz`, `effect_cosine_{ctx}.npz` |
| Pool-size curve | `python3 -m gene_open_inverse.open_vocab_generalization_v1.poolsize` | `--standardize {pool,subset}` | Emits the curve JSON |
| Phase C | `python3 -m gene_open_inverse.open_vocab_generalization_v1.mixture` | (driver reads the masking record) | Consumes `effect_cosine_{ctx}.npz` caches |
| Leverage sensitivity | `python3 -m gene_open_inverse.open_vocab_generalization_v1.leverage_sensitivity` | `--record <masking JSON>` | Consumes masking record + cached cosines |
| Verification | `python3 -m gene_open_inverse.open_vocab_generalization_v1.verify_masking` | `--record`, `--context`, `--fold`, `--tolerance` | Emits PASS/FAIL JSON; refuses overwrite |
