Run order matters: Phase B's artifacts feed Phase C and the sensitivity; the verification run needs Phase B's record. Every long-running stage should write to an explicit new output path.

Sources: [natural.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/natural.py#L375-L399), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L481-L540), [leverage_sensitivity.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/leverage_sensitivity.py#L107-L124), [poolsize.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/poolsize.py#L182-L213), [PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md](PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md#L24-L30)

## Reading Path

This page assumes the metric vocabulary of [Ranking Metrics: BU@B, MU@B, PHR@B](8-ranking-metrics-buatb-muatb-phratb) and the arm-grading machinery of [Held-Out Context Evaluation Protocol](9-held-out-context-evaluation-protocol); the ridge and basis being masked are defined in [Response Basis Construction](11-response-basis-construction) and [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor), and the feature layout behind the support diagnostics in [Knowledge Features: STRING and MAP-KG](13-knowledge-features-string-and-map-kg). For what precedes these analyses, read [Four-Context Data Contracts](17-four-context-data-contracts); for how the same evaluators compare against comparator methods, continue to [External Baselines: GEARS, CellNavi, PHR](19-external-baselines-gears-cellnavi-phr) and [Utility Ground Truth Validation](20-utility-ground-truth-validation). The cross-validation and bootstrap defects recorded here are part of the broader integrity story in [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation) and [Post-Review Corrections](22-post-review-corrections).

# External Baselines: GEARS, CellNavi, PHR



This page documents `src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/`, the module that adapts published methods — GEARS, CellNavi, and the PHR@B realized-value machinery — into a single frozen evaluation closure named `EXTERNAL_BASELINE_AND_EVALUATION_CLOSURE_V1`. The design goal is strict comparability: every method, whether a third-party model or an internal reference arm, is graded on the same queries, the same candidate stratum, the same utilities, budgets, tie rule, and bootstrap, with all protocol constants fixed in one machine-readable contract before any outcome is observed.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L1-L20), [scores.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/scores.py#L1-L6)

## The Frozen Contract: Arms, Taxonomy, and Legality

The contract declares the experimental frame once: three primary held-out contexts (`RPE1`, `HepG2`, `Jurkat`), four training contexts (`K562` plus the three primary), two regimes (`SEEN` and `MASKED` over 5 cross-validation folds), budgets `(10, 20, 50)` with `BU@20` as the primary metric, and a single global seed `20260919`. Frozen run directories (`C018_RUN`, `EVIDENCE_RUN`, `FOUR_CONTEXT_RUN`) are the only inputs, and paths are recorded in every output for provenance.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L8-L20), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L66-L76)

Eleven arms are organized into a lettered taxonomy (`A. random` through `F. analysis-only oracle`) plus three companions, each with an explicit legality statement — the protocol's answer to "what information was this arm allowed to see?" GEARS and the internal forward arms are *strict legal in both regimes* (no masked identity's response enters their fit), while CellNavi variants are *MEASURED-CANDIDATE inverse baselines* that require a candidate's measured cells in some training context and therefore run `SEEN` only. The oracle reads held-context responses and is marked `DIAGNOSTIC_ORACLE_NOT_DEPLOYABLE`.

| Arm constant | Label | Taxonomy | Legality | Regimes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RANDOM` | Random | A. random | no information | both |
| `GOAL_BLIND_PRIOR` | Goal-blind prior (‖raw CED‖) | B. goal-blind candidate prior | strict legal, goal blind | both |
| `BASE` | Direct inverse | C (and E. VCDesign base) | strict legal | both |
| `CELLNAVI_DESIGN_COMPATIBLE` | CellNavi, official recipe | C. direct inverse, published | measured-candidate inverse; SEEN only | SEEN |
| `CELLNAVI_NATIVE_SCALE` | CellNavi at native class scale | C, published (Deviation 5) | same legality as CellNavi | SEEN |
| `GEARS_FORWARD_ENUMERATE` | GEARS | D. forward-enumerate-retrieve, published | strict legal in both regimes | both |
| `INTERNAL_FORWARD_THEN_MATCH` | RIDGE_UNIT effect-only cosine | D. internal reference | strict legal | both |
| `VCDESIGN_BASE_PLUS_RIDGE_UNIT` | VCDesign | E. VCDesign | strict legal | both |
| `MEASURED_RESPONSE_ORACLE` | Measured-response oracle | F. analysis-only | diagnostic, not deployable | both |
| `RIDGE_UNIT_K562_ATLAS` | RIDGE_UNIT on K562 atlas | companion (GEARS-matched) | strict legal | both |
| `PROFILED_SIGNATURE_RETRIEVAL` | Library retrieval on training signatures | companion | SEEN-only library retrieval | SEEN |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L22-L64)

## Adapter Architecture: Isolated Environments, One Score Matrix

The module follows an *interface adapter* pattern with strict environment isolation. The two third-party models each run in their own pinned environment — GEARS via `cell-gears==0.1.2` in a `pertbench` env, CellNavi at upstream commit `ea1660fc3057c63ecd849d506f24241bdc4b3f33` in a `cellnavi` env — while data preparation, scoring, and grading all run in the shared project environment. The adapters emit only neutral artifacts (`effects.npz` of predicted shifts for GEARS, `scores.npz` of class log-probabilities for CellNavi); `scores.py` then converts those artifacts into canonical `[queries × pool]` float64 matrices per view, which `evaluate.py` grades without ever re-running a model.

To read the diagram: the left column builds inputs in the project environment from the frozen single-cell sources; the middle column is the two upstream-model environments; the right column is the closure's grading stack that all arms flow into.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph shared["Project environment — shared cell access"]
        CELLS["cells.py<br/>SHA-256 hashed, label-driven cell selection"]
        GDATA["gears_data.py<br/>K562 G_fit AnnData"]
        NDATA["cellnavi_data.py<br/>train.h5ad + query.h5ad per held context"]
        CELLS --> GDATA
        CELLS --> NDATA
    end
    subgraph pertbench["pertbench env"]
        GFIT["gears_fit.py<br/>process / fit / repro"]
    end
    subgraph cellnavi["cellnavi env"]
        NFIT["cellnavi_fit.py<br/>repro / train / infer"]
    end
    GDATA --> GFIT
    NDATA --> NFIT
    subgraph closure["Project environment — grading"]
        SCORES["scores.py<br/>canonical score matrices"]
        RK["ridge_k562.py<br/>information-matched RIDGE_UNIT twin"]
        PHRM["phr.py<br/>quarter gate + realized J"]
        EVAL["evaluate.py<br/>unified contract V1"]
        TAB["tables.py<br/>paper-ready TSVs"]
    end
    GFIT -- "effects.npz (predicted shifts)" --> SCORES
    NFIT -- "scores.npz (mean log_softmax)" --> SCORES
    RK --> SCORES
    SCORES --> EVAL
    PHRM --> EVAL
    EVAL --> TAB
```

Sources: [gears_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/gears_fit.py#L1-L12), [cellnavi_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/cellnavi_fit.py#L1-L11), [scores.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/scores.py#L1-L6), [ridge_k562.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/ridge_k562.py#L1-L6)

| File | Environment | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `cells.py` | project | deterministic hashed cell selection over backed h5ad sources; reads only chosen rows' expression |
| `gears_data.py` / `gears_fit.py` | project / `pertbench` | GEARS training AnnData builder / official-package fit and tutorial reproduction |
| `cellnavi_data.py` / `cellnavi_fit.py` | project / `cellnavi` | CellNavi train/query files / official-code reproduction, fine-tune, inference |
| `ridge_k562.py` | project | RIDGE_UNIT A1 recipe on the K562-only atlas under GEARS's masks |
| `scores.py` | project | merges all arms into self-sufficient score files |
| `phr.py` | project | PHR reconstruction gate and realized `J` matrices |
| `evaluate.py` / `tables.py` | project | unified grading with gates and contrasts / TSV emission |

Sources: [cells.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/cells.py#L1-L6), [tables.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/tables.py#L1-L3)

## GEARS: Forward-Enumerate-Retrieve on the K562 Atlas

GEARS is treated as a *forward predictor*: it is trained once on K562 `G_fit` single cells to predict perturbation responses, and its predicted shift `x_hat_c − x_s` is converted into ranking scores through the same effect-cosine used by internal arms. The data builder keeps only anchor `G_fit` identities that lie in GEARS's own default perturbation graph (`gene2go_all` restricted to its essential-gene list), caps each identity at 16 hashed-selected cells (Deviation 1, a compute-side choice made before any GEARS prediction), adds 4,096 hashed control cells, and writes log1p(CP10k) expression restricted to the frozen four-context gene axis `G_4`. Crucially, masking is deferred to fit time via splits, so this one shared cell pool serves all folds without re-reading expression.

Sources: [gears_data.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/gears_data.py#L1-L9), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L79-L88)

The fit stage uses GEARS's custom-split format: a SHA-256 hashed 10% validation bucket (`bucket 0` of 10 under a dedicated namespace), the rest training, and masked identities nowhere — with a hard `RuntimeError` if a masked identity ever reaches a split. The `MASKED` regime applies `GEARS_MASK_RULE`, the *fold union*: for fold *f*, every C-016-eligible identity of fold *f* across all three held pools is excluded from the K562 training set, so one masked fit serves all three held contexts and each pool's masked set is a verified subset. The adapter also verifies an upstream premise rather than assuming it: because GEARS's model outputs `f(pert) + x`, the predicted shift should be identical for every control cell, and the adapter checks this on 8 hashed control cells at tolerance 1e-4 before saving `effects.npz`.

Sources: [gears_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/gears_fit.py#L66-L96), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L83-L90), [gears_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/gears_fit.py#L200-L231)

Before any comparison is published, the adapter runs GEARS's official tutorial as a reproduction gate: the Norman dataset, simulation split at seed 1, one epoch, and the gate is the printed `Test Top 20 DE MSE` headline plus the split composition. The frozen verdict is `GEARS_OFFICIAL_REPRODUCTION_FAILED` — headline 0.2456 versus the published 0.2540 and composition 9/43/19/36 versus 9/52/18/37 — so GEARS is placed as a labelled companion outside the main table (Deviation 4). A two-environment shim, `SeriesSafeAnnData`, wraps `adata.X` so GEARS 0.1.2's pandas boolean Series indexing works against the environment's scipy, documented as an environment-only change with no numerical effect.

| Setting | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Package / env | `cell-gears==0.1.2` / `pertbench` | official package, isolated environment |
| Training context | K562 (`G_fit` anchors only) | paired with random controls of its own dataset |
| Cells per identity / controls | 16 (Deviation 1) / 4,096 | hashed selection, deterministic |
| Validation split | SHA-256 bucket 0 of 10 | GEARS's own validation bucket |
| Hyperparameters | hidden 64, epochs 20, lr 1e-3, wd 5e-4, batch 32/128 | official, best-validation epoch kept |
| `MASKED` rule | fold union across three held pools | one fit serves all contexts |
| Prediction check | 8 controls, invariance ≤ 1e-4 | adapter premise verified, not assumed |
| Reproduction gate | norman / simulation / 1 epoch; target Top-20 DE MSE 0.2540 ± 0.05 | verdict: FAILED → companion placement |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L79-L104), [gears_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/gears_fit.py#L116-L163), [gears_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/gears_fit.py#L33-L60)

> [!TIP]
> Because the frozen verdict records that every GEARS fit collapses to one perturbation-independent shift (`GEARS_COLLAPSE_DIAGNOSTIC.json`), its ranking degenerates to the tie rule. When reading results tables, GEARS rows are commented with this verdict in the companion TSVs — the number you see is effectively the tie-breaking behavior, not a discriminating ranking.

## CellNavi: Class-Based Inverse Under the Official Recipe

CellNavi is adapted as a *published inverse baseline*: its classifier, fine-tuned with the official trainer and the official tutorial recipe, scores each candidate identity as a class. The data builder creates per-held-context files in the project environment. The training file holds raw-count cells of every identity the held context's `RIDGE_UNIT` SEEN fit may train on, drawn from the three training contexts only, capped at 32 hashed cells per (context, identity) — no control cells, since CellNavi's released code never reads them. The query file takes up to 16 hashed cells per (query, view) *from that view's batches only*, so a view-v row's CellNavi input comes from the same batches that build its view-v query direction. The gene axis is the released CellNavi graph's genes in its exact column order, filled only where graph genes intersect `G_4`; unmeasured graph genes stay zero and are never tokenized, guaranteeing every arm sees the same measured gene universe.

Sources: [cellnavi_data.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/cellnavi_data.py#L1-L14), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L107-L123)

The fit adapter runs three stages, each with a verifiable gate. `repro` first verifies MD5 hashes of the released pretrain weights and tutorial checkpoint, then evaluates the released step-1000 checkpoint on the released test file: it must reproduce accuracy 0.510, weighted F1 0.498, 3,158 cells, and 70 classes within ±0.005 (three-decimal rounding of the published tutorial output). `train` fine-tunes from `pretrain_weights.pth` with the official distributed trainer; the only code change is widening the class-head MLP (`n_cls` is hard-coded to 2058 upstream) to the number of training classes. `infer` runs the official validation tokenization — no down-sampling, no truncation — over held-context query cells and emits the score contract defines: mean over the query-view cells of `log_softmax(logits)[class of c]`.

Sources: [cellnavi_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/cellnavi_fit.py#L1-L11), [cellnavi_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/cellnavi_fit.py#L114-L170), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L107-L123)

Two interface patches keep the official code intact otherwise. `_patch_io` replaces the graph-distance mask gather: upstream builds each cell's mask as `mtx[u][:, u]` on an int64 11,936 × 11,936 matrix (~195 MB copied per cell, 0.33 s), so an int8 copy gathered with `np.ix_` (identical values, 0.043 s) is substituted after a self-check compares both gathers on a hashed 512-index probe. `_patch_classes` re-wraps only the final linear layer. Additionally, two class rules are frozen for the class head: `all_training` (every trainable identity) and `stratum` — the held context's C-016 SEEN stratum, which is exactly the candidate library the task ranks; the latter defines the `CELLNAVI_NATIVE_SCALE` arm (Deviation 5), kept as a separate variant directory `cellnavi_native` via the `--subdir` flag.

| Setting | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream pin | commit `ea1660fc…` / env `cellnavi` | interface adapter only |
| Released assets | MD5-gated pretrain + tutorial checkpoint | mismatch aborts |
| Reproduction gate | acc 0.510, wF1 0.498, 3,158 cells, 70 classes, ±0.005 | notebook gene-name route |
| Train / query cells | 32 per (context, identity) / 16 per (query, view) | deterministic hashed selection |
| Eval checkpoint | step 1000 | the tutorial's own evaluation point |
| Score | mean `log_softmax` over query-view cells | frozen `CELLNAVI_SCORE` |
| Class rules | `all_training` vs `stratum` | the latter is Deviation 5 (native scale) |
| Code changes | class-head width; int8 `np.ix_` gather (self-checked) | everything else untouched |

Sources: [cellnavi_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/cellnavi_fit.py#L72-L98), [cellnavi_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/cellnavi_fit.py#L209-L242), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L121-L123)

## Information-Matched Companions and Reference Arms

An external baseline is only interpretable against arms that hold information constant. `RIDGE_UNIT_K562_ATLAS` runs the frozen A1 ridge recipe — same modality, rank 256, K562-only atlas — under exactly GEARS's fold-union masks, and its SEEN fit must equal the evidence run's saved K562-only spec to 1e-10 before anything is kept; this isolates "the recipe" from "the atlas + masks". `INTERNAL_FORWARD_THEN_MATCH` (RIDGE_UNIT effect-only cosine, read from C-018's saved arrays) provides the internal forward-then-match reference in taxonomy class D, and `PROFILED_SIGNATURE_RETRIEVAL` builds unit-norm mean consensus-response signatures per candidate across training contexts to emulate CMap-style library retrieval. Floors and ceilings complete the frame: seeded `RANDOM` Gaussian scores, the goal-blind `‖raw CED‖` magnitude prior, and the measured-response oracle.

Sources: [ridge_k562.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/ridge_k562.py#L1-L6), [ridge_k562.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/ridge_k562.py#L36-L44), [scores.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/scores.py#L89-L103), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L22-L33)

> [!TIP]
> Watch the two-tier unscored convention in `scores.py`. Effect-producing arms (GEARS, RIDGE_UNIT twins) follow the contract's `UNSCORED` rule — an unrepresentable candidate gets a zero effect, which the frozen effect cosine scores 0 — while score-producing arms (CellNavi) use `NOT_SCORED = -1.0e300` columns for uncovered candidates. Both cases are recorded in per-arm `covered` masks, and `evaluate.py` additionally re-grades everything on a *common-coverage stratum* so headline contrasts are never silently affected by coverage differences.

## PHR Under the Closure: Quarter Gate and Realized J

Within this closure, PHR@B is realized through `phr.py` on the *four-way sub-pool*: candidates in the C-016 stratum and queries meeting `MIN_VIEW_CELLS` in all four batch quarters. The frozen build computes quarter responses in the same streaming pass that built the two views, so no reprocessing is needed — but the module proves it rather than trusting it. The reconstruction gate checks, per held context, that the cell-count-weighted mean of Q0 and Q1 reproduces view A's responses, Q2 and Q3 reproduce view B's, the pack's responses equal the build's side responses exactly, quarter batches refine the A/B sides, and at least 25 cells exist per quarter, all at tolerance 1e-5 (float32 storage of responses of magnitude ≤ ~4). PHR is computed only when the gate passes; otherwise the frozen sentinel `PHR_UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_PACK_LIMITATION` applies.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Q["Four-way identity<br/>meets MIN_VIEW_CELLS in all 4 quarters"]
    Q --> Q0["Quarter 0"] 
    Q --> Q1["Quarter 1"]
    Q --> Q2["Quarter 2"]
    Q --> Q3["Quarter 3"]
    Q0 --> PA["Side-v pair:<br/>proposer statistics"]
    Q1 --> PA
    Q2 --> GR["Side 1-v pair:<br/>grader statistics"]
    Q3 --> GR
    PA --> DEC["View-v row: action chosen on side v<br/>— the side that also builds its query"]
    GR --> J["Realized J: cross-fitted value<br/>read on the untouched opposite side"]
    DEC --> PHR["PHR@B on the four-way sub-pool"]
    J --> PHR
```

Sources: [phr.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/phr.py#L1-L13), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L71-L76)

`realized_j` then assembles the per-view gain matrix `J` whose rows are four-way queries and columns are four-way stratum candidates. For a view-v row, `act.view_statistics` derives the proposer statistics from side v's quarter pair — the same side that builds the row's query — `act.optimal_attenuation` selects the action, and `act.cross_fitted_value` reads the gain on side 1-v, which nothing in the decision touched. This separation is what makes PHR a *realized* utility rather than a re-derived one, and it plugs directly into `mt.row_metrics` via the `realized_j` argument during grading.

Sources: [phr.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/phr.py#L63-L85), [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/evaluate.py#L120-L137)

For metric definitions of PHR@B itself (and BU@B / MU@B), see [Ranking Metrics: BU@B, MU@B, PHR@B](8-ranking-metrics-buatb-muatb-phratb); the held-out protocol these views implement is described in [Held-Out Context Evaluation Protocol](9-held-out-context-evaluation-protocol). Because the four-way gate requires 25+ cells per quarter, PHR is reported per row on the sub-pool and pooled only when a context has at least `MIN_PHR_POOL = 200` candidates (four times the largest budget), surfaced as `pooled_powered` in the main table.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L66-L76), [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/evaluate.py#L156-L178)

## Unified Grading: Gates, Coverage, Contrasts, Tables

`evaluate.py` grades every arm on identical footing — same queries, same C-016 stratum, same self-exclusion, same utilities, budgets, tie rule, and query-gene cluster bootstrap — and enforces a provenance gate before publishing: VCDesign, BASE, and the internal forward arm must reproduce C-018's saved per-query MBRU vectors *exactly* (max abs difference 0.0), otherwise the run aborts. Beyond headline metrics it computes per-arm coverage within the stratum, a common-coverage re-grading, and candidate-level prediction quality via `specific_cosine` — Evidence E6's measure of predicted-versus-measured response cosine after removing the SPED-fitted common axis — for the predictor arms (internal FTM, GEARS, RIDGE_UNIT K562).

Sources: [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/evaluate.py#L1-L7), [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/evaluate.py#L96-L114), [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/evaluate.py#L54-L63)

The output layer emits paired headline contrasts with cluster-bootstrap CIs and QWR win-rates — including `VCDESIGN_minus_GEARS`, `GEARS_minus_RIDGE_K562` in `MASKED`, and `VCDESIGN_minus_CELLNAVI`, `VCDESIGN_minus_CELLNAVI_NATIVE` in `SEEN` — plus companion contrasts over the companion metrics (`BU@10`, `BU@50`, `MU@20`, `HvHit@20`). `tables.py` converts the JSON result into paper-ready TSVs: main tables exclude GEARS, while companion tables carry the frozen reproduction verdict and placement rationale as an inline comment, so no reader can mistake the degenerate GEARS ranking for a competitive result.

Sources: [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/evaluate.py#L180-L194), [tables.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/tables.py#L10-L18), [tables.py](src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/tables.py#L59-L64)

For how these numbers land in the paper's claims, continue to [Key Benchmark Findings](26-key-benchmark-findings); for how the frozen artifacts are hash-verified end-to-end, see [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests), and for protocol-level deviation accounting see [Post-Review Corrections](22-post-review-corrections).

## Where to Go Next

The baselines consume the frozen pack and stratum machinery built earlier in the book: identity eligibility, folds, and strata come from C-016/C-018 as described in [Four-Context Data Contracts](17-four-context-data-contracts), and the utilities PHR realizes against are validated independently in [Utility Ground Truth Validation](20-utility-ground-truth-validation). A natural reading order from here is [Utility Ground Truth Validation](20-utility-ground-truth-validation) → [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation) → [Key Benchmark Findings](26-key-benchmark-findings), which together explain why the legality column of the arm table is the load-bearing constraint of this entire closure.


# Utility Ground Truth Validation



This page documents `src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/` — the module that decides whether the project's new **latent candidate value** may serve as the utility ground truth. The question is deliberately narrow: not "is this definition better," but "can a candidate ordering produced by one measurement view be trusted when graded by a fully independent view, after the frozen eligibility rule has decided which queries are measurable at all." Nothing in this module trains a model, and nothing reads a model score — the module header states both invariants explicitly, and the run record asserts them as `trained_anything: False` and `read_G_check: False`.

Sources: [\_\_init\_\_.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/__init__.py#L1-L8), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L1-L11), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L226-L233)

## Two-Phase Architecture: Eligibility First, Verdict Second

The module splits its work into two frozen phases. **Phase 1** freezes which queries are measurable at all using a statistical rule fixed before any downstream score exists. **Phase 2** asks the only question that can promote the new value definition to ground truth: does a budget prefix ranked by one measurement view keep its experimental utility when graded by a fully independent view — computed identically for the latent value and for the incumbent cosine, on the same queries, candidates and cells.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["quarter_responses.npy<br/>(4 measurement views)"] --> B["Phase 1: cross-view Gram<br/>E_q = &lt;d_A^q, d_B^q&gt;"]
    B --> C["Permutation p-value<br/>vs. mismatched partners"]
    C --> D["BH-FDR at 0.05<br/>+ positive-energy gate"]
    D --> E["Eligibility mask<br/>(applied to both roles: G_fit, G_select)"]
    E --> F["Phase 2: two estimators"]
    F --> G["latent_value (Q0,Q1) ↔ (Q2,Q3)"]
    F --> H["incumbent_cosine (side A) ↔ (side B)"]
    G --> I["rank by view X,<br/>grade by view Y"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["MBRU / nRU@B<br/>paired difference +<br/>identity-cluster bootstrap"]
    J --> K["utility_gt_v2_phase12.json<br/>+ per-query .npy artifacts"]
    K --> L["verify.py:<br/>independent recomputation"]
```

The module decomposes into three layers: a frozen mathematical **contract** (`contract.py`), the **endpoint machinery** that turns orderings into graded decisions (`validate.py`), and a set of **runners** — the primary `run.py`, four diagnostics (`mechanism.py`, `steelman.py`, `pool_composition.py`, `stratify.py`), an adversarial test suite (`test_protocol.py`), and an independent verifier (`verify.py`). The runners share the contract and validator but never modify them; every threshold in this module is a constant, not a fitted parameter.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph frozen["Frozen layer"]
        C[contract.py<br/>rule + value definitions]
        V[validate.py<br/>grading machinery]
    end
    subgraph runners["Runners (read-only consumers)"]
        R[run.py<br/>Phase 1 + 2]
        M[mechanism.py]
        S[steelman.py]
        P[pool_composition.py]
        ST[stratify.py]
    end
    T[test_protocol.py<br/>16 adversarial tests] --> C
    T --> V
    R --> OUT1["utility_gt_v2_phase12.json"]
    OUT1 --> VF[verify.py<br/>re-derived from definitions]
    V2A[decision_alignment_v1<br/>BUDGETS, nRU, MBRU] --> V
    GOA[global_objective_knowledge_attribution_v1<br/>role arrays] --> R
    C --> R
    C --> M & S & P & ST
    V --> M & S & P & ST
    V --> R
```

Sources: [\_\_init\_\_.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/__init__.py#L1-L8), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L1-L56), [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L1-L19), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L25-L30)

## Phase 1: The Frozen Eligibility Rule

A query is only a question if its transition is measurable at all. The metric space is deliberately `W = I`; a noise-weighted `W` is absent from this module because it is a later sensitivity analysis that must not touch a primary verdict — a `W` chosen while looking at downstream scores would make the whole comparison circular. The eligibility statistic is the **shared latent transition energy** `E_q = <d_A^q, d_B^q>`, computed as the diagonal of the cross-view Gram `M[i, j] = <first_i, second_j>`. Because the two views are measured on disjoint batches, the noise cross term vanishes in expectation, so `E_q` is unbiased for `||d*_q||²` rather than inflated by measurement variance.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L1-L23), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L97-L105), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L46-L48)

The null hypothesis needs no extra computation. Row `q` of the cross-view Gram already contains `<d_A^q, d_B^j>` for every mismatched partner `j` — the same statistic under the hypothesis that the identity pairing carries no signal. The one-sided empirical p-value is `(1 + b) / n` where `b` counts mismatched partners at least as large as the observed diagonal; the smallest attainable p-value is therefore `1/n`, which bounds how small an FDR level can ever be met. Holding `d_A^q` fixed makes the null conditional on that identity's own magnitude instead of pooling across identities of very different scale.

> [!TIP]
> The permutation null is free: it is the off-diagonal of the same Gram matrix you already computed for the energy. There is no resampling loop and no second pass over the data — the identifiability test costs exactly one matrix product.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L108-L122), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L19-L23)

The decision combines two conditions: significance under Benjamini–Hochberg at the primary FDR level of 0.05 **and** a positive energy. The BH q-values are computed with a stable sort and a running minimum so monotonicity holds by construction. The rule is frozen governance, not calibration: `CALIBRATION_ROLE = "G_fit"` prescribes that the rule is developed on the calibration role and applied to `G_select` unchanged, and `GATE_SELECTED_FROM_G_SELECT = False` is a machine-checkable declaration that nothing in this module may read a `G_select` pass count, a model score, or a reproducibility number in order to set the level. Sensitivity is reported, not fitted — at FDR levels 0.01 and 0.10, and via a fixed p-value cutoff taken from `G_fit`'s BH rejection boundary and applied verbatim to `G_select`.

| Frozen constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `METRIC_SPACE` | `"IDENTITY"` | Primary metric space is `W = I`; no noise weighting |
| `ELIGIBILITY_STATISTIC` | `SHARED_LATENT_TRANSITION_ENERGY` | `E_q = <d_A^q, d_B^q>` (cross-view diagonal) |
| `ELIGIBILITY_NULL` | `MISMATCHED_PARTNER_PERMUTATION_ONE_SIDED` | Off-diagonal Gram entries as the null distribution |
| `PRIMARY_FDR` | `0.05` | BH step-up level, prescribed not tuned |
| `SENSITIVITY_FDR` | `(0.01, 0.10)` | Reported only; never replaces the primary verdict |
| `REQUIRE_POSITIVE_ENERGY` | `True` | Significance alone is insufficient |
| `CALIBRATION_ROLE` / `GATE_SELECTED_FROM_G_SELECT` | `"G_fit"` / `False` | Rule frozen on the calibration role; auditable anti-circularity flag |

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L57-L70), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L125-L143), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L146-L160), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L196-L203)

Phase 1 produces a full audit trail per role: energy, p-value, and q-value distributions (including the fraction of p-values sitting at the `1/n` resolution floor), the BH p-cutoff, sensitivity counts, and an `Eligibility` dataclass carrying every array needed to reconstruct the decision. The `run()` driver applies the identical rule to both `G_fit` and `G_select`, writes per-role eligibility masks, and records the pool composition — nominal identities, four-way survivors, eligible identities, and any duplicate identity IDs.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L73-L94), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L47-L84), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L205-L224)

## Phase 2: The Latent Candidate Value Without a Denominator

The candidate value is the reduction in squared endpoint distance that candidate `c` buys for query `q`:

```text
V_qc = 2 ⟨r*_c, d*_q⟩ − ||r*_c||²  =  ||d*_q||² − ||r*_c − d*_q||²
```

Implemented over the cross-view Gram `M = first @ second.T` as `V = M.T + M − diag(M)` — the four-way estimate `<r_c^first, d_q^second> + <r_c^second, d_q^first> − <r_c^first, r_c^second>` — with no division, no clipping, and no per-query rescaling. A structural sanity property falls out for free: the diagonal of `V` equals the transition energy `E_q` (a query "applied to itself" moves the state by the whole transition). Every term is a cross-view product, so the estimator is unbiased for the latent quantity rather than biased by `−features·σ²` the way a same-view form would be.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L25-L33), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L163-L174), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L46-L48)

The formula's most consequential design decision is what it **omits**. The earlier definition divided each utility row by an estimate of `||d*_q||²` — a per-query constant that never changed a within-query ranking, but that flipped the sign of every utility in the row whenever the energy estimate came out non-positive, producing a catastrophic MBRU tail. Dropping the denominator removes that failure mode *by construction* rather than by filtering, and the change is metric-neutral because nRU is invariant to any positive affine transform of the utility row (a negative multiplier reverses the ordering — exactly what the old denominator did). The invariance is exact only while the nRU denominator stays above the contract's absolute floor of `1e-8`; the smallest denominators observed in Phase 2 were `0.038` for the cosine and `4.15` for the latent value, so the floor never bound. Both historical facts are pinned as executable tests (`test_04`, `test_05`), not just narrative.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L34-L44), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L62-L79)

Because `V` estimates a squared-distance reduction, the estimator itself has a physical bound: `V > E_q` would imply a negative squared distance, which is impossible, so `physical_bound_violation` reads out estimator variance rather than identifying candidates that "overshoot the goal." Phase 2 records its frequency alongside the fraction of non-positive energy estimates per side — diagnostic channels for how noisy the quarter-view estimates are on the eligible pool.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/contract.py#L186-L192), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L141-L152)

## The Endpoint in Decision Units: Rank by One View, Grade by the Other

The primary endpoint is explicitly **not** Top-B identity overlap. Overlap counts how many of the same candidates come back and is blind to what they are worth, so two orderings that disagree about which near-equal candidate sits at rank 7 are punished exactly as hard as orderings that disagree about a candidate worth ten times the median. The deployment question is the second one, so the endpoint is graded in decision units: rank every query's candidates by one measurement view, then report how much of the other view's own achievable value the budget prefix delivers, in nRU at budgets `B ∈ {10, 20, 50}` and their mean (MBRU) — the machinery imported from `decision_alignment_v1.contract`.

Sources: [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L1-L19), [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L41-L67)

The comparison is a strict A/B on identical cells. Each estimator contributes two instances; the incumbent cosine consumes side A for its first instance and side B for its second, while the latent value consumes the quarter pair `(Q0, Q1)` for its first instance and `(Q2, Q3)` for its second — the same cells, differently used. Both directions (`first_ranks_second_grades`, `second_ranks_first_grades`) are run and the paired `latent − cosine` difference is reported per direction and averaged, with identity-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals (cluster unit = query identity, fixed seed and replicate count from the decision-alignment contract) and per-budget nRU differences.

| Estimator | First instance (proposes) | Second instance (grades) | Cells consumed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `incumbent_cosine` | Side A | Side B | `base.transitions[0]`, `[1]` |
| `latent_value` | `(Q0, Q1)` | `(Q2, Q3)` | `quarter_responses[0..3]` |
| Directions | `first_ranks_second_grades` | `second_ranks_first_grades` | both, then averaged |

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L29-L30), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L86-L116), [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L82-L99)

Ranking legality is enforced positionally. `legal_orders` produces a self-excluded descending order per query, where exclusion is by candidate-axis position — never by score — so a tie at the top can never smuggle the target intervention back into its own prefix; `grade` then consumes that ordering under the independent view, carrying the per-query nRU denominator alongside the score for auditability. Secondary channels quantify *how* the views disagree rather than only how much: `set_overlap` (against its chance level `B/pool_size`), `boundary_flip` (how often the independent view reverses the rank-B vs rank-B+1 pair that decides the budget — chance 0.5 by construction, requiring no noise model), and `spearman` over whole rows, which is marked auxiliary-only because the budget never uses it.

> [!TIP]
> Self-exclusion by position rather than score is what makes the whole A/B falsifiable. If exclusion were score-based, any estimator that ties with itself at rank 1 would grade its own target at the boundary — the test suite pins this with `test_10`, which places every diagonal at 100.0 and asserts no row's order contains its own index.

Sources: [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L41-L50), [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L101-L126), [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L128-L146), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L133-L141)

## The Goal-Independent Control (Decision D-005)

The control that matters most for a proposed ground truth is not random — it is the **goal-independent prior**: rank every query by the candidate's mean value across queries, one shared ordering for the entire pool. If a value definition is more reproducible mainly because it carries a large query-independent component, a policy that ignores the goal entirely will reproduce most of its advantage; this control therefore upper-bounds the goal-conditioned content of any definition. Two details make it airtight: the column mean excludes each query's own diagonal entry (the largest value in its column by construction — leaving it in would let the self-similarity of 24% of the candidates leak into a policy that is supposed to carry no query information), and the ordering maximizes MBRU for a single shared permutation only as an unweighted mean, so the reported advantage is a *lower bound* on goal-blind performance and thus a conservative cap on goal-conditioned content.

Sources: [validate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/validate.py#L161-L201), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L118-L138)

`test_11` pins the defining property — every row of the prior ordering is the same permutation (minus self-exclusions) — and `test_12` calibrates the grading scale itself: a perfect replicate must score MBRU exactly 1.0 and an unrelated ordering must land near zero. The `goal_conditioned_advantage_MBRU` recorded for each estimator in Phase 2 is the difference between the definition's own ordering and this prior, graded under the independent view.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L143-L160), [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L120-L138)

## The Diagnostic Battery: Four Steelman Scripts

Four scripts interrogate the Phase-2 verdict from independent angles. None of them changes a rule or a threshold; each writes its own schema-tagged JSON record and is runnable as `python -m gene_open_inverse.utility_gt_v2.<script>` from the repository root.

| Script | Question it answers | Method | Output schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mechanism.py` | What does the latent value's ordering actually rank by, given that it is nearly goal-independent? | Grades a policy ranking *purely* by the candidate-only term `−⟨r_c^Q0, r_c^Q1⟩` (the cross-view estimate of `−||r_c||²`); decomposes value variance into shared vs query-independent; correlates the prior with negative response energy; reports the response-energy percentile of selected prefixes at B ∈ {10, 20, 50} | `VCDESIGN_UTILITY_GT_V2_MECHANISM_V2` |
| `steelman.py` | Does the incumbent cosine's high-magnitude prefix actually move the state toward the goal? | Uses `V > 0 ⟺ ||r_c − d_q||² < ||d_q||²` (closer to goal than doing nothing) and grades each definition's prefix under the *other* definition's independent view; reports fraction-closer-than-no-op and value-relative-to-energy against a whole-pool reference | `VCDESIGN_UTILITY_GT_V2_STEELMAN_V1` |
| `pool_composition.py` | Is the latent value's goal-independent reproducibility an artifact of pool composition? | 76% of the 1081 candidates are identities whose own transition the frozen rule judges unmeasurable; reruns the comparison with the candidate vocabulary restricted to eligible identities only — a diagnostic, explicitly not a production filter | `VCDESIGN_UTILITY_GT_V2_POOL_COMPOSITION_V1` |
| `stratify.py` | What does the Phase-1 gate buy, in the same decision units? | Splits the four-way pool into `all_four_way_survivors`, `eligible`, and `rejected_by_the_gate`, and grades both estimators plus the goal-independent prior per stratum with bootstrapped advantage CIs | `VCDESIGN_UTILITY_GT_V2_GATE_STRATIFICATION_V1` |

Sources: [mechanism.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/mechanism.py#L1-L7), [mechanism.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/mechanism.py#L51-L63), [steelman.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/steelman.py#L1-L14), [steelman.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/steelman.py#L64-L85), [pool_composition.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/pool_composition.py#L1-L13), [pool_composition.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/pool_composition.py#L44-L77), [stratify.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/stratify.py#L1-L14), [stratify.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/stratify.py#L48-L71)

`steelman.py` exists because the goal-independent control alone cannot settle whether `−||r_c||²` is nuisance or signal: the cosine divides `||r_c||` out by construction and is therefore structurally favoured by any control that rewards removing the candidate main effect. The direct question — of the candidates each definition puts in the prefix, how many actually reduce the squared endpoint distance, and by how much — is answered with no shared measurement and no shared normalization by grading each definition's prefix under the other's independent view.

Sources: [steelman.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/steelman.py#L1-L14), [steelman.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/steelman.py#L55-L67)

## The Adversarial Test Protocol

`test_protocol.py` contains sixteen pytest targets, and its framing is stated in the first line: each test targets a specific way this phase could report a *valid-looking lie*. The suite is organized around the failure surfaces of the statistics above rather than around code coverage.

| Group | Tests | Lie they prevent |
|---|---|---|
| Estimator correctness | `test_01`–`test_03` | A same-view form silently biased by `−features·σ²`; `V` not equal to energy minus squared endpoint distance; diagonal of `V` not equal to `E_q` |
| Metric invariance | `test_04`, `test_05` | Claiming denominator removal changed the metric (positive-affine invariance holds to `1e-9`); forgetting that the retired normalization inverted rows under negative energy |
| Statistical machinery | `test_06`–`test_09` | Permutation p-values diverging from a brute-force loop; BH q-values diverging from a direct step-up reference; eligibility passing on significance without positive energy (or vice versa); BH cutoff disagreeing with the q-value decision |
| Protocol legality | `test_10`–`test_12` | Self-inclusion in prefixes via positional ties; the prior varying per query (it must be one shared ordering); a broken grading scale (perfect replicate ≠ 1.0, unrelated ≠ ~0) |
| Bootstrap & diagnostics | `test_13`–`test_15` | Cluster bootstrap failing to bracket a known shift of 0.30 or a centered null; boundary-flip rate not at 0.5 under pure-noise grading; `physical_bound_violation` deviating from its exact definition |
| Frozen governance | `test_16` | Any code change that flips `GATE_SELECTED_FROM_G_SELECT`, `CALIBRATION_ROLE`, `PRIMARY_FDR`, or `METRIC_SPACE` away from their frozen values |

Sources: [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L1-L13), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L14-L38), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L80-L131), [test_protocol.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L162-L209)

## Independent Verification: Lesson L3

`verify.py` is the module's external witness, and its docstring names the governing lesson: **a script must not be its own only witness (L3)**. Nothing in it imports the frozen metric module or the Phase-2 code it checks — ranked utility with logarithmic discounting, the random and oracle nRU references, the permutation p-value, and the BH step-up are all rewritten from their definitions, so agreement between the saved record and the verifier means two independent implementations agree.

Sources: [verify.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/verify.py#L1-L20)

The verifier recomputes the cross-view Gram from raw assets and checks the saved energy vector to `1e-9`, resamples 120 identities for permutation-p agreement, rebuilds eligibility from its own BH implementation, recounts candidate and query rows from `four_way_eligible`, spot-checks 400 sampled (query, candidate) pairs of the latent value against explicit dot products, confirms no self inner product enters the estimator, recomputes MBRU from scratch for 48 sampled queries under all four proposing/grading comparisons, and asserts the saved orderings exclude the query and that no identity appears twice on the candidate axis. A subtle correctness point lives in the gating logic: because a numeric check result is a dict, gating only on `is False` booleans would let every numeric check pass regardless of its error — each numeric check therefore carries an explicit tolerance and is gated separately (default `1e-10`, `1e-9` for the explicit-dot-product check), with the process exiting non-zero on any failure.

Sources: [verify.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/verify.py#L85-L150), [verify.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/verify.py#L206-L227)

## Running the Module and Its Artifacts

The primary entry point runs both phases in one pass and writes one record directory (`--asset`, `--config`, `--output`); `output.mkdir(..., exist_ok=False)` makes the long-running stage refuse to overwrite an existing result, mirroring the repository-wide reproduction convention. Every artifact is exported for audit:

| Artifact | Content |
|---|---|
| `utility_gt_v2_phase12.json` | Full Phase 1 + Phase 2 record, schema `VCDESIGN_UTILITY_GT_V2_PHASE12_V1`, with runtime stamp, Python/numpy versions, and config provenance |
| `G_select_{eligible,p_value,q_value,energy,ids}.npy` | Phase-1 decision arrays for the selection role (plus `G_fit_eligible.npy`, `G_fit_p_value.npy` for the calibration role) |
| `per_query__{estimator}__{direction}.npy` | Per-query MBRU for all four A/B comparisons |
| `per_query__order_first_{latent_value,incumbent_cosine}.npy` | The first-instance orderings themselves |
| `phase2_candidate_rows.npy`, `phase2_query_in_candidate.npy` | The exact candidate and query axes, recounted independently by the verifier |

Sources: [run.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/run.py#L226-L244), [REPRODUCE.md](REPRODUCE.md#L3-L4)

The full battery, run from the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.utility_gt_v2.run         --asset ... --config ... --output results/utility_gt_v2
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.utility_gt_v2.mechanism   --asset ... --config ... --result results/utility_gt_v2 --output ...
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.utility_gt_v2.pool_composition --asset ... --config ... --result results/utility_gt_v2 --output ...
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.utility_gt_v2.steelman    --asset ... --config ... --result results/utility_gt_v2 --output ...
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.utility_gt_v2.stratify    --asset ... --config ... --result results/utility_gt_v2 --output ...
python3 -m pytest src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py -q
python3 -m gene_open_inverse.utility_gt_v2.verify      --asset ... --config ... --result results/utility_gt_v2 --output ...
```

Sources: [mechanism.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/mechanism.py#L1-L6), [pool_composition.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/pool_composition.py#L10-L13), [steelman.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/steelman.py#L10-L14), [stratify.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/stratify.py#L1-L8), [verify.py](src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/verify.py#L219-L227)

## Position in the Documentation

This page sits inside the *Experiments and Baselines* section. The ranking vocabulary used throughout (nRU, MBRU, budgets `B ∈ {10, 20, 50}`) is defined in [Ranking Metrics: BU@B, MU@B, PHR@B](8-ranking-metrics-buatb-muatb-phratb); the decision route this validation gate protects is described in [Decision Routes: Retrieval versus Prediction](10-decision-routes-retrieval-versus-prediction); the `four_way_eligible` candidate pool consumed here is specified in [Four-Context Data Contracts](17-four-context-data-contracts). For the integrity machinery that surrounds this module, continue to [Protocol Test Suite](24-protocol-test-suite), [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests), and [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation); the downstream consequences of the Phase-2 verdict are summarized in [Key Benchmark Findings](26-key-benchmark-findings).


# Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation



Leakage is the quiet way a ranking method fakes its own success: the same gene appears on both sides of a train/eval boundary, or a held-out response shapes the very object used to grade it. This page documents how VCDesign closes every one of those channels at four distinct levels: **gene-grouped cross-validation** inside the ridge effect predictor, **identity-based strata** at evaluation time, **controlled response masking** for the open-vocabulary experiments, and the **pre-`G_check` lock** that freezes the method of record. The core story centers on `revision_v1`, a module added during post-review correction, but the identity-discipline runs through the entire pipeline.

Sources: [PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md](PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md#L4-L14), [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L1-L21)

## Why "Identity" Is the Fold Unit, Not the Row

The ridge effect predictor maps static candidate knowledge (STRING + MAP-KG descriptors) to a gene-space effect. Every tunable choice — the basis rank, the ridge penalty grid, the fold seed — is fixed in a frozen contract, and the penalty is selected by five-fold cross-validation on `G_fit` only. The contract states the invariant directly: *a candidate never appears in both the training and validation side of a fold, and no `G_select` quantity is consulted at any point*.

Sources: [predictor.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/predictor.py#L1-L10), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L37-L44)

The subtlety is what "one candidate" means in a pooled multi-context atlas. Rows carry keys of the form `context|identity`, so a gene measured in three training contexts contributes **three rows but one identity**. Splitting rows randomly therefore splits genes — which is precisely the defect a reviewer found in the submitted implementation.

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L26-L30), [predictors.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/predictors.py#L50-L56)

## The Leakage Defect Found During Review

External review identified two compounding leaks in the submitted `four_context_v1.predictors.fit`:

1. **Row-index folds split genes.** The penalty selection cut cross-validation folds over row indices. In a multi-context pool, rows of one gene could sit on both sides of a fold, so the "held-out" fold was not held out at the identity level.
2. **The basis was fitted before the folds were cut.** The frozen fit built the response basis from *every* row before fold assignment, so held-out responses shaped the basis in which their own predictions were reconstructed.

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L3-L12)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph SUBMITTED["Submitted selection — two leak channels"]
        A1["Response basis fitted<br/>on EVERY row"] --> B1["Folds cut over ROW indices"]
        B1 --> C1["Gene X on train side<br/>and held side"]
        C1 --> D1["Held-out responses shaped<br/>the space that grades them"]
    end
    subgraph CORRECTED["Grouped selection — both channels closed"]
        A2["Folds cut over GENE IDENTITIES<br/>every row of one gene stays on one side"] --> B2["Per fold: basis rebuilt<br/>from training rows ONLY"]
        B2 --> C2["Zero identity overlap<br/>asserted per fold"]
        C2 --> D2["Held-out predictions<br/>reconstructed in a held-out-blind basis"]
    end
    SUBMITTED -.corrected by.-> CORRECTED
```

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L5-L12)

## Gene-Grouped Cross-Validation Mechanics

The corrected pipeline lives in `revision_v1.grouped_fit` and consists of three cooperating functions:

| Function | Responsibility | Key invariant |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `row_identities` | Parses `context\|identity` keys down to the bare identity | One gene = one fold unit |
| `grouped_folds` | Assigns identities to blocks, then expands to row index blocks | Sort-then-permute: assignment depends only on the identity set + seed, never row order |
| `cross_validate_grouped` | Scores every penalty on gene-grouped folds | Raises `AssertionError` if any identity intersects train and held |

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L26-L60)

Inside each fold the response basis is **rebuilt from that fold's training rows alone** (`bs.randomized_basis(responses[train])`), and the weighted ridge path is fitted on the fold's projected targets. The selection criterion remains the frozen one — mean held-out gene-space cosine between the reconstructed prediction and the row's consensus response — so the correction changes *where* the penalty is validated, not *what* the penalty optimizes.

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L47-L79)

Critically, the **final deployed predictor is built exactly as the frozen one builds it**: basis on every row, the same weighted ridge path. When the grouped selection lands on the same penalty as the submitted one, the two predictors are mathematically identical, and the difference lives entirely in the selection record. This is what makes the correction auditable rather than a silent method change.

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L83-L119)

> [!TIP]
> The sort-then-permute construction in `grouped_folds` is deliberate anti-fragility: because identities are sorted before permutation, fold membership is a pure function of `(identity set, seed)`. Row-order shuffles upstream of the fitter cannot change which genes are held out — and test 02 in the protocol suite proves it.

## The Selection Switch: Grouped versus Frozen

`four_context_v1.predictors.fit` exposes a `selection` argument so the corrected and submitted paths remain comparable byte-for-byte:

| Aspect | `selection="grouped"` (default, corrected) | `selection="frozen"` (as submitted) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Fold unit | Gene identity (`"gene identity"`) | Row index (`"row index (as submitted)"`) |
| Basis during CV | Refit on each fold's training rows | Fitted on every row before folds are cut |
| Purpose | Leakage-free penalty selection | Exact reproduction of submitted numbers |
| Fitted model | Identical whenever penalties coincide | Identical whenever penalties coincide |
| Record provenance | `"selection": "grouped"` | `"selection": "frozen"` |

Sources: [predictors.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/predictors.py#L115-L141)

The equivalence claim is not asserted in a comment — it is tested: at a fixed penalty, `grouped.basis` and `frozen.basis` must be bitwise identical (`max diff == 0.0`) and both paths must predict identically, otherwise a ranking change could be wrongly attributed to the corrected selection rather than a different fitted model.

Sources: [test_grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L101-L126), [predictors.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/predictors.py#L143-L146)

## Protocol Tests That Name the Failure

`revision_v1.test_grouped_fit` documents four checks, each naming a failure that would otherwise look like a valid selection. Under pytest, any failing check raises and fails the suite; the standalone runner prints the pass/fail table.

| Check | What it asserts | Failure it guards against |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `01_folds_never_split_a_gene` | Grouped fold overlap = 0, folds cover all rows, and submitted-style row folds **do** overlap (`leaky > 0`) | A "fixed" fold that still splits one gene across train/held |
| `02_folds_ignore_row_order` | Fold block per identity is identical before and after a row permutation | Order-dependent fold assignment |
| `03_fold_basis_sees_training_rows_only` | Fold-local basis differs from the whole-row basis (> 1e-8) and the record names `"refit on each fold's training rows"` | A basis fitted on every row, so held responses shape their own grading space |
| `04_selection_switch_changes_only_the_search` | Same basis (`0.0` diff), same path predictions, and record flags distinguish `grouped` from `frozen` | A selection switch that silently changes the fitted predictor, corrupting attribution |

Sources: [test_grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L1-L8), [test_grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L46-L126)

## Identity-Level Boundaries at Evaluation Time

Leakage prevention does not stop at the predictor. The evaluation contract enforces identity discipline in three more places, all keyed on the same parse-and-partition pattern:

**Self-exclusion in ranking.** Every scored row is ranked over the *self-excluded legal pool*: `row_metrics` takes `self_positions` (where the query's own identity sits in the candidate stratum, or `-1`), and both the stable ordering and the reference normalization drop that position before any budget is counted. The graded quantity literally cannot include the query's own measured response.

Sources: [metrics.py](src/gene_open_inverse/evaluation_contract_v1/metrics.py#L1-L11), [metrics.py](src/gene_open_inverse/evaluation_contract_v1/metrics.py#L18-L43)

**Strata by supervision history.** `four_context_v1.overlap` partitions each held context's candidate axis into `SEEN_CANDIDATE` (identity response-supervised in the training contexts — tests *context* transfer) and `UNSEEN_CANDIDATE` (identity no training context measured — tests *candidate mapping* transfer), plus `COMMON4` (measured in all four contexts). The module docstring's rule is explicit: these two generalizations are *never added together*, and **membership is a property of which identities were measured where — it never depends on a score**.

Sources: [overlap.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/overlap.py#L1-L11), [overlap.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/overlap.py#L17-L43)

**Fixed evaluation population per LOCO fold.** In leave-one-context-out runs, `SEEN` is defined against the *full* three-context training set rather than per-design, so a one-context design and the pooled design are graded on identical candidate sets — with each design additionally reporting what fraction of each stratum it actually supervised, a number that would otherwise hide inside a moving population. The fold record carries `"read_anchor_G_check": False` and `"context_feature_given_to_any_model": False` as machine-checkable non-leakage attestations.

Sources: [loco.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/loco.py#L1-L10), [loco.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/loco.py#L96-L101), [loco.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/loco.py#L46-L52)

## Controlled Response Masking: Making "Unseen" Surgical

Natural unseen candidates differ from seen ones in library membership and assay history. The masking phase manufactures the response-unseen condition instead: the candidate identity, its static knowledge, the evaluation pool, the queries, the base ranker, and the graded utility are all held fixed, and the only thing that changes is whether the identity's measured responses entered the effect predictor's fit.

Sources: [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L4-L11)

Fold assignment is **outcome-independent by construction**: each candidate's masking fold is derived from a SHA-256 digest of `"{namespace}:{identity}"`, so nothing about a response, a feature value, or a result can influence it — and the same identity is masked in the same fold everywhere it appears. Removal in `masked_training_pool` is by identity across *every* named context at once, so a masked candidate has no response supervision anywhere in the atlas rather than in one context of it.

Sources: [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L22-L35), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L38-L53)

The leakiest subtle channel is the response basis itself: a deployment in which the candidate was never measured is a deployment in which it never entered the basis either. Reusing the seen arm's basis would leak the masked responses *through the very object the protocol says must be rebuilt* — so the basis and ridge are rebuilt inside the masked pool, and a cross-fit homogeneity gate verifies the five fold predictors' intercept directions, selected penalties, and candidate-specific shrinkage shares before per-candidate columns may be mixed into one score row.

Sources: [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L14-L17), [masking.py](src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L79-L98)

> [!TIP]
> Two masking designs coexist and are deliberately not equivalent: `cross_context` (primary — neither arm has ever seen the held context's responses, so neither can memorize what it is graded on) versus `within_context` (its SEEN arm fits on the very response the utility is built from, making `SEEN − MASKED` a mechanically confounded upper bound reported as a reference, never as the estimate of record).

## The Pre-`G_check` Lock and Split-Semantics Discipline

The three-split contract is stated in the frozen final contract: training may read `G_fit` knowledge plus measured responses; a `G_select` candidate's own measured response is used for grading and **never as an input, in any view**; `G_check` is sealed. The ridge penalty recorded in the lock (`1e4`) was chosen by `G_fit` five-fold identity CV, and none of it is re-selected later.

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/contract.py#L10-L21), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L6-L12), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L11-L16)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph LOCK["Phase F — final_clean_model_v1.lock"]
        L1["Hash every source file<br/>of dependent packages"] --> L2["Record selected checkpoints<br/>with SHA-256"]
        L2 --> L3["Record ridge penalty from<br/>distillation CV record"]
        L3 --> L4["lock_sha256 — refuses<br/>to overwrite existing lock"]
    end
    subgraph EVAL["Phase G — gcheck (only G_check reader)"]
        E1["locked_check_arrays requires<br/>explicit ACKNOWLEDGEMENT"] --> E2["Verify predictor reproduces<br/>locked artifact (≤1e-3)"]
        E2 --> E3["Refuses to overwrite<br/>its own output record"]
    end
    LOCK -->|method frozen before<br/>any G_check access| EVAL
```

Sources: [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L1-L9), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L23-L36), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L1-L11), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L69-L76)

The lock is honest about its limits rather than overstating them: the code digest exists because a commit hash alone does not identify the code (the authoring checkout carries uncommitted work), and the record embeds `G_check_never_used_to_select` flags alongside the note that *earlier phases of the wider programme did read `G_check`* — which is why the split is contractually named a **"locked final evaluation split"** and is forbidden from being called an "untouched blind test."

Sources: [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L26-L35), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L82-L89), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L41-L44)

Finally, `gcheck` closes the loop on the predictor identity: before scoring, `FrozenEffectPredictor.verify_against` re-derives the `G_select` predicted effects and compares them to the locked artifact — a reproduction error above `1e-3` raises, guaranteeing the evaluated predictor *is* the locked one, not a retrained look-alike.

Sources: [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L69-L76), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L88-L96)

## Summary: Four Layers, One Invariant

| Layer | Module | Identity rule enforced |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Penalty selection | `revision_v1.grouped_fit` | Folds cut over gene identities; per-fold basis refit; zero overlap asserted |
| Evaluation | `evaluation_contract_v1.metrics`, `four_context_v1.overlap` | Self-excluded pools; strata from measurement history, never from scores |
| Masking | `open_vocab_generalization_v1.masking` | Fold from SHA-256 of symbol; identity removed everywhere; basis must be rebuilt |
| Locked eval | `final_clean_model_v1.lock` / `gcheck` | Everything hashed before `G_check`; predictor verified against locked artifact |

The unified invariant: **whenever a boundary is cut — CV fold, eval stratum, masking fold, or final split — it is cut on the candidate identity, never on the row, and the object that grades held-out quantities is rebuilt without them.** For the full narrative of what external review found and how each defect was corrected, continue to [Post-Review Corrections](22-post-review-corrections); for the executable guarantees, see [Protocol Test Suite](24-protocol-test-suite) and [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests); for how the strata feed the held-out protocol, see [Held-Out Context Evaluation Protocol](9-held-out-context-evaluation-protocol) and [Ridge Effect Predictor](12-ridge-effect-predictor).


# Post-Review Corrections



This page documents the exact differences between the current release of the code package (version `0.3.1`) and the version submitted alongside the paper. The corrections exist for one reason: external review identified weaknesses in how the ridge penalty for the Candidate Effect Distillation predictor was selected, and how the fusion normalization was specified. The release fixes the selection procedure as its default, documents the normalization semantics explicitly, and adds an option for subset-standardized fusion — while guaranteeing that the submitted numbers remain exactly reproducible through an explicit `selection="frozen"` switch. Corrections are deliberately quarantined in a dedicated module, `gene_open_inverse/revision_v1`, so reviewers can audit the delta between submitted and released behavior without reading the entire pipeline.

Sources: [CODE_PACKAGE_README.md](CODE_PACKAGE_README.md#L86-L94), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L6-L7), [__init__.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/__init__.py#L1-L9)

## Design Principle: Corrections Quarantined From the Submitted Modules

The revision strategy follows a strict boundary: submitted code is never silently edited. The corrected ridge selection lives in `revision_v1.grouped_fit`, and the original `four_context_v1.predictors.fit` gains a single new keyword, `selection`, which defaults to `"grouped"` (the corrected path) and accepts `"frozen"` (the submitted path). The module docstring records the critical empirical claim: **on the published pools the selected penalty is unchanged** — meaning the correction tightens the *validity* of the selection procedure without altering reported results. Whenever both paths land on the same penalty, the fitted predictor is bit-for-bit identical, because the final fit is constructed the same way in both branches; only the cross-validation *record* differs (its fold unit, basis handling, and held-out cosines).

Sources: [predictors.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/predictors.py#L126-L165), [__init__.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/__init__.py#L1-L9), [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L11-L16)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["predictors.fit(features, responses, present,<br/>keys, contexts, selection=...)"] -->|"selection='grouped'<br/>(release default)"| B["revision_v1.grouped_fit.fit_grouped"]
    A -->|"selection='frozen'<br/>(reproduces submission)"| C["_cross_validate:<br/>row-index identity folds,<br/>basis fitted on all rows pre-split"]
    B --> D["grouped_folds:<br/>permute sorted gene identities,<br/>assign whole identity blocks"]
    D --> E["cross_validate_grouped:<br/>basis refit per fold from<br/>training rows only"]
    E --> F["selected penalty"]
    C --> G["selected penalty"]
    F --> H["final fit built by the frozen recipe:<br/>basis on every row + WeightedRidgePath"]
    G --> H
    H --> I["EffectPredictor — identical model<br/>whenever both paths select the same penalty"]
```

## Correction 1: Gene-Grouped Ridge Penalty Selection

### What the submitted selection did wrong

The submitted `four_context_v1.predictors.fit` selected its ridge penalty using `identity_folds` computed **over row indices**. In a multi-context pool this is structurally unsound: a gene owns one row per training context that measured it, so the rows of a single gene can sit on both sides of a fold — the model trains on context A's measurement of gene *g* while holding out context B's measurement of the same gene, and cross-validation overstates generalization. The second flaw compounded the first: the frozen fit built the response basis from **every row before the folds were cut**, so held-out responses shaped the very low-rank basis in which their own predictions were reconstructed. This is basis-level leakage, exactly the family of failures the leakage-prevention protocol is designed to eliminate.

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L1-L9), [predictors.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/predictors.py#L98-L106)

### What the corrected selection does

`fit_grouped` changes **the selection only** — nothing about the final model recipe. Folds are cut over gene identities via `grouped_folds`, which sorts identities before permuting them (so fold assignment depends only on the identity set and the seed, never on row order), then assigns each whole identity to one of `RIDGE_FOLDS` blocks. Inside each fold, the response basis is rebuilt from that fold's training rows alone via `bs.randomized_basis(responses[train])`, and an explicit assertion raises if any identity appears on both sides of a fold. The selection criterion is unchanged from the frozen one: mean held-out cosine between the reconstructed prediction and each row's consensus response, maximized over the penalty grid. The final predictor is then built exactly as the frozen fit builds it — basis fitted on every row, the same `WeightedRidgePath` — so if the grouped search lands on the frozen penalty, the two predictors are identical objects.

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L32-L48), [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L51-L97), [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L100-L119)

### Frozen versus grouped, side by side

| Dimension | `selection="frozen"` (as submitted) | `selection="grouped"` (release default) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Fold unit | Row indices | Gene identity (`context\|identity` → identity) |
| Can one gene straddle train/held? | Yes — structural in multi-context pools | No — asserted impossible at runtime |
| Basis fitted before split | On every row | Refit inside each fold, training rows only |
| Selection criterion | Held-out cosine (unchanged) | Held-out cosine (unchanged) |
| Final fit recipe | Basis on all rows + `WeightedRidgePath` | Identical |
| Cross-validation record | `"selection": "frozen"`, `"fold_unit": "row index (as submitted)"` | `"selection": "grouped"`, `"fold_unit": "gene identity"`, per-fold identity counts |
| Result on published pools | Reproduces submitted numbers exactly | Same selected penalty |

Sources: [grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/grouped_fit.py#L83-L97), [predictors.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/predictors.py#L144-L165)

## Corrections 2 and 3: Fusion Normalization Semantics

### Correction 2 — the normalization is now stated, not implied

`four_context_v1.evaluate.fuse` performs z-score additive fusion at unit weight with no fitted coefficient: each branch (base scores and predicted-effect cosines) is standardized per query row with `row_z`. The correction here is documentation of scope: the function standardizes each branch **over every column of the matrix it is given**, and in the published runs that matrix is the whole scored pool — so fusion normalizes over the full pool, not over the evaluated candidate subset within it. The docstring now states this explicitly, eliminating ambiguity about whether normalization windows move with strata.

Sources: [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/evaluate.py#L82-L96), [CODE_PACKAGE_README.md](CODE_PACKAGE_README.md#L91), [harness.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/harness.py#L157-L160)

### Correction 3 — `standardize_over` for subset-normalized fusion

A new optional parameter, `standardize_over`, accepts a boolean mask or an integer index array and standardizes both branches **over those columns only**, returning exactly `0.0` everywhere else. The rationale is causal hygiene: with subset standardization, a ranking of the selected columns cannot depend on what lies outside them, and columns outside the subset must not be graded (they carry no signal). Validation in `_columns` rejects malformed inputs — a boolean mask must have one entry per column, indices must lie in `[0, width)`, and an empty selection raises. With the default `None`, the function returns exactly what the pre-revision function returned.

Sources: [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/evaluate.py#L63-L79), [evaluate.py](src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/evaluate.py#L95-L104), [CODE_PACKAGE_README.md](CODE_PACKAGE_README.md#L92)

| Call | Standardization window | Columns outside window |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `fuse(base, effect)` | Per query row, all columns given (whole scored pool in published runs) | N/A — all columns scored |
| `fuse(base, effect, beta)` | Same as above, at fusion weight `beta` | N/A |
| `fuse(base, effect, standardize_over=mask)` | Per query row, columns selected by boolean mask or index array only | Returned as `0.0`, must not be graded |

## Smaller Changes: Hardened Protocol Checks and Packaging

The protocol checks in `revision_v1`, `external_baselines_v1`, and `open_vocab_generalization_v1` now **fail their test under pytest** when a check does not hold; previously only their standalone runners reported failure, meaning `python -m pytest -q` could pass while a protocol check was silently violated. The mechanism is visible in `revision_v1.test_grouped_fit`: each `check()` records its result and raises `CheckFailed` (an `AssertionError` subclass) immediately, so pytest fails the test, while the standalone `main()` runner still collects and reports all results from the `RESULTS` list. Two packaging refinements complete the delta: `requirements-cpu.txt` pins `torch==2.4.1` against PyTorch's CPU wheel index so CPU verification does not pull several gigabytes of unused CUDA libraries, and the package version is recorded as `0.3.1`.

Sources: [test_grouped_fit.py](src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L26-L34), [CODE_PACKAGE_README.md](CODE_PACKAGE_README.md#L94), [requirements-cpu.txt](requirements-cpu.txt#L1-L6), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L6-L7)

## Verifying the Corrections in Practice

The revision ships with four protocol tests, each named after the specific failure it would catch. Two tests attack the selection directly: they verify that grouped folds never split a gene *while* demonstrating that the submitted-style row-index folds demonstrably do leak, and that fold assignment ignores row order.
