```mermaid
    T6 --> B6
    T7 --> B7
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L28-L29)

## What Each Module Guards

**The distillation pipeline suite (11 tests)** protects the response-basis and ridge-predictor chain. Its centerpiece is `test_05_out_of_fold_predictions_are_not_in_sample`, which documents the economic reason for the check in its docstring: "An in-sample effect would make beta be chosen for a model that does not exist." The test computes both the honest held-out effect and the in-sample path on the same fixture and asserts the in-sample cosine is strictly *higher* — proving the optimism being guarded against is real, not hypothetical. Companion tests pin the frozen constants (`BASIS_RANK == 256`, `RIDGE_FOLDS == 5`, `ALL_MISSING_SCORE == 0.0`) and verify identity folds partition exactly with no overlap.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L78-L100), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L149-L158), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L55-L68)

**The final clean model suite (12 tests)** guards the locked model pair: no learnable unknown token, all-missing candidates scoring exactly the declared neutral value, a G_check gate that cannot be reached without an explicit acknowledgement constant, and a fusion (`z_score_additive`, `FINAL_BETA == 1.0`) that must equal `row_z(base) + row_z(effect)` to within 1e-12. Notably, `test_06` also asserts the *contract strings*: the fusion must carry `FINAL_FUSION_SELECTION_REASON` containing "Not selected on performance", and the evaluation split must be named "locked final evaluation split" while `EVALUATION_SPLIT_MUST_NOT_BE_CALLED` records what it must never be called. The suite tests its own honesty vocabulary.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/test_protocol.py#L46-L105)

**The four-context suite (63 tests)** is the largest module and is organized into labeled sections: split determinism and refinement (tests 01–02), solver equivalence and stratum metrics (03–21), the frozen response-asset storage contract (22–27), the dual-sgRNA identity gate (28–45), and the V2 identifiability positive control (46–60), closing with the fusion standardization-subset semantics (61–63). Each section guards one pipeline stage against a named defect class — for example `test_30` ensures a cross-gene guide pair is never relabelled as one of its genes, because that "would put TP53's response into BRCA1's distillation target and every downstream number would inherit it."

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L20-L49), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L357-L443), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L376-L390)

**The utility ground-truth suite (16+ tests)** validates the estimator mathematics itself: `test_01` runs a Monte-Carlo comparison showing the cross-view latent-value estimator is unbiased while the naive same-view form carries a systematic `-features × σ²` bias, and `test_04`/`test_05` pin exactly why a retired no-op normalization was removed — it silently inverted entire ranking rows whenever per-query energy came out negative. Statistics implementations (permutation p-values, Benjamini–Hochberg) are each checked against a brute-force reference loop on the same inputs.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L12-L33), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L47-L99)

**The external-baselines suite** is explicitly labeled "Data-free tests": each guards a failure that would otherwise look like a valid external comparison, using a synthetic build directory whose four views are exact count-weighted quarter means — so `test_01` can corrupt one quarter by 0.01 and prove the PHR reconstruction gate fires. `test_03` additionally proves a GEARS split can never contain a masked identity and that the validation bucket is invariant to input ordering.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/test_protocol.py#L1-L3), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/test_protocol.py#L74-L125)

## Firewalls Enforced by Source Inspection

The suite's most distinctive mechanism is three tests that read the *source code* of other modules rather than their behavior. `test_37_no_module_reads_the_raw_anchor_response_cache_directly` globs every `.py` file in its package (excluding itself) and fails if any module references `responses_ab.npy` or `eligible_ids.npy` by path — because the sealed G_check rows live inside that file alongside the readable ones, and a module that opens the file directly has bypassed the loader that drops them. `test_56_the_hindsight_sweep_never_enters_the_verdict` uses `inspect.getsource` on the identifiability pass rule and asserts the tokens `hindsight`, `sweep`, and `lambda_sweep` never appear: if the penalty sweep leaked into the PASS rule, "the control would be selecting on the answer."

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L445-L489), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L801-L831), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/test_protocol.py#L46-L70)

The G_check gate is enforced the same way at the model layer: `test_04` proves `locked_check_arrays` raises `PermissionError` for the empty string, "yes", and even a lowercase copy of the acknowledgement constant, and `test_05` inspects the frozen loader's source to confirm it still refuses G_check for every caller outside the `("G_fit", "G_select")` roles. These tests turn architectural boundaries into CI failures rather than documentation statements.

> [!TIP]
> Source-inspection tests enforce *architecture*, not behavior: deleting the firewall fails the suite even if every computed number stays identical. When porting this pattern, exclude the test module itself from the scan (as `test_37` does) or the suite will detect its own reference to the forbidden path.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/test_protocol.py#L46-L70), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L445-L489)

## The Storage Tolerance Contract: Verification, Not Formality

The response-asset verifier is guarded by a six-test block that treats numerical tolerance as a claim to be tested, not a constant to be trusted. The declared bound is pinned verbatim — `TOLERANCE_ULPS == 2.0` and `TOLERANCE_EXPRESSION == "abs(stored - expected32) <= 2 * eps32 * max(abs(expected32), 1)"` — and `test_27` walks both sides of the boundary to show exactly-on-bound passes and just-over fails. The counterpart mechanism is `corrupt_for_witness`, a helper that injects a known 1e-3 magnitude error so `test_23` can prove the comparator actually rejects a realistic corruption ("This is the test that makes the tolerance a verification rather than a formality," per its comment).

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L291-L354)

The tolerance design itself is stress-tested at its mathematical edges: `test_24` shows the `max(·, 1)` floor survives subtractive cancellation near zero (where the ULP distance exceeds 1000 but nothing is wrong, because a response is a difference of order-one quantities), `test_25` pins ULP-distance monotonicity across signed zero, and `test_26` refuses non-finite values instead of silently comparing them.

| Behavior under test | Test | Pinned property |
|---|---|---|
| 1-ULP float32 storage round-trip | `test_22` | `nextafter` difference passes; ULP distance ≤ 1 |
| Realistic magnitude corruption | `test_23` | 1e-3 injected error fails with exactly 1 violation |
| Cancellation near zero | `test_24` | tiny results with large ULP distance still pass |
| ULP distance symmetry | `test_25` | 0 ULP across ±0.0; ±1 at one step; 2 across subnormal zero |
| Non-finite refusal | `test_26` | NaN fails the comparison outright |
| Bound is the declared expression | `test_27` | string constant matches; boundary exact on both sides |
| Corruption helper on non-contiguous blocks | `test_38` | fancy-indexed slice actually modified |
| Corruption helper refuses no-ops | `test_39` | sub-spacing magnitude raises `RuntimeError` |

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L291-L354), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L490-L513)

## Differential Testing: Fast Paths Checked Against Brute Force

Several fast implementations exist only to make expensive computations affordable, and the suite validates each against a naive reference on identical inputs. `test_16` expands the closed-form V2 interaction cosine term-by-term in a double loop and requires agreement within 1e-9, noting that "if it drifted from the definition every V2 number would be wrong in a way no downstream check could see." `test_17` checks the limit behavior — V2 must degenerate to V1 as the penalty grows — while `test_03` proves the weighted ridge solver reduces to the frozen `RidgePath` at equal weights, with the residual bounded at float64 round-off magnitude.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L188-L227), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L38-L49)

The same pattern repeats across modules: `utility_gt_v2` compares its vectorized permutation p-value against a per-row loop and its Benjamini–Hochberg against a direct step-up reference at four levels; `open_vocab_generalization_v1` validates ridge leverage against the explicit `(XᵀX + λI)⁻¹` form — including the case with more features than rows, asserting the null-space term is retained — and `four_context_v1` verifies the ridge effect predictor recovers a planted linear map at median cosine > 0.9.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L68-L99), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/test_protocol.py#L82-L114), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L189-L228)

## Regression Tests as Institutional Memory

A recurring convention: when a real defect caused a wrong number in the past, the fix ships with a test whose comment records the incident. `test_38` is "the regression test for the round-four witness failure" — the corruption helper silently returned non-contiguous fancy-indexed slices unchanged, so the fixture itself asserts `C_CONTIGUOUS` is false before testing the repair. `test_40` records the first HepG2 audit, where the GSE264667 pair separator `|` lost to the `"_+_"` substring occurring *inside* guide names, shredding the dataset into unparsed labels that looked like a disqualified context. `test_52` and `test_53` both pin the same slip from the first positive-control run, which stacked an already two-view array into four dimensions.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L490-L543), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L718-L799)

The `revision_v1` module is an entire test file of this kind: it guards the post-review correction that re-keyed cross-validation folds from row index to gene identity. `test_folds_never_split_a_gene` is constructed as a differential assertion — it computes the overlap of the *old* row-index folds and requires it to be positive while the grouped folds' overlap is zero, so removing the correction or reintroducing leaky folds both fail. Its docstring names the leak precisely: "A fold that still splits one gene across train and held, so the 'fixed' selection leaks exactly as the submitted one did."

Sources: [test_grouped_fit.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L1-L68), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/utility_gt_v2/test_protocol.py#L47-L67)

## The Dual Runner Pattern

Three modules (`open_vocab_generalization_v1`, `external_baselines_v1`, `revision_v1`) implement a runner dualism: instead of bare `assert`, each check goes through a `check(name, condition, detail)` helper that appends to a module-level `RESULTS` list *and* raises a `CheckFailed(AssertionError)` for pytest. Under pytest the exception fails the test normally; executed standalone (`python3 -m gene_open_inverse.revision_v1.test_grouped_fit`), the `main()` loop catches each failure, records it, prints a PASS/FAIL line per check, and exits with code 1 if any failed. Two details are deliberate: a crash inside a test is recorded as a failure rather than a skip ("a crash is a failure, not a skip"), and every detail string carries numeric context for the failing case.

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/test_protocol.py#L24-L37), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/test_protocol.py#L27-L41), [test_grouped_fit.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L36-L41), [test_grouped_fit.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L117-L144)

> [!TIP]
> The dual pattern costs nothing under pytest but makes each protocol module independently executable — useful when a phase is being iterated on in isolation and the full pytest discovery sweep is unnecessary. If you add a module, follow `revision_v1`'s shape: exception classes, `check()`, numbered check names, and a `main()` returning a process exit code.

Sources: [test_grouped_fit.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py#L110-L144)

## Conventions for Extending the Suite

The suite's conventions are consistent enough to serve as a checklist for anyone adding a phase or a test:

| Convention | Example from the code |
|---|---|
| Sentence-style test names naming the failure mode | `test_05_self_exclusion_never_deletes_the_last_candidate_when_the_query_is_absent` |
| Docstring or comment states *why* the defect would look valid | "An in-sample effect would make beta be chosen for a model that does not exist." |
| Fixed seeds via `np.random.default_rng(seed)` for reproducibility | seeds 7, 11, 23, 101, 103, 107 across the four-context module |
| Data-free synthetic fixtures; no dataset download required | `external_baselines_v1` docstring: "Data-free tests" |
| Prove the trap exists before guarding it | oracle vs. constant ranker; leaky-fold vs. grouped-fold overlap |
| New defect ⇒ new regression test recording the incident | `test_38`, `test_40`, `test_52`–`test_53` |
| Frozen constants asserted literally, including contract strings | `fc.PRIMARY_MODALITIES == ("STRING", "MAPKG")`, split naming strings |

Sources: [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L58-L69), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/candidate_effect_distillation_v1/test_protocol.py#L79-L80), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/test_protocol.py#L91-L105), [test_protocol.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/four_context_v1/test_protocol.py#L273-L289)

## How This Page Fits the Documentation

The Protocol Test Suite is the executable layer beneath the repository's integrity story. The data-side counterpart — hash manifests and the release verifier — is covered in [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests); the specific leakage mechanisms several tests guard (identity-level folds, G_check exclusion, masked identities) are analyzed in [Leakage Prevention and Identity-Level Cross-Validation](21-leakage-prevention-and-identity-level-cross-validation). The correction that `revision_v1/test_grouped_fit.py` protects is described in [Post-Review Corrections](22-post-review-corrections). To see where the suite sits in the end-to-end reproduction order, follow [Reproducing Paper Results](4-reproducing-paper-results), which runs it as step 2 before any training begins.

# Frozen Model Components Library



This page is the reference catalog of every frozen model component in VCDesign-CED: the base scorer architecture, the checkpoint registry, the effect predictor, the fusion rule, and the freeze/lock records that bind them. A component is "frozen" here in a precise, mechanically enforced sense — its inputs, code, and hyperparameters are hashed before any evaluation split is touched, and the locked evaluation refuses to run against anything that does not reproduce those hashes byte-for-byte. If you have followed the pipeline pages through [Score Fusion and Beta Selection](14-score-fusion-and-beta-selection) and [Training Pipeline and Frozen Configuration](16-training-pipeline-and-frozen-configuration), this page is where those contracts terminate in concrete, verifiable artifacts.

## What "Frozen" Means: The Governance Chain

Freezing in this repository is not a convention — it is a chain of records that each assert, with hash evidence, what was and was not read at the time of their creation. The lifecycle runs through three mechanisms: **freeze manifests** (written before response-dependent work), **locks** (written after selection but before the evaluation split opens), and **runtime self-verification** (every consumer re-checks the frozen artifact before using it). The final evaluation split, `G_check`, is deliberately never called a blind test — the contract renames it to "locked final evaluation split" precisely because earlier phases of the wider program did read it, and the assertion that matters is only that this phase's method was selected without it ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L58-L60)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Static feature build<br/>no response read] --> B[freeze.py<br/>FROZEN_BEFORE_RESPONSE_OR_G_SELECT_READ]
    B --> C[Fit + select on G_fit / G_select]
    C --> D[lock.py<br/>LOCKED_BEFORE_G_CHECK_OPEN<br/>checks post-freeze code drift]
    D --> E[Phase F: final lock<br/>VCDESIGN_FINAL_LOCK_V1<br/>hashes 4 code packages]
    E --> F[Phase G: locked evaluation<br/>G_check opened exactly once<br/>acknowledgement required]
    F --> G[Release<br/>DATA_MANIFEST.json<br/>verify_processed_data.py]
    B -.->|code_sha256| D
    E -.->|penalty + artifact sha256| F
```

Two structural guarantees make this chain tamper-evident rather than merely documented. First, the lock scripts refuse to overwrite an existing record — `lock.py` raises `RuntimeError` if the output exists, and `gcheck.py` applies the same rule to its evaluation record, so an adjusted second run cannot silently replace the first ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L41-L44), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L51-L53)). Second, the sub-library lock verifies that the code files hashed at freeze time have not drifted: it re-hashes every name in the freeze's `code_sha256` map and fails on mismatch with the explicit message `"post-freeze code drift"` ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/candidate_knowledge_v1/lock.py#L29-L30)).

Sources: [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L1-L61), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L1-L45), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/candidate_knowledge_v1/lock.py#L1-L42)

## Frozen Component Inventory

The library divides into four tiers: the architecture (code-level), the parameters (checkpoint-level), the transfer map (predictor-level), and the binding records (manifest-level). Each entry lists where the component is defined, what freezes it, and what hash anchors it.

| Component | Definition / artifact | Frozen binding | Hash anchor |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CleanAttributionModel` / `CleanCapabilityEncoder` | [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L25-L53) | Inherited from incumbent; unknown token deleted | `code_sha256` in Phase F lock |
| Base scorer checkpoint | `checkpoints/final_clean_epoch_008.pt`, epoch 8 | Selected per-arm on `G_select` only | `58da13d2…9484` in run config |
| Comparator checkpoints | `m_pair_epoch_010.pt`, `m_set_epoch_010.pt`, epoch 10 | "frozen GOKA final config endpoint" | `DATA_MANIFEST.json` |
| Effect predictor | rank-256 basis, ridge penalty 1e4, consensus target | Hyperparameters kept from distillation, never re-selected | `predicted_effect_G_select.npy` sha256 in lock |
| Fusion rule | `z_score_additive`, β = 1 | No fitted coefficient; selected before `G_check` | Recorded in lock `fusion` block |
| All-missing rule | `ALL_MISSING_CONTRIBUTION = 0.0` | Non-learnable; identical in both arms | Contract constant [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L47-L52) |
| Modality set | `PRIMARY_MODALITIES = ("STRING", "MAPKG")` | TEXT excluded by `GENE_INFORMATION_POLICY_v1` | Contract constant [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L43-L45) |
| Query gate | `QUERY_ELIGIBILITY_V1`, FDR 0.05 | Applied unchanged to whichever role is evaluated | Recorded in lock `query_gate` block |
| Cached comparator scores | `inputs/comparators/*.npy` | Pre-computed under frozen configs | `DATA_MANIFEST.json` |

The checkpoint registry that binds all of these into one portable file is [configs/paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L1-L44), whose `selected_checkpoint_sha256` field pins the reference epoch-8 checkpoint, and whose `data_manifest` field points at the release-wide `DATA_MANIFEST.json` for full-tree verification.

Sources: [configs/paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L1-L44), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L34-L52), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L96-L140), [README.md](README.md#L150-L166)

## The Base Scorer Architecture: One Deletion From the Incumbent

The frozen scorer is not a new design — it is the incumbent `GlobalObjectiveKnowledgeAttributionModel` with exactly one intentional modification: the learnable shared unknown token is deleted. `CleanCapabilityEncoder` calls `del self.unknown_token` in its constructor, then implements masked pooling where the denominator is clamped to at least one present modality, and finally zeroes the embedding of any candidate with no evidence at all. Because scoring is an inner product against this embedding, an all-missing candidate scores exactly the neutral value against every query — zero, which is a cosine's own indifference point, not a value chosen by inspecting `G_select` ([model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L25-L45)). The docstring explains the motivation bluntly: the incumbent's learned token had been measured sitting at the top of every goal-blind ordering, with 100% of its goal-blind Top-10 being information-free genes ([model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L1-L10), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L23-L30)).

Everything else is inherited literally, which is itself a freezing decision: by minimizing the architectural diff against the incumbent, the phase isolates the one variable it intends to test. Two modality-restricted methods (`encode_modality_embeddings`, `encode_modality_candidates`) are replaced with `NotImplementedError` stubs, encoding the constraint that modality banks are undefined without an unknown token ([model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L46-L67)). The companion helper `all_missing_mask` reconstructs the all-missing candidate set from the strict-legal present flags so downstream prefix metrics can report how much of each top-B prefix is information-free.

Sources: [model.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/model.py#L1-L67), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L23-L30)

## The Frozen Effect Predictor: Rebuild, Then Verify

The most distinctive pattern in the library is that the effect predictor is **never loaded** — it is rebuilt deterministically from `G_fit` at evaluation time and then checked against the saved artifact. `FrozenEffectPredictor` reconstructs the consensus response, the rank-256 randomized basis, and the ridge path from the frozen contract constants, then `verify_against` compares its re-prediction against the distillation phase's `predicted_effect_G_select.npy` with a maximum absolute difference threshold of 1e-3; exceeding it aborts with "the rebuilt effect predictor does not reproduce the frozen artifact" ([scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L73-L92), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L59-L65)). Both the selection phase (Phase E) and the locked evaluation (Phase G) run this check before anything else touches the predictor, and Phase G additionally reads its ridge penalty **from the lock record itself**, so a tampered distillation output cannot substitute a different penalty ([gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L87-L97)).

> [!TIP]
> The rebuild-then-verify pattern makes the locked evaluation self-contained: no serialization format, no `weights_only` pitfalls, no version-skew risk on the predictor object — only integer/float contract constants and the raw `.npy` artifact as ground truth. When porting this library, preserve the constants in [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L34-L45) and the distillation record together; one without the other breaks reproduction.

Sources: [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L1-L11), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L73-L109), [select.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/select.py#L56-L65), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L87-L97)

## The Frozen Fusion and Score Assembly

Scoring assembles from three frozen pieces: `base_scores` produces the encoder's inner-product matrix per view, `effect_scores` produces `cos(d_q, r̂_c)` and overwrites all-missing candidate columns with `ALL_MISSING_CONTRIBUTION` (exactly 0.0), and `fuse` combines them as per-row z-scores with `FINAL_BETA = 1.0` ([scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L99-L139)). The fusion's frozen status is unusual among hyperparameters: it was selected for having **no fitted coefficient at all**, meaning no `G_select` or `G_check` quantity could enter it — the contract states explicitly that it was "not selected on performance" and that the alternative family members (rank-average, β = 0.25) are not being re-compared ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L12-L16, L38-L41)). The lock records this as `FINAL_FUSION_SELECTED_BEFORE_G_CHECK: True` with the selection reason inline ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L127-L132)).

A second frozen input-boundary rule lives in `strict_legal_role`: the frozen asset loader admits STRING or STRING+MAPKG+TEXT configurations, so rather than editing anything frozen, the restriction happens downstream — the loader is used exactly as frozen, and `strict_legal_role` drops TEXT before any model or tensor can see it, raising if TEXT survives the restriction ([scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L28-L51)). This is the code-level enforcement of `TEXT_STATUS = "EXCLUDED_FROM_FINAL_PRIMARY_TRACK"` under the `GENE_INFORMATION_POLICY_v1` literature-leakage bar ([contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L43-L45)).

Sources: [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L99-L139), [contract.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/contract.py#L12-L45), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L127-L133)

## The Phase F Lock and the G_check Seal

Phase F (`lock.py`) is the pivot of the library: everything the locked evaluation will use is hashed here, before `G_check` is touched. Its `code_digest` walks four code packages (`final_clean_model_v1`, `candidate_effect_distillation_v1`, `utility_gt_v2`, `action_conditioned_utility_v1`), hashing every source file — because the authoring checkout had uncommitted work, a commit hash alone does not identify the producing code, so the per-file SHA-256 map does ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L1-L39)). The record then enumerates the full frozen surface: method of record, the effect predictor with its artifact path and sha256, the architecture class and parameters from the training manifest, the training recipe, the fusion rule, per-arm selected checkpoints with epoch and sha256, and the evaluation spec including its statistic ("paired identity-cluster bootstrap, 10000 replicates, seed 20260916") and the fixed row policy list from RANDOM to MEASURED_RESPONSE_ORACLE ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L66-L143)). Finally, the record hashes itself: `lock_sha256` is computed over the serialized payload and appended ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L144-L148)).

Access to `G_check` is then sealed behind a single function. `locked_check_arrays` in [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L54-L70) is the only path in the repository to that split, and it refuses to run unless the caller passes the exact string `I_AM_PERFORMING_THE_ONE_LOCKED_FINAL_EVALUATION` — there is no default argument that can reach it accidentally, and it additionally validates the source/goal delta invariant before returning. Phase G's docstring is explicit that this is an *awkwardness* guardrail, not cryptography: the goal is that the evaluation cannot be reached by accident or convenience ([scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L1-L10), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L1-L14)). The evaluation then applies the frozen query gate unchanged, reads the penalty from the lock, and refuses to overwrite its own output record ([gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L51-L97)).

> [!TIP]
> When auditing a downstream fork, check three things in order: does the lock record exist and self-hash correctly, do the `code_sha256` entries match the current tree, and does the `G_check` accessor still demand the acknowledgement string? A fork that relaxes any of the three has silently converted the locked evaluation split into a tunable one.

Sources: [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/lock.py#L1-L162), [scoring.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/scoring.py#L54-L70), [gcheck.py](src/gene_open_inverse/final_clean_model_v1/gcheck.py#L1-L100)

## Sub-Library Freeze Records for Knowledge Features

Two feature-construction libraries carry their own freeze/lock pairs, predating the Phase F lock. `candidate_knowledge_v1/freeze.py` writes a `CANDIDATE_KNOWLEDGE_V1_PROSPECTIVE_FREEZE` record asserting `STATIC_FEATURES_COMPLETE_NO_RESPONSE_READ` and hashing the complete prospective surface: config, design, split, features, feature manifest, and each static asset (STRING, sequence, Reactome GMT zip, NCBI gene info, plus a whole text-encoder tree digest), alongside per-file code hashes and the exact environment (Python/NumPy/SciPy/scikit-learn/torch versions and device) ([freeze.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/candidate_knowledge_v1/freeze.py#L1-L56)). Its lock then demands the freeze status, demands the selection record prove `SELECTED_ON_G_SELECT_ONLY` with `G_check_response_or_relevance_opened` false, and re-verifies all frozen code hashes for post-freeze drift before writing `LOCKED_BEFORE_G_CHECK_OPEN` ([lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/candidate_knowledge_v1/lock.py#L13-L30)). The MAP-KG adjudication library mirrors this with `MAPKG_CANDIDATE_ADJUDICATION_V1_FREEZE`, binding its own feature build, provenance, checkpoint, and ten code files before response fit ([freeze.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/freeze.py#L1-L20)).

The shared governance vocabulary across all freeze records is worth noting for integrators: each asserts the same triple — `response_or_relevance_read_before_freeze: False`, `official_DEV_TEST_response_or_relevance_opened: False`, `benchmark_modified: False` — so feature libraries can be composed without re-negotiating what "frozen" means ([freeze.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/candidate_knowledge_v1/freeze.py#L20-L25), [freeze.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/freeze.py#L8-L11)).

Sources: [freeze.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/candidate_knowledge_v1/freeze.py#L1-L56), [lock.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/candidate_knowledge_v1/lock.py#L1-L42), [freeze.py](src/gene_open_inverse/model/mapkg_candidate_adjudication_v1/freeze.py#L1-L20)

## Release Artifacts and Verification

The repository ships source, configuration, demo, and manuscript; the frozen artifacts themselves live in the companion Hugging Face release under four directories — `inputs/` (frozen response, STRING, MAP-KG, candidate-knowledge, and comparator arrays), `checkpoints/` (the selected epoch-8 reference checkpoint), `records/` (training, selection, evaluation, external-baseline, and verification records), and a top-level `DATA_MANIFEST.json` with byte sizes and SHA-256 digests for every released file ([README.md](README.md#L150-L166)). Verification is a single command against the manifest: `tools/verify_processed_data.py` loads the `VCDESIGN_PROCESSED_DATA_V1` schema manifest, rejects absolute paths, path traversal, duplicates, and symlinks, checks byte size before hashing to fail fast, and exits nonzero on any mismatch ([verify_processed_data.py](tools/verify_processed_data.py#L1-L53)).

```bash
hf download Boom5426/VCDesign --repo-type dataset --local-dir . \
  --include 'inputs/**' 'checkpoints/**' 'records/**' 'DATA_MANIFEST.json'
python tools/verify_processed_data.py --root .
```

| Verification layer | What it proves | Failure mode |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `DATA_MANIFEST.json` + verifier | Every released byte matches the published digest | `SHA-256 mismatch` / `size mismatch` per file |
| `selected_checkpoint_sha256` in run config | The reference checkpoint is the one evaluated | Config/asset divergence |
| Phase F `code_digest` | The evaluation code is the code that produced the lock | Post-freeze code drift |
| `FrozenEffectPredictor.verify_against` | The live predictor equals the saved artifact (≤1e-3) | `not the locked one` abort |
| Phase F/G output-existence checks | No second, adjusted run replaces the first | `refuses to overwrite` |

Together these layers close the loop the other pages describe analytically — [Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests) covers the manifest tooling, [Protocol Test Suite](24-protocol-test-suite) covers the behavioral assertions, and this page supplies the artifacts both operate on.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L150-L188), [configs/paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L1-L44), [tools/verify_processed_data.py](tools/verify_processed_data.py#L1-L53)

## Consuming the Library

For a downstream consumer, the minimal correct usage sequence is: verify the release tree, load [configs/paper_run_v1.json](configs/paper_run_v1.json#L1-L44) to resolve every asset path, construct the model over `strict_legal_dims` and load the pinned checkpoint state dict strictly, rebuild the predictor from the lock's `ridge_penalty`, and score with `base_scores` + `FrozenEffectPredictor.effect` + `fuse`. Retraining from scratch is also supported — the training entry point refuses to overwrite an existing output directory, and the frozen reference checkpoint `checkpoints/final_clean_epoch_008.pt` remains the comparison target ([README.md](README.md#L167-L188)).

This page closes the reproduction chain: components ([Final Clean Base Scorer](15-final-clean-base-scorer)), training and selection ([Training Pipeline and Frozen Configuration](16-training-pipeline-and-frozen-configuration)), integrity tooling ([Artifact Verification and SHA-256 Manifests](23-artifact-verification-and-sha-256-manifests)), and the benchmark outcomes these frozen artifacts produce ([Key Benchmark Findings](26-key-benchmark-findings)).


# Key Benchmark Findings



This page is the capstone of the catalog: it collects the benchmark results the VCDesign-CED repository was built to produce and explains, in plain language, what each number means and how much trust it deserves. Everything here is read directly from the frozen contracts, the reporting code, and the manuscript summary in the README — no numbers are invented. If you have followed the earlier pages, this is where the whole evaluation story pays off.

![VCDesign framework overview](https://github.com/Boom5426/VCDesign-CED/blob/main/assets/vcdesign_overview.png?raw=true)

## How to Read the Numbers: the Metric Glossary

Before looking at any result, you need the vocabulary. Every benchmark in this project grades a ranked list of candidate interventions for a query, over a self-excluded legal pool, and scores the top-$B$ prefix (with budgets frozen at 10, 20 and 50). The primary metric is **BU@20** — the normalized realized utility of the top-20 picks — and every companion metric answers a different practical question about that same list.

| Metric | Plain-language meaning | Frozen definition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BU@B** | How much usable value the top-$B$ list captures, as a fraction of the best possible list | Frozen `nRU@B` (normalized ranked utility) |
| **MU@B** | The average utility of the $B$ candidates actually picked | Mean of the picked utilities |
| **HvHit@B** | How many of the $B$ picks are "high-value" (top-5% of the legal pool) | Count of picks ≥ the frozen quantile threshold |
| **PHR@B** | Fraction of picks with a *realized positive effect* under an independent readout | Mean of realized $J > 0$ over the picks; four-way sub-pool only |
| **QWR@20** | On what fraction of queries a method beats the comparator | `paper` form = wins over all rows vs BASE; `gate` form = wins over decided rows |

Two details matter for interpreting every finding below. First, HvHit@20 is where the README's "1.11 more top-5% candidates" comes from — it is a *count*, not a rate. Second, the PHR metric is only computed on a specially constructed four-way sub-pool (candidates in the C-016 stratum whose queries meet a minimum-cell rule in all four batch quarters), and is reported as `PHR_UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_PACK_LIMITATION` where that pool cannot be built — so a missing PHR value is a protocol statement, not an error.

Sources: [metrics.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/evaluation_contract_v1/metrics.py#L1-L8), [metrics.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/evaluation_contract_v1/metrics.py#L37-L49), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L58-L70), [metrics.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/evaluation_contract_v1/metrics.py#L64-L69)

## Where the Evidence Comes From: Two Frozen Regimes

All headline numbers are reported under one of exactly two regimes, and every method's score is only meaningful inside the regime where it is legal. **SEEN** evaluates candidates whose measured responses exist in the training contexts (leave-one-context-out). **MASKED** is the decisive condition: each candidate identity is assigned to one of five SHA-256 folds derived purely from its gene symbol, and every row of that identity is removed from *all* training contexts at once — the response basis and ridge predictor are then rebuilt inside the reduced pool, so the graded quantity can never have been memorized.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph SEEN["SEEN regime — responses of the candidate exist elsewhere"]
        B1["BASE scorer"] --> R1["Profiled signature retrieval<br/>pooled BU@20 = 0.675"]
        B1 --> R2["VCDesign-CED<br/>pooled BU@20 = 0.508"]
    end
    subgraph MASKED["MASKED regime — candidate responses hidden everywhere"]
        B2["BASE scorer (K562-trained)"] --> R3["VCDesign-CED fused score<br/>pooled paired BU@20 gain +0.0492 over BASE"]
        E["CED effect branch<br/>(basis + ridge rebuilt<br/>inside masked pool)"] --> R3
    end
    SEEN --- MASKED
```

> [!TIP]
> The masking fold comes from a hash of the gene symbol alone (`fold_assignment`), so a candidate is masked in the same fold in every context and nothing about any response, feature or outcome can influence which candidates were hidden — this is what makes the +0.0492 gain a *controlled* result rather than an observational one.

Sources: [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L10-L14), [masking.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L1-L25), [masking.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L40-L50), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L96-L103)

## Finding 1: Distillation Beats Its Own Base When Responses Are Hidden

The paper's central positive result is a paired contrast, not an absolute score. In the three held-out cellular contexts (RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat), adding the CED effect branch on top of the same base scorer — under the MASKED regime, where the candidate's measured responses were removed from the atlas — yields a **pooled paired BU@20 gain of +0.0492**, and among the 20 selections delivers **1.11 more top-5% candidates on average** (the HvHit@20 companion). Because the contrast is paired per query and pooled over the three held-out contexts, this says: *the same scorer, on the same queries and pools, ranks better when the effect branch is added.*

Three protocol facts tell you how much to trust that gain. The comparison excludes self (a query never ranks itself), the candidate-level pairing is exact, and the primary exposure quantity is deliberately *size-controlled*: removing a candidate's rows also shrinks the atlas, so the protocol separates "this candidate was never measured" from "the atlas got a fifth smaller" by using the *next* fold's predictor as the size-control arm — no extra fit, fixed by hash, never re-chosen after seeing numbers.

| Quantity | Formula | What it isolates |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `exposure_value` | SEEN − MASKED | Upper bound of response exposure, *including* atlas shrinkage |
| `exposure_value_size_controlled` | SIZE_CONTROL − MASKED | The candidate-specific effect alone (**primary**) |
| `atlas_shrinkage_cost` | SEEN − SIZE_CONTROL | What losing one fifth of the atlas costs |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L79-L92), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L125-L140), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L58-L64)

## Finding 2: Measured Responses Still Beat Distillation — the Retrieval Ceiling

The honest counterpart to Finding 1: when candidate responses *have* been measured in other contexts, directly retrieving the measured profile scores higher than predicting it. In the SEEN regime, **profiled signature retrieval reaches pooled BU@20 0.675 versus VCDesign-CED's 0.508**. This is not a contradiction of Finding 1 — it is the boundary of the method. Distillation buys performance exactly where measurements are missing; where measurements exist, using them directly is better. This pairing is precisely why the project exposes two decision routes, and you should read them side by side on the [Decision Routes: Retrieval versus Prediction](10-decision-routes-retrieval-versus-prediction) page.

The paper-table generator encodes this reading directly: `PROFILED_SIGNATURE_RETRIEVAL` is a *companion* row (not a main-table competitor), and its legality annotation marks it as reading the candidate's measured training-context responses — information a deployment candidate would not have.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L79-L92), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L29), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L42-L52), [tables.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/tables.py#L15-L18)

## Finding 3: The Baseline Roster — Who Was Compared, Under Which Rules

Every method in the benchmark is registered in a frozen contract with a taxonomy family (A–F) and a *legality* statement — what information it was allowed to read. This is what makes the comparison fair to audit: a method's score can only be interpreted inside its legal regime. Note that the two strongest "published" baselines (CellNavi variants) are **SEEN-only**: they require the candidate's measured cells in a training context, so they simply cannot run in the MASKED regime.

| Arm | Family | Legality | Regime |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `RANDOM` | A. random | no information | both |
| `GOAL_BLIND_PRIOR` | B. goal-blind prior | strict legal, goal blind | both |
| `BASE` | C. direct inverse | strict legal | both |
| `CELLNAVI` (design-compatible) | C. direct inverse, published | needs candidate's measured training cells | **SEEN only** |
| `CELLNAVI_NATIVE` | C. direct inverse, published | native class scale (Deviation 5) | **SEEN only** |
| `GEARS` (forward-enumerate) | D. forward-enumerate | strict legal in both regimes | both (companion) |
| `INTERNAL_FTM` | D. forward-then-match, internal | strict legal | both |
| `VCDesign` (BASE + RIDGE_UNIT) | E. VCDesign | strict legal | both |
| `MEASURED_RESPONSE_ORACLE` | F. oracle | reads the held-context response — **not deployable** | analysis only |

One quiet but important rule for beginners: any candidate a method cannot represent receives a zero predicted effect, which the frozen effect-cosine scores as 0. So a method that simply cannot express many candidates is *penalized* by the protocol rather than silently excused.

Sources: [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L18-L29), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L30-L52), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L53-L56)

## Finding 4: GEARS Could Not Be Reproduced — and Its Fits Collapsed

The benchmark's most sobering external result is recorded as a frozen verdict string: `GEARS_OFFICIAL_REPRODUCTION_FAILED`. Following the official tutorial notebook, the split composition came out 9/43/19/36 against the published 9/52/18/37, and the headline top-20 DE MSE was 0.2456 versus the published 0.2540 — outside the declared tolerance. On the VCDesign task itself, the diagnosis is harsher: every GEARS fit predicts a single perturbation-independent shift (recorded in `GEARS_COLLAPSE_DIAGNOSTIC.json`), meaning its ranking reduces to the tie rule — a degenerate ordering, not a competitor.

The protocol therefore handles GEARS with explicit honesty rather than deletion: it is labelled a **companion row outside the main table** (Deviation 4), paired with an information-matched internal companion (`RIDGE_UNIT_K562_ATLAS` — the same K562-only atlas GEARS sees, scored by the VCDesign ridge recipe), and every companion table prints the verdict and placement in its header comment. For comparison depth beyond the headline budget, companion tables also report BU@10 and BU@50 for all arms.

| Reproduction check | Reproduced | Published | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Split composition (seen0/seen1/seen2/unseen) | 9/43/19/36 | 9/52/18/37 | mismatch |
| Top-20 DE MSE | 0.2456 | 0.2540 | outside tolerance 0.05 |
| Fit behavior on task | one context-independent shift per fit | — | `DEGENERATE` |

Sources: [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L72-L93), [tables.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/tables.py#L53-L57), [tables.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/tables.py#L48-L52)

## Finding 5: CellNavi Was Run Twice — at Two Different Class Scales

CellNavi is the strongest published inverse baseline, and the benchmark runs it in two deliberately distinct configurations. The **design-compatible** variant uses every identity the held context's training fit may use as classes; the **native-scale** variant restricts classes to the held context's C-016 SEEN stratum — the actual candidate library the task ranks (registered as "Deviation 5"). Both are SEEN-only by legality, both use the official recipe (pinned commit, pre-trained checkpoint MD5s, frozen training hyperparameters), and both are scored identically to every other arm: the mean over query-view cells of the log-softmax at each candidate's class.

The adapter's own fidelity was anchored first: the official reproduction target (accuracy 0.510, weighted F1 0.498, 3158 cells, 70 classes) had to be hit within a 0.005 tolerance before its scores could enter the benchmark — the same reproduce-before-compare discipline applied to GEARS, just with a passing outcome.

Sources: [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L96-L113), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L24-L25)

## Finding 6: The Masking Protocol Was Audited Before the Numbers Existed

Several benchmark findings are about the *protocol itself*, fixed in a contract written before any masked result existed. The pool-size plan is a good example: at the pre-registered five folds, masked pools came out K562 286, RPE1 254, Jurkat 290 and HepG2 152 candidates. Rather than quietly re-picking the fold count to chase the 300 target (which would have made the fold itself a post-hoc choice), the protocol fixed a primary-inclusion floor of 200 — so **HepG2 folds are diagnostic-only** in the per-fold contrast while still entering the pooled full-pool contrast (pool of 764).

Cross-fitting five fold predictors into one score row also requires proof they are mixable. The frozen gate demands minimum pairwise intercept cosine ≥ 0.99, an identical selected ridge penalty, and a candidate-specific-share ratio ≤ 1.05 — and the code documents why the direction test alone can never fail (five pools sharing four fifths of their rows always agree on the penalty-free target mean). Finally, the protocol discovered and *recorded* an inherited defect in the frozen cluster bootstrap (it resamples query *views*, not query *identities*, making published intervals narrower than the stated cluster unit); rather than silently patching it — which would break comparability with earlier runs — the correct query-identity interval is computed and reported **beside** every headline contrast.

> [!TIP]
> This "record the defect, report the corrected interval beside it" pattern appears twice (the bootstrap and the row-index ridge fold cut). When you reproduce results, check both intervals: a conclusion that survives only under the narrower frozen interval is flagged, not hidden.

The whole controlled-masking design exists because the earlier *natural* experiment could not settle the question: on the K562 fold, unseen candidates showed delta MBRU **−0.0103** (6,255 candidates) while seen candidates showed **+0.0095** (1,570) — but those sets differed by screen library, so candidate novelty was entangled with context novelty, leaving two incompatible explanations (poor knowledge support vs. no possible extrapolation). The controlled masking exists to separate them.

Sources: [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L15-L20), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L45-L57), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L110-L124), [masking.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/masking.py#L134-L160)

## Finding 7: The Frozen Design Choice Behind VCDesign's Score

The `VCDesign` arm is not tuned during the benchmark — the contract states it is frozen as `RIDGE_UNIT` (mission C-018, arm A1: unit-target cosine), read from C-018's saved effects and never refitted. C-018 asked whether the pipeline loses candidate-specific directional predictability by unit-normalizing the predicted effect, comparing four scoring arms (A0–A3) under frozen outcome rules; the README confirms the unit-direction held-context configuration was selected on the same evaluation pools and fixed **before** external baselines were run. C-018's own decision statistic also previews the project's statistical style: 1,333 pooled query rows collapse to 976 gene identities, and the 95% interval uses the *gene* as the cluster, carrying both batch-disjoint views and every context together.

| Element | Frozen choice | Consequence for the benchmark |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Scoring core | `RIDGE_UNIT` (C-018 A1) | No baseline-era tuning; single frozen comparator target |
| Decision statistic | pooled paired MBRU median, gene-level clusters | Intervals reflect 976 genes, not 1,333 rows |
| Selection timing | fixed before baselines ran | No winner's-curse in the baseline comparison |

Sources: [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/external_baselines_v1/contract.py#L1-L6), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/decision_consistent_effect_v1/contract.py#L17-L30), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/decision_consistent_effect_v1/contract.py#L54-L63), [README.md](/README.md#L79-L92)

## Scope and Caveats Every Reader Should Keep

The README states the boundary plainly: these are **retrospective results for transcriptomic directional prioritization**, not prospective evidence of improved biological endpoints. Two further caveats keep Finding 1 honest. The response masking applies to the *CED atlas only* — the fixed base scorer was itself trained on 68% of the masked candidate identities, so the manuscript additionally reports a base-scorer-unseen subset and a locked K562 identity test. And K562 is excluded from the primary masked contexts for a structural reason: the base ranker was trained on K562 responses, so a K562-masked candidate could retain exposure through the base branch even after losing it in the effect branch.

| Caveat | What it limits | Mitigation in the records |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Retrospective design | No prospective biological claim | Stated in the manuscript scope |
| Base saw 68% of masked identities | Masked gain partly via base exposure | Base-scorer-unseen subset + locked K562 test |
| K562 not in primary masked set | No fully-exposure-free K562 masked claim | K562 designated a secondary context |
| Frozen bootstrap interval | Published intervals narrower than gene-level | Corrected interval reported beside each contrast |

Every number on this page is regenerable: the frozen inputs, checkpoints, run records and SHA-256 manifest live in the companion dataset, and the reproduction sequence from verification through table generation is documented step by step in [Reproducing Paper Results](4-reproducing-paper-results).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L79-L92), [contract.py](/src/gene_open_inverse/open_vocab_generalization_v1/contract.py#L96-L102), [REPRODUCE.md](/REPRODUCE.md#L35-L40)
